items.title: feat(cron): extend mount-namespace isolation to cron/scheduler.py spawn (t_102333c4)
items.body:
## What

Closes the cron-spawn path exposure verified by t_efef6176 (verification card). Cron-spawned agents in `cron/scheduler.py` previously ran with full filesystem privileges against the production hermes-agent tree — a worker could `git switch -c cron-evil`, `echo x >> app.py`, `git reset --hard` from inside a cron job. This card wraps `cron/scheduler.py:3281`'s `subprocess.Popen(dispatch.argv, ...)` in the same `unshare -Urm` launcher the dispatcher uses (t_ff7d30cc), so the production tree is `EROFS` at the syscall level for cron-spawned workers too.

## How

`hermes_cli/worker_isolate.py`:
- New public helper `build_isolated_cron_worker_argv(command, *, agent_home)` mirrors `build_isolated_worker_argv` for the cron (no-worktree) case.
- `_parse_launcher_argv` and `_enter_isolation` accept an optional `--cron` flag / `cron=True` parameter; the launcher uses the same bind dance.
- New `_agent_home_branch_ref_dir(agent_home)` resolves the branch ref carve-out from the agent home's own `.git/HEAD` (vs the worktree's HEAD on the dispatch path). For a top-level branch like `canonical-deploy-t_7161d9a9` it returns the branch ref **FILE** (file-level `mount --bind` is supported by the kernel and does NOT widen to the whole `refs/heads` directory — sibling refs stay ro, cross-branch moves like `update-ref refs/heads/<other-branch>` are denied). For nested branches it returns the parent directory (matches dispatch helper).

`cron/scheduler.py`:
- New `_cron_isolation_argv(dispatch_argv, repo_root)` helper that wraps the argv when the `kanban.worker_isolation` policy is effective. Applied just before `subprocess.Popen` at `cron/scheduler.py:3281`. Degrades cleanly (no wrap) on kill switch / degraded / missing-helper paths so a flaky roll-out never crashes the cron loop.
- Reuses the same `kanban.worker_isolation` config and `HERMES_WORKER_ISOLATION` kill switch as the dispatch path. Deliberately does NOT introduce a separate `cron.worker_isolation` config: a single gate keeps the failure mode homogeneous across both spawn paths.

Tests (13 new + 1 live acceptance):
- `test_build_isolated_cron_worker_argv_*` (shape, extra_rw, empty/missing rejections).
- `test_launcher_argv_parser_accepts_cron_flag` / `rejects_cron_with_worktree` (mutual exclusion with `--worktree`).
- `test_agent_home_branch_ref_dir_*` (top-level returns FILE, nested returns DIR, detached/missing/missing-ref-file all return None).
- `test_cron_acceptance_harness_isolates_synthetic_repo` (live `unshare -Urm` probe against a synthetic repo: every forbidden op — `git switch -c cron-evil`, `echo x >> app.py`, `git reset --hard`, `git checkout HEAD -- .`, `git update-ref refs/heads/<other-branch>` — returned EROFS / Read-only file system).
- `test_cron_isolation_argv_returns_unwrapped_when_kill_switch*` and `_handles_empty_argv` (policy gate).

Docs (`docs/wiki/services/canonical-deploy-branch.md`, doc-in-commit):
- Worker isolation section's "Cron spawn path" caveat now describes the cron wrap behaviour end-to-end.
- See Also lineage picks up t_102333c4 (and t_21e9f9d6 lxd correction inherited from the branch base).

## Test plan (live, run after merge)

A live cron-spawned probe against the production tree is owned by t_bc6bbb7c's verification gate (the merge-into-canonical-deploy card). The synthetic-repo acceptance harness above runs against `unshare -Urm` directly and proves the design blocks the same forbidden ops under the same syscall-level denial — same evidence pattern t_ff7d30cc shipped with t_efef6176 verifying.

Once t_bc6bbb7c merges and the dispatcher restarts, the soak window from t_efef6176 can complete with both spawn paths covered.

## Verification (current state)

- 36 unit tests pass on the merged dispatch + cron isolate code (23 inherited dispatch tests still green after the cherry-pick onto canonical-deploy; 13 new cron tests).
- 4 live acceptance tests pass: 1 dispatch-side, 1 cron-side, 2 e2e wiring.
- Synthetic-repo cron probe ran every forbidden op against a synthetic agent home and got EROFS / Read-only file system for each — see commit message for the verbatim transcript.

/cc @ultron_wallace_bot (verification owner) — please kick the live cron probe against the production tree once this lands via t_bc6bbb7c.

items.title: fs.rm, shell rm, install: treat a missing path on a read-only mount as missing
items.body:
### Problem - `fs.rm` with `force` throws `EROFS: read-only file system, rm '

'` for a missing path on a read-only mount, such as a Docker `:ro` volume. Shell `rm -f` prints `rm:

: Read-only file system`. Node and GNU rm succeed. - `bun install` fails too: `hoist is disabled, but the existing './node_modules/.bun/node_modules' could not be removed`, and `failed to delete empty lockfile`. - Linux and FreeBSD check that the mount is writable before they look up the name, so `unlink(2)` answers EROFS. `NodeFS::rm` (`src/runtime/node/node_fs.rs:7758`), the shell, `Dir::delete_tree` and `save_lockfile` accept only ENOENT. ### Fix - Add `bun_sys::removal_target_is_missing(dir, path)`, one no-follow `lstatat`, asked only after the first removal of an operand fails with EROFS. - A missing path takes the existing ENOENT code: `force` returns, no `force` reports `ENOENT ... lstat` like Node. An existing entry keeps EROFS. - Verified: new tests in `fs.test.ts`, shell `rm.test.ts`, `isolated-install.test.ts`, `bun-lock.test.ts` (all fail on bun 1.4.3), and Node's `test-fs-rm.js`. - Self-reviewed: 26 concerns raised, 21 addressed, 2 in part. Rejected (Notes): the errno inside the helper, a walker-merge tracker. ### Background - GNU rm has the same rule ([`excise`](https://github.com/coreutils/coreutils/blob/v9.7/src/remove.c#L405-L416)): after EROFS, `fstatat` decides. - Considered an `lstat` before each removal, like Node: one more syscall per `rm`. Considered the check inside `unlink`: Node's `unlinkSync` reports EROFS too. ### Downsides - After EROFS on an existing path: one more `lstat`. Other paths: +0 syscalls in 8 fixed loops. - Release `.text` grows by 1,024 bytes. - Windows is unchanged. macOS and FreeBSD: not run.

Notes No issue in this repository reports the symptom. A parity check of `rm` against Node v26.3.0 on a read-only mount found it. **Repro** (Linux x64, kernel 6.1.155, no docker) ```sh mkdir -p ro && touch ro/file.txt unshare -Urm /bin/sh -c 'mount -o bind ro ro && mount -o remount,bind,ro ro && exec "$0" -e " const fs = require(\"node:fs\"); for (const o of [{ force: true }, { force: true, recursive: true }, {}]) try { fs.rmSync(\"ro/missing\", o); console.log(\"ok\"); } catch (e) { console.log(e.code, e.syscall); } "' bun ``` | | `rmSync(missing, {force})`, recursive or not | `rmSync(missing)` | `rmSync(file, {force})` | |---|---|---|---| | Node v26.3.0 | ok | `ENOENT lstat` | throws | | Bun 1.1.45 | ok | `EROFS unlink` | ok, file left in place | | Bun 1.2.0 to 1.4.3, main | `EROFS rm` | `EROFS rm` | `EROFS rm` | | This PR | ok | `ENOENT lstat` | `EROFS rm` | - For `node:fs` this is a regression since 1.2.0. #16422 narrowed `force` from "ignore every error" to "ignore ENOENT from the removal". The 1.1.x answer was not correct either: it reports success for a file that EROFS left in place. The shell and `Dir::delete_tree` were never correct. - `fs.unlinkSync(missing)` is `EROFS unlink` in every row, Node included. So the check cannot live in the `unlink` wrappers. - Shell: `rm -f ro/missing` exits 1 on main, 0 with this PR and with GNU rm 9.7. `rm ro/missing` prints `No such file or directory` with this PR, like GNU rm. `rm -rf ro/missing tree` now removes `tree`: on main the false error stops the other operands. - The rows for entries that exist differ from Node before and after this PR. Node reports `EROFS unlink` or `EROFS rmdir` from the async forms and an error without a `code` from `rmSync`. Bun reports `EROFS rm`. For `ro/file.txt/` Node reports `ENOTDIR lstat`, Bun `EROFS rm`. **Why the kernel answers EROFS** - Linux: `do_unlinkat` calls `mnt_want_write` before it looks up the last component ([fs/namei.c](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.1/fs/namei.c#L4299-L4304)). `do_rmdir` does the same. - FreeBSD: `vfs_cache_lookup` returns EROFS for a delete on a read-only mount before the lookup ([vfs_cache.c](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/14.3/sys/kern/vfs_cache.c#L3089-L3091)). Read in the source, not run. - macOS: the generic lookup checks the name first, but nullfs (`null_lookup`) returns EROFS before the lookup. Read in the source, not run. So the helper runs on every POSIX target. - Windows: a removal opens the entry first, and that open fails with ENOENT for a missing entry. The helper returns `false` there. **Where the check is, and why there** - `NodeFS::rm`, non-recursive: after `unlink`. - `zig_delete_tree`: at the first `unlinkat` of the operand, before anything is removed. A check after the walk can report success for a tree that a real EROFS left in place. The per-entry `unlinkat` calls are not changed. - Shell `remove_entry_file`: a new arm beside the ENOENT arm, with the same `force` rule. - `Dir::delete_tree`: the first `unlinkat` of the operand. 73 call sites use it. Most discard the result. `isolated_install.rs` reads it for the `hoist = false` fallback directory. - `save_lockfile`: the `unlinkat` of `bun.lock` after a migration left no `bun.lock` on disk. **Not changed** - `fs.unlinkSync`, `fs.rmdirSync`, `Bun.file().delete()` and the `bun_sys` wrappers: Node reports EROFS there too. - The other shell arms (`rmdirat`, the directory open): for an operand the shell reaches them only after `unlinkat` answered EISDIR or EPERM. For a child the name comes from a directory listing. - The per-entry arms of both tree walkers: the names come from a directory listing. - Removers in `bun install` that look the entry up first (`remove_planted_link`, the stale store link). - `bun pm cache prune` on a read-only cache fails for a different reason: `rmdir` of a directory that is not empty answers EROFS, not ENOTEMPTY. The directory exists, so this helper does not apply. **Related open PRs** - #38550 has the same recheck for non-recursive `fs.rm` only, without the EROFS condition. This PR replaces that part. Its Windows EPERM retry is a different fix and stays needed. - #45377 and #44588 edit the same non-recursive arm. After #45377 the arm runs two lookups on an EROFS failure. The `directory` rows of the new fs test pin `ERR_FS_EISDIR` for whoever merges the two. - #41480 and #35749 change the error type of `zig_delete_tree`. The new arm there matches `crate::Error::ReadOnlyFileSystem` and needs the new spelling after either one. - #31337, #36176 and #41842 make the shell walk relative to a directory fd. The new shell arm must get the same `(dir, path)` pair as the `unlinkat` it follows. The `.cwd("ro")` and `rm -rf ro` cells of the new shell test fail if it does not. - #39226 changes `verbose_deleted` to return `()`. The new shell arm then needs `return Ok(())`, like the ENOENT arm. - #44587 (ENOTDIR for a missing path under gVisor) is the same class with another errno. This PR does not change it. #44588 can call the new helper. **Measurements** (Linux x64, kernel 6.1.155, release builds of main 0ffddcdc6d with and without this diff, built in the same directory) - Common path: +0 syscalls. The counts of `unlink`, `unlinkat`, `rmdir`, `stat`, `lstat`, `newfstatat` and `statx` are the same in 8 fixed loops on a writable directory. `strace` cannot be installed on the build machine, so a small ptrace counter did the count. - 1000 x `rmSync(missing, {force})`: unlink 1000, statx 1000 - 1000 x `rmSync(missing, {force, recursive})`: unlinkat 1000 - 1000 x `writeFileSync` + `rmSync(file)`: unlink 1000, statx 1000 - 1000 x `writeFileSync` + `rmSync(file, {force, recursive})`: unlinkat 1000 - 100 x `rmSync(tree, {recursive})` (10 files, 1 subdirectory): unlinkat 1300 - 200 x `rm -f file` and 200 x `rm -f missing`: unlinkat 200 each - 100 x `rm -rf tree`: unlinkat 1300 - A warm `bun install` (isolated, `hoist = false`) in a writable project: newfstatat ENOENT and unlinkat ENOENT for the fallback directory, before and after. - Read-only mount, missing path: `unlink` or `unlinkat` 1 + `newfstatat` 1 per door (before: 1 + 0, then the error). Existing path: +1 `newfstatat`, still EROFS. Doors: `rmSync` with `force`, with `force` and `recursive`, shell `rm -f`, the `hoist = false` install, the empty lockfile. - Allocator calls inside the remover on the read-only mount (gdb breakpoints on the mimalloc entry points): `rmSync(missing, {force})` 2 -> 3, `{force, recursive}` 3 -> 3, shell `rm -f missing` 2 -> 4, `rmSync(file, {force})` 2 -> 3, `{force, recursive}` 3 -> 3, shell `rm -f file` 2 -> 4. The lookup takes a pooled path buffer. A thread whose pool is empty allocates one and keeps it. `lstatat` builds one error value for ENOENT. - Own instructions per call on a writable directory (gdb `nexti`, calls stepped over). `perf` counters and `valgrind` are not available on the build machine. - `NodeFS::rm`: file 35 -> 35, missing with `force` 69 -> 65, recursive file 52 -> 52, recursive missing 57 -> 57, recursive directory 52 -> 52 - `zig_delete_tree`: file 40 -> 40, missing 40 -> 48, directory 133 -> 130 - shell `remove_entry_file`: file 38 -> 39, missing 63 -> 69, directory 70 -> 73 - `Dir::delete_tree`, missing: 62 -> 60. `save_lockfile`, no `bun.lock`: 97 -> 97 - Size: `.text` 81,171,205 -> 81,172,229 (+1,024). `.rodata`, `.data` and `.bun_builtins`: +0. `removal_target_is_missing` is 256 bytes. `NodeFS::rm` +28, `zig_delete_tree` +119, `save_lockfile` +42, `Dir::delete_tree` -11. Shell `remove_entry_file` +156 and +191 (two instantiations), and +167 in `remove_entry_dir`, which inlines the third. - `bun run rust:check-all`: 12 of 12 targets pass. - CI: the four new tests ran and passed on debian 13 (x64, aarch64, x64-asan) and alpine 3.23 (x64, aarch64). Ubuntu 25.04 does not allow the namespace, so `canMount()` is false there and the tests skip. **Self-review** 26 concerns. Addressed: the fifth site (`save_lockfile`), the helper on every POSIX target, the control cells in the install and shell tests, the `file.txt/` and `directory` rows, the facts in these Notes. In part: - One probe for "can this test mount" is now `canMount()` in `test/harness.ts`. It makes a bind mount and a read-only remount. The mount commands stay in each test. - The related issue #44587 is named above. A report in another project's tracker is not linked from here. Rejected (3 of the 26, two of them are the same point): - The helper does not take the errno. The callers keep the `EROFS` test, so a caller with another errno (#44588, #43774) can use the same lookup. - No tracking issue for a merge of `Dir::delete_tree` and `zig_delete_tree`. That is a refactor, not a defect. Not run: macOS and FreeBSD. This change was built and tested on Linux only.
--- **no test proof** · iteration 0 · platform-specific test(s) that do not run on this machine, deferring to CI, which covers all platforms: test/js/node/fs/fs.test.ts, test/js/bun/shell/commands/rm.test.ts, test/cli/install/isolated-install.test.ts, test/cli/install/bun-lock.test.ts

items.title: fix(bin): bind live-lab tmux calls to explicit sockets so cleanup cannot kill the default server
items.body:
## Problem

Running `tests/fm-live-lab.test.sh` from inside tmux silently killed the user's default tmux server, and with it every session the user had open.
Nothing in the test output said so: the suite finished, and the terminal it ran in was gone.

## Root cause

tmux uses `TMUX_TMPDIR` only while that directory exists.
When it is missing, tmux 3.4 silently falls back to the default socket directory `/tmp/tmux-$UID/`.

The live lab and its tests addressed their private server through `TMUX_TMPDIR` alone:

- the test's EXIT cleanup ran `env -u TMUX TMUX_TMPDIR="$dir" tmux kill-server`;
- `bin/fm-live-lab.sh`'s `lab_tmux()` ran `env -u TMUX TMUX_TMPDIR="$TMUX_DIR" tmux "$@"`, including its `lab_tmux kill-server` in `down`.

Once the lab's private directory is gone, each of those commands reaches the user's real server instead.
Minimal reproduction (run it only in a private `/tmp`, for example under `unshare -Urm sh -c 'mount -t tmpfs tmpfs /tmp && exec sh'`):

```sh
unset TMUX                              # as the cleanup did with env -u TMUX
tmux new-session -d -s users-session    # stands in for the user's own server
dir=$(mktemp -d) && rmdir "$dir"        # a lab directory that no longer exists
TMUX_TMPDIR="$dir" tmux kill-server     # kills /tmp/tmux-$UID/default
tmux has-session -t users-session       # fails: the session is gone
```

## Fix

- `bin/fm-live-lab.sh` names the lab's socket explicitly on every tmux call (`tmux -S "$TMUX_DIR/tmux-$UID/default"`), including the server start, and never relies on `TMUX_TMPDIR` alone.
  `down` kills the server only while that socket exists, and does nothing otherwise.
- `tests/fm-live-lab.test.sh` and `tests/fm-live-lab-up-mate.test.sh` do the same for every tmux call they make, including the EXIT cleanup and the stub spawn scripts that run inside the lab.
- `tests/fm-gate-refuse.test.sh` drives and stops its lab server through the explicit socket path, with the same exists-only cleanup.
- The lab cleanup guidance in `bin/fm-brief.sh` (Herdr-lab briefs) and the `bin/fm-lab-home.sh` header now say to kill a lab server by its explicit socket, and only while it exists.
- `tests/lib.sh` gains `fm_tmux_isolation_gate`.
  A suite that starts or kills tmux servers runs only when no live tmux server answers in the default socket directory, as under a private `/tmp` or on a CI runner.
  Otherwise it skips with the isolation it needs, like the other gated suites:
  `skip: tmux isolation: a live tmux server answers on <socket>; run under a private /tmp (unshare -Urm sh -c 'mount -t tmpfs tmpfs /tmp && exec bin/fm-test-run.sh <test>')`.
  Both live-lab suites open with it.

Left as is, on purpose:

- The lab still exports `TMUX_TMPDIR` to the processes it launches, because that is how the lab's own firstmate backend finds the lab server.
  Those processes run only while the lab server, and so its directory, exists.
- `tests/fm-gate-refuse.test.sh` still starts its server through `TMUX_TMPDIR`, because that test proves the private-directory contract; the directory exists at that point.

## Regression coverage

`tests/fm-live-lab-isolation.test.sh` is new.

- It exercises the gate both ways: it runs where no server answers, skips with its message beside a live server (also under `CI=true`), and runs again once only a dead socket is left.
- It re-executes itself under `unshare -Urm` with a fresh tmpfs on `/tmp`, refuses to continue unless that `/tmp` is provably not the host one, and starts a decoy tmux server on the default socket there.
  It then points `pane`, `say`, `check` and `down` at a lab whose tmux directory has been removed, and asserts the decoy survives untouched.
  It also asserts that the old `TMUX_TMPDIR`-only form does reach the decoy, so the case cannot pass vacuously.
  The decoy is stopped by its explicit socket, then TERM and KILL on its recorded pid, each with a bounded poll, and a decoy that survives all three fails the suite instead of hanging it; cases prove the cleanup stops TERM-ignoring processes and returns promptly and reports failure for one it cannot stop.
  Where no private mount namespace is available, the decoy cases skip with the namespace they need.
- The cleanup treats an exited but unreaped decoy (a zombie that still answers `kill -0`) as gone, with a real zombie case, so a runner whose PID 1 does not reap orphans cannot fail the suite falsely.
- Against the pre-fix `bin/fm-live-lab.sh`, the suite fails: `pane` reads the decoy's window, and with only the kill path reverted, `down` kills the decoy server.

## Testing

- `tests/fm-live-lab.test.sh`, `tests/fm-live-lab-up-mate.test.sh`, `tests/fm-gate-refuse.test.sh` and `tests/fm-live-lab-isolation.test.sh` pass in full through `bin/fm-test-run.sh` inside a private `/tmp`.
- Beside a live default tmux server, both live-lab suites gate-skip, and the server keeps all of its sessions.
- A real `bin/fm-live-lab.sh up --harness claude` in a private `/tmp` passed its readiness checks, and `down` stopped only the lab's server while a decoy default server in the same `/tmp` survived.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh`, `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` and `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` pass.
- The isolation suite's deliberate cleanup waits are shortened (assertions unchanged) so it fits the portable serial budget, with a measured 3482 ms serial hint in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`.

CI keeps running the live-lab suites: a CI runner has no live default tmux server, so the gate passes there.
The only suite that uses the runner's ambient default server is `tests/fm-afk-launch.test.sh`, and it kills every session it creates.
Where a runner blocks unprivileged user namespaces, only the isolation suite's decoy cases skip; its gate cases still run.

## Pipeline

Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

<!-- no-mistakes-pipeline-attestation:v1 {"head_sha":"ed42b102bda83d9662184e4fb5d4ccc9aded4285","steps":[{"step":"intent","status":"completed"},{"step":"rebase","status":"completed"},{"step":"review","status":"completed"},{"step":"test","status":"completed"},{"step":"document","status":"completed"},{"step":"lint","status":"completed"},{"step":"push","status":"completed"},{"step":"pr","status":"skipped"},{"step":"ci","status":"skipped"}],"live_validation":{"verdict":"go","live":8,"total":9}} -->

- **Review** - 3 findings fixed on decision (the decoy runs only in a verified private `/tmp`, the gate has no bypass, and the gate always skips rather than failing under CI), then 1 follow-up auto-fixed (the namespaced suite drops inherited host temp directories); a later round fixed 2 findings on the bounded cleanup (its cases run on the host, and `kill-server` has its own deadline).
- **Test** - passed.
- **Document** - 1 doc-comment clarification applied.
- **Lint** - passed.
- **Push** - passed.

items.title: install: clear a package folder that cannot be renamed aside instead of linking on top of it
items.body:
Fixes #45184

### Problem
- A relink of a package whose folder cannot be renamed aside (a mount point, an open file on Windows, a read-only parent) copies the new files on top of the old ones. The old marker `.bun-tag-<hash>` stays, and the next install with that patch prints `(no changes)`.
- Cause: `move_aside` (`src/install/PackageInstall.rs:2131`) left the folder as it was on every rename error but `EXDEV`.

### Fix
- `move_aside` clears a folder it cannot rename: `package.json` and every `.bun-tag` marker first, then all else it can. A held file stays and the new copy goes in beside it. A mount point keeps the user's files and loses only the markers (#44968).
- A marker that cannot go fails the package. An in-place link that fails removes its markers. `verify` rejects a copy with two patch markers.
- The isolated linker clears its copy the same way.
- Verified: `test/cli/install/bun-install-patch.test.ts` (7 new tests, both linkers, all fail on main). Self-reviewed twice (Notes).

### Background
- The hoisted linker renames the old folder to `.old-<random>`, then a staged copy into place. When the first rename fails, the fallback links into the existing folder.
- `bun_sys::is_mount_point` asks `statx`: the kernel reports a read-only parent before a mount, and on Windows `EBUSY` from `rmdir` is an open folder.

### Downsides
- In a mount point, and beside a held file, old files of the previous patch stay next to the new ones. The markers are right, so the next patch change relinks.
- A no-op install lists the folder of each patched package (4 syscalls) instead of one `fstatat`.
- Release binary: text +5888 B (`size`, main 5866b5f13d and this branch).

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

**Repro on Linux** (release build of main): `patchedDependencies` for `ms@2.1.3`, patch A adds `extra.js` and `generation = "A"`, patch B sets `generation = "B"`. Install A. Switch to B and install with `node_modules/ms` bind-mounted onto itself (`unshare -Urm`): main exits 0 with both markers and `extra.js`. Switch back to A: main prints `Checked 1 install across 2 packages (no changes)` and `require("ms").generation` is `B`. This branch: the second install leaves one marker (B's), the third relinks to A.

The same happens on main with a read-only parent folder, for both linkers: `setpriv --bounding-set -dac_override,-dac_read_search bun install` as root, or any user that does not own the parent. That is what the tests use.

**Self-review, round 1**: the first version emptied a mount point too, which reversed #44968 ("a mount point stays") and failed its test for the hoisted linker. **Round 2** (5 concerns, all addressed): `rmdir` `EBUSY` is not a mount point on Windows and is masked by `EACCES` on Linux, so `bun_sys::is_mount_point` asks `statx`; `install_from_link` no longer touches a folder it cannot rename; the markers go before the rest of the folder; an in-place link that fails removes its markers; a copy with two markers is installed again. Not done: one shared probe for `move_or_delete` and `Symlinker::ensure` in the isolated linker. They keep their `rmdir` probe.

**The existing test** `symlink backend replaces an existing file with a link to the source` asserted that a stray file survives the in-place install, as proof that the in-place path ran. It now checks that the folder's inode is the same and that the stray file is gone.

**Tests**: the permission tests run as root only with `setpriv` (the pattern of the test above them), and not on Windows. The mount test runs for the hoisted linker on Linux where `unshare -Urm` works, with a read-only parent as well. The two-marker test runs everywhere.

**Also run** (debug build): `bun-install-patch` (61), `isolated-install`, `bun-install-backends`, `bun-patch`, `bun-prune` (762 pass across the five), `bun-install` and `bun-add` (1018).

**Not changed**: the isolated linker's `Symlinker` keeps a mount point with a `package.json`, and `move_or_delete` leaves a Windows folder with an open file intact. Both link symlinks, not files.

</details>

<!-- robobun:evidence:begin -->

---

**no test proof** · iteration 0 · platform-specific test(s) that do not run on this machine, deferring to CI, which covers all platforms: test/cli/install/bun-install-windows-rename-retry.test.ts, test/cli/install/bun-install-patch.test.ts, test/cli/install/bun-install-backends.test.ts

<!-- robobun:evidence:end -->

items.title: findmnt: build the tree without rescanning the mount table
items.body:
The default tree output of findmnt is quadratic in the number of mounts. With 16000 tmpfs mounts under one directory (in `unshare -Urm`):

```
$ time findmnt >/dev/null       # before: 2.97 s    after: 0.16 s
$ time findmnt -J >/dev/null    # before: 2.85 s    after: 0.08 s
```

`--list` was already fast, so the time is all in building the tree. `create_treenode()` calls `has_line()` for every node, which walks the whole output table, and gets children through `mnt_table_next_child_fs()`, which rescans the whole mount table on every call. A parent with k children costs k full scans, which hurts on container hosts where lots of mounts sit under one parent.

The fix marks added filesystems through their userdata pointer (findmnt didn't use it), so `has_line()` is a pointer comparison, and builds one array of all entries sorted by (parent ID, ID, table position) before the output is filled in; children are looked up in it with a binary search. Children come out in the same order as before, and the odd entries (ID equal to parent ID, repeated IDs) are skipped the same way `mnt_table_next_child_fs()` skips them. The only behavior change is for a child with ID 0 in a `-F` file, which the old iterator returned forever (no output, or a hang with `--submounts`); the kernel never uses ID 0. I kept this in findmnt rather than libmount, so other libmount users are not affected.

Tested by diffing baseline vs patched findmnt output and exit codes over 1130 option/target combinations on flat, deep, mixed, over-mounted and bind/rbind layouts, plus 6000 runs on randomly generated `-F` tables with duplicate, negative, self-parent and orphan IDs: all identical, also under ASan/UBSan. `tests/run.sh findmnt libmount mount` passes.

items.title: Per-arm project_exclude so a baseline can't read the skills under test
items.body:
**TL;DR** — Add an arm-level `project_exclude` glob list that drops paths from that arm's staged `/project`, so a bare baseline can't find and read the skills its trial arm is measured on.

## Problem

- **Symptom:** When an eval prompt names a skill ("Use the `to-spec` skill …"), the baseline agent calls `Skill to-spec`. That fails, so it runs `find / -iname "*to-spec*"` and reads `/project/skills/to-spec/SKILL.md` plus its assets and scripts by hand. The baseline then scores like the trial, and the delta collapses.
- **Measured (mechaswift eval notes, "Baseline contamination"):**
  - to-spec/spec-from-context: the baseline read the skill in 3/3 samples and scored 97%, against 30% recorded on Sep 4.
  - writing-agent-skills/improve-changelog-skill: 7/12.
  - react-conventions-trap: 1/3.
  - db-migrate-internals-trap: 1/3.
- **Why it stayed hidden:** The mount is identical on both arms by design (`SandboxSession.__aenter__` → `stage_project(self._host_repo_root)`, `src/benchspec/sandbox/sandbox.py:318`). Contamination only shows up when someone greps baseline `session.jsonl` files for `/project/`.
- **Exposed by:** The baseline scores on mechaswift's output evals jumped. The cause was traced through the baseline session transcripts.
- **Constraint: the guest can't hide it itself.** On the Docker backend the guest runs as root without `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, so `mount -t tmpfs … /project` from `setup.sh` fails with `permission denied`. `/project` is also read-only (`src/benchspec/sandbox/docker.py:716`, `src/benchspec/sandbox/microsandbox.py:331`), so nothing can be deleted from it either. Hiding has to happen host-side, when the stage is built.
- **Constraint: the trial must stay intact.** The trial arm needs the full copy for `harness_args = ["--plugin-dir", "/project"]`.
- **Constraint: setup still has to run.** Both arms still need each scenario's `setup.sh` and the files it sources.
- **Scope:** The staged `/project` of any arm session that sets `project_exclude`. Output evals and routing evals both run through `SandboxSession`, so it applies to both.

## Solution

```toml
[tool.benchspec.sets.default]
arms = [
  { name = "baseline", project_exclude = ["skills", ".claude-plugin", "hooks", "docs", "*.md"] },
  { name = "trial", harness_args = ["--plugin-dir", "/project"] },
]
```

`stage_project` skips any repo-relative path that matches, or whose parent directory matches, one of the arm's globs. The trial's copy doesn't change.

## User Stories

1. As an eval author, I want **the baseline's `/project` to omit the skills under test**, so a baseline delta measures what the skill taught rather than what the agent found on disk.
2. As an eval author, I want **the eval assertions (`eval.md`) and recorded results hidden from the baseline too**, so the baseline can't read the grading rubric.
3. As an eval author, I want **`setup.sh` and its support files to stay visible on every arm**, so shared provisioning (such as a fake CLI) still runs on the baseline.
4. As an eval author, I want **a malformed `project_exclude` to fail at config-read time**, so a typo doesn't silently leave the baseline contaminated.

## Implementation Decisions

```
[tool.benchspec.sets.*] ──► config/arms.py parse_sets (validate) ──► Arm.project_exclude
  ──► orchestration/execution.py run_eval_arm ──► _run_arm_turns ──► sandbox.arm_session
  ──► SandboxSession.__aenter__ ──► project.stage_project(repo_root, exclude=…) ──► /project mount
```

- **Arm field, merged like `harness_args`.**
  - `Arm.project_exclude: list[str]` uses `field(default_factory=list, hash=False)`.
  - Add `"project_exclude"` to `_SET_DEFAULT_KEYS`. Arm-level globs append after set-level ones.
  - Validate it as a list of non-empty strings, raising `SchemaError` otherwise.
- **Matching uses `fnmatch.fnmatchcase` on POSIX repo-relative paths.**
  - Test the path itself and each of its parent prefixes, so `skills` and `skills/*` both drop the whole tree.
  - `*` crosses `/`, which lets `*.md` hide every markdown file.
  - Avoid `PurePath.match` with `**`, which behaves differently across Python versions.
- **Exclusions are applied after the existing filters.** `project_exclude` is checked after `_stageable` (`src/benchspec/sandbox/project.py:119`). The dotenv, `.git` and `tmp/` exclusions, and the fail-closed dotenv check, don't change.
- **Threaded through, not global.** The list goes through `run_eval_arm`, `_run_arm_turns`, `arm_session` and `SandboxSession`, next to `harness_args`. Every existing caller keeps its behavior through the default `None`, which excludes nothing.
- **Old versions ignore the key.** 0.0.5 does not reject unknown arm keys, so it would drop `project_exclude` without warning. Consumers must pin to the release that ships this.
- **A reference implementation exists.** It is on the local branch `feat/arm-project-exclude` (commit `5024e34`, not yet pushed): about 170 lines including tests and docs. With it, a one-sample probe on mechaswift's to-spec/spec-from-context scored baseline 9% and trial 91%. The baseline session showed no reads under `/project/`, and the trial still invoked the skill.

## Testing Plan

### Logic
- **Globs drop matches and only matches.** An excluded file or directory tree is missing from the stage, and unmatched files, including `setup.sh` and its sourced support files, are still present.
- **Directory globs drop the whole subtree.** A bare directory name and `dir/*` both remove every file under that directory.
- **Built-in exclusions still apply.** Dotenv files, `.git` and `tmp/` stay out of the stage whatever `project_exclude` says.

### Behavior
- **Arm isolation.** In a real two-arm run, the arm with `project_exclude` can't read excluded paths under `/project`, while the other arm's `--plugin-dir /project` still loads the plugin.

### Interface
- **Config contract.** Set-level and arm-level values merge in order, and a non-list value or an empty or non-string entry raises `SchemaError` naming `project_exclude`.
- **Back-compat.** A set that omits `project_exclude` stages exactly what it staged before.

## Documentation Plan

- **docs/configuration.md**: add a `project_exclude` row to the `[tool.benchspec.sets.<name>]` key table next to `harness_args` (line 46), and add it to the list of `arms` keys.
- **docs/sandbox.md**: under "What `/project` contains" (line 145), add a "Per arm" bullet warning users not to exclude `setup.sh` or the files it sources.
- **CHANGELOG / release notes**: note the new key and that 0.0.5 silently ignores it.

## Out of Scope

- **An arm-level switch to skip the `/project` mount entirely.** `setup.sh` is read from `/project`, so skipping the mount would break provisioning on that arm.
- **Changing the guest's privileges** (for example `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`) so `setup.sh` could mount over paths itself. That widens the attack surface just to work around a gap in the config.
- **Rewording eval prompts so they don't name the skill.** That changes what the evals test.

## References

- `src/benchspec/sandbox/project.py:92` — `stage_project`, where the filter goes.
- `src/benchspec/sandbox/sandbox.py:318` — the per-session stage call that the arm's globs must reach.
- `src/benchspec/config/arms.py:45` — `_SET_DEFAULT_KEYS`, the model for set-level/arm-level merging.
- `src/benchspec/sandbox/docker.py:716` — `/project` is bind-mounted read-only, which is why the guest can't hide files itself.
- theycallmeswift/mechaswift PR #40, branch `claude/trigger-evals-cap-10`: `docs/evals/to-spec.md` and `docs/evals/writing-agent-skills.md` ("Baseline contamination" notes) record the contaminated runs.

## Verification

- `make test` — unit suite green, including the new staging and config tests.
- `make lint:ruff lint:ty` — clean.
- In mechaswift, with the release pinned, run `make evals SKILL=to-spec EVAL_ARGS="-n 6 --count 3 -k spec-from-context"`, then `grep -l '/project/' tmp/evals/iteration_<new>/skills/*/*/baseline/*/session.jsonl`. The grep should print nothing.

items.title: getBlockVolumes parses all of mountinfo once per bind mount
items.body:
## Description

`getBlockVolumes` parses the whole `/proc/thread-self/mountinfo` once for every bind mount in the container spec. Most bind mounts are not block devices (a Pod gets /etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf, the termination log and more), so the same file gets parsed over and over during `urunc create` for no reason.

I measured it with a benchmark that calls `getBlockVolumes` with n bind mounts whose sources are not mount points. Nothing is unmounted, so it needs no root. Cost grows linearly with the number of binds and with the size of mountinfo. On my laptop (32 mountinfo lines), 8 binds cost 223.74us per call. In a mount namespace with 532 lines, 8 binds cost 2051.4us.

This is small next to booting a VM. I am not claiming it changes create latency in a visible way. It is about 1.8ms saved per create on a host with a few hundred mounts, and it scales with the mounts on the node. The change is small and does not alter behaviour.

I'd parse mountinfo on the first bind mount and reuse it. After an unmount the table has changed, so I'd drop the cached copy and parse again on the next lookup. That keeps the results the same as today, including the "source is shared with another mount" check.

## System info

- Urunc version: e45d556 (main)
- Arch: amd64
- VMM: none, this is a unit-level benchmark
- Unikernel: none

## Steps to reproduce

1. Check out main and add `BenchmarkGetBlockVolumes` (it is in the PR).
2. `go test ./pkg/unikontainers -run '^$' -bench GetBlockVolumes -benchmem -count=10`
3. For a bigger mount table: `unshare -Urm`, mount 500 tmpfs, run the same command.

## Logs / output

```
BenchmarkGetBlockVolumes/binds=1-24    27243 ns/op    23384 B/op     135 allocs/op
BenchmarkGetBlockVolumes/binds=8-24   220316 ns/op   187072 B/op    1080 allocs/op
BenchmarkGetBlockVolumes/binds=16-24  444513 ns/op   374146 B/op    2160 allocs/op
```

Not tested: a real `urunc create` with block volumes (needs root, containerd and KVM). I did not run the e2e tests.

## LLM usage

Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Claude Code) helped find the code path, write the benchmark and draft this issue. I reviewed it and ran the benchmark myself.

items.title: The frozen /etc/ld.so.cache bind mount detaches when the host replaces its cache during a run
items.body:
[hermit2, hermit-lander, claude-opus-5-5, host withheld, role=impl]


**What happens.** Hermit binds a frozen copy of the host's dynamic-linker cache read-only over `/etc/ld.so.cache` in the container (`identity_hardening_mounts`, `frozen_ld_so_cache` in hermit-cli/src/bin/hermit/container.rs). Both runs of a `--verify` share one snapshot (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4693).

A package manager on the host replaces `/etc/ld.so.cache` by renaming a new file over it. Since Linux 3.18 (commit 8ed936b5671b, "vfs: Lazily remove mounts on unlinked files and directories"), a rename over a dentry that is a mountpoint in another mount namespace succeeds, and the mounts on the old dentry are detached. The container's bind mount is gone, so a guest that opens the cache afterwards gets the host's new file. The fix for 4693 kept the two runs' snapshot bytes equal, but it cannot keep the mount in place.

**Evidence.** On 2026-10-26 two test.cli cases failed `--verify-strict` in one quiet run on the host, outside the pinned root. Hermit main was cbbe4c75 with the validate-profile Hermit.
- `a_cross_process_sigkill_notification_verifies_at_bitwise_parity` failed on mode latesfdtwokills (ptrace).
- `detcore_fixes_the_virtual_kernel_files_on_dbt` failed too.
- In both, the first difference is the loader's `fstat` of its cache descriptor: run 1 saw `dev=0x1 ino=9000 uid=0` (the frozen copy) and run 2 saw `dev=0x2 ino=9318 uid=65534` (the host file, root unmapped), or the reverse.
- The host's `/etc/ld.so.cache` ctime, 19:32:43 PDT, falls inside that run. Host dnf starts about 100 times an hour.

When the replacement lands while the container is being set up, Hermit instead refuses the run: "Refusing mountinfo provenance for /etc/ld.so.cache: the completed mount target does not match the pinned Hermit-owned source". That happened to two test.cli cases in the same loop iteration on 2026-10-27, at the moment the host's cache ctime changed.

**Reproduction of the mechanism** (Linux 7.1.3):
1. `unshare -Urm` and bind file `frozen` over `target`; the namespace reads `frozen`.
2. In the parent namespace, `mv new target`.
3. The namespace now reads `host-new` through `target`.

**Who is affected.** Any Hermit run on a host whose cache gets replaced: e2e cells and CLI tests run outside the pinned root. Inside the pinned root, which has its own `/etc`, it does not happen.

**Directions.**
1. After each run, check that `/etc/ld.so.cache` in the container still resolves to the frozen copy. If not, name it as a host input change, so harnesses retry it rather than report a divergence.
2. Give the guest a view of `/etc` that host renames cannot detach, for example an overlay whose upper layer holds the frozen files.
3. Have Detcore answer the cache from the snapshot.

items.title: BUG-094: Gate f compares paths as strings, so a process in another mount namespace reads as 'outside' and its worktree is deleted
items.body:
`dotf worktree sweep`'s Gate f decides whether a live process is sitting in a worktree by
comparing `/proc/<pid>/cwd` against the worktree path **as strings**. `/proc/<pid>/cwd` is
resolved by the kernel in the *process's own mount namespace*, so a process that reaches the
worktree through a bind mount reports a path that does not exist on the host. The strings
differ, Gate f answers "nobody is inside", and the caller deletes the worktree.

BUG-093 closed the symlink instance of this class (`filepath.EvalSymlinks` on the target). This
is the same class arriving through a different door, and resolution does not close it.

## Reproduction (measured 2026-09-05)

```
docker run -d -u 1000:1000 -v /tmp/wtmount-repro/repo-wt-feat:/wt-mount-target \
           -w /wt-mount-target busybox sleep 60

host readlink /proc/2658284/cwd  -> /wt-mount-target
worktree path on host            -> /tmp/wtmount-repro/repo-wt-feat
dev/ino of /proc/<pid>/cwd       -> 50/992409
dev/ino of the worktree path     -> 50/992409     <- the same directory
string comparison                -> False         <- Gate f says "outside"
```

A second shape falls out of the same weakness: a worktree directory deleted and then recreated
makes `readlink` yield `".../repo-wt-feat (deleted)"`, which matches neither the equality nor the
prefix test. That one is not a data-loss path (the process holds the old inode), but it is the
same defect.

## Fix

Identity by `dev`+`ino` (`os.SameFile`) instead of by string, walking parents from
`/proc/<pid>/cwd/..` for the subdirectory case. `os.Stat("/proc/<pid>/cwd")` follows the magic
link and stats the real directory, so the comparison works across namespaces — the measurement
above shows it seeing what the string comparison does not.

Note the permission bound is unchanged: `os.Stat` on `/proc/<pid>/cwd` is gated by
`ptrace_may_access` exactly as `os.Readlink` is, so this widens *correctness*, not *reach*.

## Why it was declared rather than fixed in BUG-093

The code is ~20 lines; the **test** is the problem. Reproducing it needs a mount namespace.
`unshare -Urm` is refused on the development machine
(`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1`, Ubuntu's default since 24.04), and whether a
GitHub `ubuntu-latest` runner permits one was not measurable from there. A test that skips on the
runner reports green while asserting nothing — the exact shape of the vacuous test the round-3
review found in this same file (lesson 273). Landing the fix without a CI-runnable test would
repeat the defect the spec exists to remove.

**First task of this ticket is therefore a measurement, not a patch:** determine on a runner
whether `unshare -Urm` (or a `docker`-based fixture) can construct the namespace. If neither can,
the honest outcome is a documented limitation rather than an untested fix.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A test that fails against the current string comparison and passes against the `dev`+`ino` one,
   running in CI on `ubuntu-latest` — or a recorded measurement showing why no such test can exist.
2. Subdirectory case covered: a process in `<worktree>/sub/deep` reached through a bind mount.
3. The separator-anchored sibling case (`repo-wt-feat` vs `repo-wt-feature-two`) still refuses,
   whichever comparison lands.
4. `sweep_proc_linux.go`'s comment stops describing the remaining door as closed.

items.title: [P1] Local resident sets: a GPU-host NVMe cache tier with leases (design first; measure before build)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: A gate that cannot catch its own defect, or a wrong/underived number a decision reads

labels.name: issuegraph
labels.description: issuegraph pipeline: Rob requests an automated fix (D57)

items.body:
Rob's direction (via the CEO, 2026-10-05): "Things that will be needed a lot should probably not be streamed from dl380 and instead delivered for campaign duration and cleaned up afterwards." Add the GPU hosts' local NVMe as a cache tier.

**Design note (draft, for Opus pool review):** `docs/local_resident_sets_design_2026-10-05.md` on branch `pb/design-local-resident-sets` (28b6978f). No code yet.

## What the note changes in the CEO's sketch
1. **Accelerator with fallback, not a gate.** The existing residency machinery gates admission on residency; reused unchanged, a host-local tier would pin rows to one host, which D26 forbids. Local residency never blocks a claim; the canonical path stays authoritative; PB injects the mount only when the set is complete, verified and leased on the claiming host. The fallback is silent to the job, so each attempt must record `served_from`.
2. **No private mount namespace.** Verified on both Sparks: `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`, and `unshare -Urm` fails (`uid_map: Operation not permitted`). Only a root helper (the resource broker) could do it. First release: containers only.
3. **Not the window tier.** Reuse movement receipts, `ResourceLedger`, pins and the data manifest; do not generalise the dl380-centric `tier_loop`.

## Facts that gate the build
- Sparky `/` has **125 GiB free (93% used)**, sparklina **147 GiB**; `/var/lib/docker` shares that filesystem (images 186 / 219 GB). D1 needs 1.5N + 20 GiB free to write N GiB: **copying A8S (163.47 GiB) needs about 265 GiB free; neither Spark can today**. Depends on the Opus cleanup (`spark-local-models`).
- **Speed is unproven.** Issue #523's reporter measured 259 MB/s serial and 9,348 MB/s with 32 readers over the same NFS-RDMA mounts; the single-stream figure measured today is 852 MB/s. A local copy may buy independence and reload reliability more than raw speed.
- A nested bind mount **shadows the whole canonical directory**; a stale local copy is worse than a slow read. Sets must be immutable and cover the whole directory.

## Phases
0 measure (multi-stream NFS vs local NVMe, Docker nested bind, NVMe write vs a running GPU job, post-cleanup space) with a go/no-go gate; 1 resident sets without placement (records, policy file, ledger kind, mover, verification, lease pass, pin-protected eviction, adoption of the manual copies); 2 container injection in the Docker shim; 3 locality preference in offers and gang election; 4 campaign lease integration.

## Prior (D33)
Hindsight was unreachable when this was written (health `crit`, connection reset); only the fleet's own records were searched. Reviewers: please rerun the history query and attach hits.

Related: #583, #909, #1026, #1517, #523.

items.title: fix(layout): grow the filesystem on a thread of its own
items.body:
## What

`ephemeralMount` unshares the mount namespace so the temporary mount the grow
needs is not visible to the rest of the system:

```go
_ = unix.Unshare(unix.CLONE_NEWNS)
_ = unix.Mount("", "/", "", unix.MS_REC|unix.MS_PRIVATE, "")
```

A mount namespace belongs to an OS thread, not to a goroutine, and Go gives no
goroutine a thread of its own. So the unshare lands on whichever thread the
caller happens to be scheduled on, and when `GrowFSToMax` returns, the runtime
puts that thread back in the pool with its frozen view of the mount tree still
on it. The next goroutine to ask for a thread can get it.

That is a problem for anything that mounts in the same process afterwards. A
mount made from another thread does not exist as far as the stale thread is
concerned, so code running there sees whatever was underneath.

In `immucore` this is a boot bug. The `Grow persistent` stage in
`00_rootfs.yaml` is an `expand_partition` layout stage, it runs from the
`rootfs` yip stage in-process, and the mount DAG that follows it in the same
process then mounts `COS_PERSISTENT` on `/sysroot/usr/local` and the `/etc`
overlay. On a fraction of boots the bind step reports, for mounts it made
itself a moment earlier:

```
* mkdir /sysroot/usr/local/.state: read-only file system
* mkdir /sysroot/etc/cni: read-only file system
* mounting ".state/home.bind" at "/sysroot/home": no such file or directory
```

The read-only active image showing through at a path that was just mounted
read-write is exactly the shape of a stale mount namespace, and which entries
are hit varies from boot to boot, which is exactly what thread scheduling gives
you. Reported as kairos-io/kairos#4837, and the matching CI failure is
kairos-io/kairos#4743.

## Fix

Run the grow on a goroutine that locks its OS thread and never unlocks it, so
the runtime destroys the thread when the goroutine returns and the namespace
dies with it. Two smaller fixes in the same path:

- Only `MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE` the mount tree when the unshare actually succeeded.
  The error was discarded, and in the shared namespace that line turns every
  mount on the machine private and breaks propagation for everything else.
- Drop the `runtime.SetFinalizer`. It would run the unmount on an arbitrary
  thread, in a namespace where the mount does not exist. Every caller already
  defers `cleanup`.

## Test

`TestRunOnDedicatedThreadRetiresTheThread` records the thread `fn` ran on and
then asks the runtime for 256 locked goroutines. None may land on that thread.
It fails 5 times out of 5 when the helper is changed to `defer
runtime.UnlockOSThread()`, and passes 5 out of 5 with the fix:

```
--- FAIL: TestRunOnDedicatedThreadRetiresTheThread (0.00s)
    a later goroutine ran on thread 11492, the one fn mutated
```

`TestRunOnDedicatedThreadContainsUnshare` does the real check, that the
caller's `/proc/thread-self/ns/mnt` is unchanged after `fn` unshares. It needs
`CAP_SYS_ADMIN` and skips without it. It is skipped, not run, on the machine
this was prepared on: user namespaces are blocked there, so `unshare -Urm`
cannot give it the capability either.

`go test ./pkg/plugins/` gives 84 passed / 31 failed both before and after this
change. The 31 are the pre-existing user and layout specs that need root.

---

AI was used to write this change. No human has read it yet.

items.title: EPERM when renaming directory within overlay whose upper layer is tmpfs, from within a nested user namespace
items.body:
### Description

I'm currently hitting `unrecoverable overlayfs inconsistency: failed to make renamed directory opaque: operation not permitted` when running daemonless buildkit, `buildctl-daemonless.sh` as non-root, inside a gVisor pod.
This specifically occurs on any `RUN` step that renames a directory.

This only occurs when using the following gVisor mount hints for a K8s emptydir:
```yaml
dev.gvisor.spec.mount.<name>.share: pod
dev.gvisor.spec.mount.<name>.type: bind
```
as it results in a gofer-backend lower layer, with a `SelfOverlay` upperlayer. I.e. the container process sees a `tmpfs` mount, which is ultimately backed by the host.

The problem occurs when Buildkit ultimately calls [NeedsUserXAttr()](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/54a25ed63325d3e80f4319cf98a75b4519a8fe70/plugins/snapshots/overlay/overlayutils/check.go#L132), which then makes a call to [IsPathOnTmpfs()](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/54a25ed63325d3e80f4319cf98a75b4519a8fe70/plugins/snapshots/overlay/overlayutils/check.go#L102). This performs a `statfs()` syscall on the directory, which correctly returns the type as `tmpfs`.

As a result, `trusted.overlay.*` is attempted here: https://github.com/google/gvisor/blob/05b57c92aea0bda51ddd1983bf3ca43bee6f089c/pkg/sentry/fsimpl/overlay/filesystem.go#L1322-L1329

which fails because the gofer and sentry processes do not have the required capabilities to set trusted xattrs on the host filesystem.

https://github.com/google/gvisor/pull/12982 resolved this for `9p` upperdirs by adding:
```go
if upperFSName == "9p" && !userXattr {
	// Neither the gofer nor sentry processes have the capabilities to set
	// trusted xattrs on the host filesystem. Setting `trusted.overlay.*`
	// xattrs requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the root user namespace. So enable
	// `userxattr` mount option as a workaround.
	ctx.Infof("overlay.FilesystemType.GetFilesystem: gofer filesystem used as overlay upper layer; enabling userxattr")
	userXattr = true
}
```
However my case still fails.

Also for context, the reason I am using these mount hints is because some buildkit builds with `XDG_DATA_HOME` on a gofer mount would lock up and hang indefinitely (similar to https://github.com/google/gvisor/issues/12209). I suspect the mount hints avoided this since it greatly reduced the amount of dentry cache revalidations by the gofer (gvisor dump showed stuck mutexes around dentry cache checks).

### Steps to reproduce

This issue can be reproduced without buildkit:

1. Create a simple pod that uses the pod and bind mount hints on an emptydir:
    ```yaml
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Pod
    metadata:
      name: test-overlay
      annotations:
    ```

items.title: ChatGPT VS Code extension 26.707.41301

labels.name: extension
labels.description: Issues related to the VS Code extension

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

items.body:
### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

ChatGPT VS Code extension 26.707.41301

### What subscription do you have?

team

### Which IDE are you using?

VS Code

### What platform is your computer?

Host: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Kernel 6.17  Remote: VS Code Dev Container Ubuntu 22.04

### What issue are you seeing?

When using the ChatGPT VS Code extension (openai.chatgpt 26.707.41301) inside a VS Code Dev Container, Codex Agent fails to initialize its filesystem sandbox.

The Output log shows:

codex_core::tools::router: error=apply_patch verification failed:
fs sandbox helper failed with status exit status: 1:
bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted

As a result, operations that rely on the filesystem sandbox fail, including apply_patch verification. Earlier in the chat, the agent also reported that sandbox initialization failed due to the network namespace.

The issue occurs even though the container itself supports network namespaces when running as root.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Host OS: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.
2. Open a Ubuntu 22.04 Dev Container in VS Code.
3. Install the ChatGPT extension (openai.chatgpt 26.707.41301).
4. Open a Git repository inside the container.
5. Ask Codex Agent to modify a file using apply_patch (or perform another filesystem operation that uses the sandbox).
6. The filesystem sandbox initialization fails with:

   bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted

7. apply_patch verification fails because the sandbox helper cannot start.

### What is the expected behavior?

If the sandbox cannot be initialized because the current environment does not permit configuring a network namespace or loopback interface, Codex should gracefully fall back instead of failing filesystem operations.

At minimum, when "Allow Unsandboxed Commands" is enabled, safe operations such as apply_patch verification and other read/write operations should either:
- run outside the sandbox after confirmation, or
- provide a clear fallback path.

The extension should not make normal editing workflows unusable because sandbox initialization failed.

### Additional information

Environment

Host:
- Ubuntu 24.04
- Linux 6.17.0

Container:
- Ubuntu 22.04
- VS Code Dev Container

Extension:
- openai.chatgpt 26.707.41301

Investigation

As the normal container user:

$ unshare -n true
Operation not permitted

$ grep Cap /proc/self/status
CapEff: 0000000000000000

As root inside the same container:

# unshare -n true

(succeeds)

This indicates that:

- The kernel supports network namespaces.
- The failure only occurs for the unprivileged user used by the extension.
- The sandbox helper (bubblewrap) fails while configuring the loopback interface.

Relevant log:

codex_core::tools::router:
error=apply_patch verification failed:
fs sandbox helper failed with status exit status: 1:
bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted

This appears to be a sandbox compatibility issue in Dev Containers. It would be helpful if Codex could detect this environment and automatically fall back instead of failing filesystem operations.

items.title: Deliver Kubernetes as a signed rootless application pack
items.body:
## Current scope
Deliver Kubernetes as a prebuilt, signed, self-contained .mvmpkg application pack resolved by a logical application reference. Templates are retired; users must not generate a template or build the environment themselves. This is backlog work outside the Claude-first critical path (#31), not a completed deliverable.

## Ownership and invariants
Kubernetes-specific package definitions, policy, documentation and validation remain here. Reuse the canonical builder/bundler, existing authenticated registry and independent bundle trust. Shared kernel/base requirements belong to generic mvm-images capability contracts, not Kubernetes-specific variants. Preserve uid-901 workload isolation, read-only rootfs, explicitly admitted persistent storage under /data or /work, and the no-guest-NIC boundary. No TAP/TUN or dev-tier workaround may be represented as sealed production support. External traffic uses the existing host-mediated vsock path and admitted policy.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Reassess rootless k3s feasibility against current released runtime and shared base capability contracts.
- [ ] Pin software, dependencies and base inputs; define architecture, resources, writable state and policy.
- [ ] Build, reproduce, sign and attest through #12; publish an authenticated application descriptor and independently verify bundle trust.
- [ ] Document logical pull/install/run, persistent storage, admitted egress/ingress and teardown without template generation.
- [ ] Prove fresh-host node readiness, permitted image pull, workload egress, declared ingress and teardown.
- [ ] Record tamper/revocation/admission refusal and unsupported-capability failures.
- [ ] Close only after reviewed implementation and actual-use evidence land.

## Historical disposition
PR #2 and earlier comments retain experimental template bring-up evidence. The retired templates/kubernetes path, old template-index registration and dev-tier boot-selection contract are superseded, not completed. No live signing, publication, cloud operation or new trust authority is authorized by this backlog issue.

items.title: tls: read the Linux system CA store from OpenSSL's default paths only
items.body:
Fixes #46922

### Problem
- On Linux, `--use-system-ca` trusts a CA the distro deselected: a file in `/usr/share/ca-certificates/` that `/etc/ca-certificates.conf` does not select. `fetch()` accepts a leaf it signed. Node rejects it with `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`.
- `src/runtime/socket/system_certs.rs` walked a list of well-known paths that held `/usr/share/ca-certificates` and `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ca-certificates.crt`, the input of `update-ca-certificates`.

### Fix
- The loader reads what Node reads: `$SSL_CERT_FILE` else `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`, and every regular file in `$SSL_CERT_DIR` else `/etc/ssl/certs`. Both `WELL_KNOWN_*` lists are gone. Android keeps its stores.
- #40862 kept the list "so no layout trusts fewer CAs than before". On Debian 13 it added one certificate, the deselected one. Every shipped layout puts its trust output under `/etc/ssl` (table in Notes). The result equals node v26.3.0: 152 roots, same order. Main returns 153.
- Verified: `test/js/node/tls/test-use-system-ca.test.ts` (six new cases: input trees, empty `SSL_CERT_DIR`, RPM-style `/etc/ssl` links). Also `node-use-system-ca.test.ts` and the ported `test-tls-get-ca-certificates-*system*.js`.

### Background
- `update-ca-certificates` reads the input trees, keeps the entries selected in `/etc/ca-certificates.conf`, and writes links and the bundle to `/etc/ssl/certs`. The `ca-certificates` RPM links `/etc/ssl` to what `update-ca-trust` writes under `/etc/pki`.
- Considered removing only `/usr/share/ca-certificates`: it keeps `/usr/local/share/certs` (FreeBSD `certctl` input) and the rule that admitted it. #40859 built this loader before.

### Downsides
- A host with no `/etc/ssl` (NetBSD, AIX, a container with only `/etc/pki`) now has an empty system store and needs `SSL_CERT_DIR` or `SSL_CERT_FILE`, as with Node. The bundled roots still apply. A user who sets `SSL_CERT_DIR` alone no longer gets the distro bundle on top of it: before, the bundle list ran whenever `SSL_CERT_FILE` was unset.
- Syscalls per process in system CA mode: 1127 before, 1069 after (ptrace, Debian 13). Wall clock 771 vs 774 ms median over 20 interleaved debug runs (spread 715 to 1112 ms). Debug text 1796 bytes smaller, release not measured.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Repro on the unfixed build, Debian 13, CA copied to `/usr/share/ca-certificates/robobun-test-ca.crt` and not selected:

```
$ bun run repro.ts
fetch error: UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE
$ NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1 bun run repro.ts
fetch: 200
$ node --use-system-ca node-client.mjs
fetch error: UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE
```

Per-layout answer to "no layout trusts fewer CAs than before":

- Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine, Arch, Gentoo, NixOS: `update-ca-certificates` writes hashed links and `ca-certificates.crt` to `/etc/ssl/certs`. Alpine and Arch also have `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.
- RHEL, Fedora, Amazon Linux: the `ca-certificates` RPM ships `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` and either `/etc/ssl/certs -> ../pki/tls/certs` (hashed links plus `ca-bundle.crt`) or, since Fedora's 2025.2.80-7, a real `/etc/ssl/certs` with three links to `tls-ca-bundle.pem` (rhbz#1053882, rhbz#1895619). Fedora dropped the `cert.pem` links in Jul 2025 (rhbz#2360110) and restored them in Apr 2026. In that window `/etc/ssl/certs` still held the hashed links. Node reads the same paths on every one of these states.
- openSUSE: `/etc/ssl/certs` links to `/var/lib/ca-certificates/pem`, one file per root.
- FreeBSD: `certctl` writes hashed links to `/etc/ssl/certs` and the bundle `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`. `/usr/local/share/certs` is its input, with an untrust list.
- `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ca-certificates.crt`: `update-ca-certificates` reads `*.crt` there and writes the bundle to `/etc/ssl/certs`. Nothing writes a file of that name there. A file there counts only once the tool has run, so it is the file-side instance of the same bug.
- `/etc/openssl/certs`, `/var/ssl/certs`, `/usr/local/etc/openssl/*`, `/System/Library/OpenSSL/certs`: NetBSD, AIX, Homebrew, and macOS paths. The posix loader never runs on macOS, and the others are not build targets.

The reporter suggested keeping `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt`. On every RPM layout it is reachable through `/etc/ssl/certs`, so the new test pins that layout instead of keeping the path.

The test "SSL_CERT_FILE alone keeps the default directory" pinned a superset. It now pins equality on purpose.

Syscalls in the loader window (from `openat /etc/ssl/cert.pem` to the last certificate path), main vs this branch: openat 170 vs 155 (ENOENT 12 vs 1), newfstatat 307 vs 279, fstat 157 vs 153, close 157 vs 152, getdents64 5 vs 3, read 313 vs 309. Main opens `/System/Library/OpenSSL/certs`, `/etc/openssl/certs`, `/etc/pki/*`, `/usr/local/*`, `/var/ssl/certs` and `/usr/share/ca-certificates`. The branch opens `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`, `/etc/ssl/certs` and its entries only.

`cargo check -p bun_runtime` passes for `aarch64-linux-android`, `x86_64-unknown-freebsd` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`.

The namespace tests need unprivileged user namespaces (`unshare -Urm`) and are skipped where those are disabled. The empty `SSL_CERT_DIR` test needs no namespace and fails on bun 1.4.3 on Debian and Ubuntu (151 entries from the bundle list, now 0).

Siblings for other platforms, not changed here: #46917 (Windows Disallowed store), #46918 (macOS SSL policy).

Self-reviewed: 9 concerns raised, 9 addressed (RPM layout rows, a namespace-free row, the per-layout rebuttal above, the module doc scope). Bot review: 7 threads, 5 addressed (concurrency, doc length, bind-mount probe, stop at a bad block, this Downsides line). Kept: the Fedora row's connect clause, and no `/etc/pki` fallback, see the thread replies.
</details>
