items.title: Can a codex turn run on a short-lived token instead of a readable auth.json?

labels.name: blocked-on-owner
labels.description: Waits on something only the owner can supply: a physical act, money, or a judgement

milestone.title: Post-cutover
milestone.description: Everything that does NOT block the owner moving off the legacy system: web/mobile polish, quality-of-life, and anything the spec defers.

items.body:
Splits out the one measurement that would close a security residual named in the codex persistence spike (#543), where it could not be settled without disturbing live credentials.

## Why it matters

The spike's credential criterion had to narrow its subject to **the adapter and its spawn boundary**, because two ways of covering the spawned turn itself both measured out:

- **Confinement is unavailable on this host.** `unshare -Urm` fails with `write failed /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted`; `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1`. So a test cannot make the turn's writable set equal the set an instrument scans.
- **Removing the credential from disk is unproven.** A turn with no `auth.json` at all, carrying only `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, reached the API and returned **401 Unauthorized** — the token was sent and rejected, which an unsupported channel would not do. But the only token obtainable without refreshing the live shared credential was **eight days old** against a lifetime of roughly an hour. *Expired* and *unsupported* are therefore indistinguishable from that result.

The named residual that follows: a `danger-full-access` turn — which is what a build runs — is unconfined, reads the long-lived credential file like any process of that user, and can copy it anywhere that user can write. No assertion covers that, and none can while both options above are closed.

A per-call short-lived token would close it, because there would be no durable credential on disk for a turn to copy. That makes this measurement the only remaining route.

## What to measure

Obtain a **fresh** access token and run one turn with no credential file present at all. The result separates the two hypotheses:

- the turn succeeds → the channel is supported, and a per-call token becomes a real design option; size the work to mint one per call and drop the file.
- the turn returns 401 with a token known-fresh → the channel is not supported, or not supported alone; record what else it needs, and the residual stands until confinement becomes available.

Design the run so it cannot be read the wrong way round: assert the credential file is absent at spawn (from the environment object captured at the spawn boundary, not from anything the subject can rewrite), and pin the token's age at the moment of use, so a later reader can tell a fresh 401 from a stale one. A 401 with an unrecorded token age proves nothing, which is exactly why this is a separate item.

**Do not refresh the shared live credential to get the token** — that is what blocked the measurement in the first place, because the refresh writes the file other work is using.

items.title: sys: replace the destination atomically in the cross-device move fallback
items.body:
### Problem
- `bun patch --commit` with the install cache on another filesystem than the project can lose the previous `patches/<pkg>.patch`. A full disk fails the move with `ENOSPC: No space left on device: failed renaming patch file to patches dir (write)` and leaves a truncated patch under the final name. The next `bun install` fails with `hunk_header_integrity_check_failed`.
- Two places in `src/sys/lib.rs` destroy the destination early. `renameat_concurrently_without_fallback` answers `EXDEV` with `delete_tree(dest)` plus a `renameat` that fails with `EXDEV` again. Then `copy_file_z_slow_with_handle` unlinks the destination, creates it with `O_TRUNC` and copies into it.

### Fix
- `renameat_concurrently_without_fallback` returns `EXDEV` at once, like `ENOENT`. Its last resort now tries a plain `renameat` first and deletes the destination only when that rename fails for another reason (a directory is in the way).
- `copy_file_z_slow_with_handle` copies into `dir/.base.<hex>.tmp` (`O_EXCL`) beside the destination, `fsync`s it, then renames it over the destination. A failed copy unlinks the temp file. `move_file_z_with_handle` calls it instead of an inline duplicate.
- Correct because the final rename stays inside one directory. The destination names the previous file or the complete copy at every moment.
- Verified: `test/cli/install/bun-patch.test.ts` (new test, bun 1.4.3 leaves a 135168 byte torn patch). Also the rest of that file, `bun-install-patch.test.ts`, the lcov tests, `cargo check -p bun_sys` on four targets.

### Background
- `rename(2)` replaces a name atomically, but only inside one filesystem. Across filesystems it fails with `EXDEV` and the caller has to copy.
- `move_file_z`, `move_file_z_with_handle` and `renameat_concurrently` share this `EXDEV` arm. Callers: `bun patch --commit`, `bun upgrade`, `--compile --outfile`, the lcov writer.
- `renameat_concurrently_without_fallback` tries `RENAME_NOREPLACE`, then `RENAME_EXCHANGE`, then delete-tree plus rename. It publishes directories into the install cache.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

This layout is common: a devcontainer or docker build with the project bind-mounted, a CI cache volume, `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` on another disk. A kill during the copy tears the file the same way as `ENOSPC` did.

Repro without root, bun 1.4.3, project on `/dev/shm` (64 MB tmpfs), cache on `/tmp`:

```sh
export BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/cache; cd /dev/shm/proj
# package.json depends on file:./markerbig-1.0.0.tgz (4000 line lib/big.js)
bun install && bun patch markerbig
echo '// small' >> node_modules/markerbig/lib/big.js && bun patch --commit node_modules/markerbig
stat -c %s patches/*.patch                       # 430
bun patch markerbig && sed -i 's/padding padding/PATCHED PATCHED/' node_modules/markerbig/lib/big.js
dd if=/dev/zero of=filler bs=1k count=$(( $(df -k --output=avail . | tail -1) - 100 ))
bun patch --commit node_modules/markerbig        # ENOSPC ... (write), exit 1
stat -c %s patches/*.patch                       # 106496, cut mid-hunk
rm filler; rm -rf node_modules; bun install      # hunk_header_integrity_check_failed
```

With this branch the second `stat` prints 430, `bun install` applies the patch, and nothing is left in `patches/` or in the cache temp dir. A cross-filesystem commit with enough space writes the complete 459971 byte patch with mode 0644.

strace of the unfixed move, for reference:

```
renameat2(cachetmp, ".3e9d…tmp", AT_FDCWD, "patches/markerbig@1.0.0.patch", RENAME_NOREPLACE) = -1 EXDEV
unlinkat(AT_FDCWD, "patches/markerbig@1.0.0.patch", 0) = 0
renameat(cachetmp, ".3e9d…tmp", AT_FDCWD, "patches/markerbig@1.0.0.patch") = -1 EXDEV
openat(AT_FDCWD, "patches/markerbig@1.0.0.patch", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0644) = 13
sendfile(13, 12, NULL, …) = -1 ENOSPC
```

The first `unlinkat` is the delete-tree of the sad path, the `openat(O_TRUNC)` is the copy fallback. Both are gone.

Replacing a running executable by rename also avoids the `ETXTBSY` that the old "unlink dest first" worked around, so `bun upgrade` across filesystems keeps working.

The test steps live in `test/cli/install/bun-patch-xdev-fixture.ts`. The project needs a small filesystem of its own that the fixture may fill for about a second. Where unprivileged user namespaces work, the test runs the fixture under `unshare -Urm` with a 16 MB tmpfs mounted on the project directory, so no other process can see or be affected by the fill. Where that is not available it uses `/dev/shm`, but only when `/dev/shm` is a mount of its own, at most 128 MB, and not the filesystem of the temp dir, which in practice means a container whose `/dev/shm` is its own. Elsewhere (macOS, Windows, hosts without user namespaces and with a large `/dev/shm`) it skips. The fixture leaves 128 KB free while the one `bun patch --commit` runs and removes the filler in a `finally`.

The sad path of `renameat_concurrently_without_fallback` used to be "delete-tree, then rename" unconditionally. Where the flagged renames are unsupported (FreeBSD reports `ENOSYS`, NFS `EINVAL`, Windows ignores the flags) every replace went through it. It now tries the plain rename first: a file destination is replaced atomically, an `EXDEV` or `ENOENT` ends the attempt with nothing deleted, and only a destination that is in the way (a directory) is deleted before the second rename.

`move_file_z_slow` still unlinks the source before the copy, as before. Every caller passes a temp file as the source, and unlinking first is what keeps a failed commit from leaving that temp file in the cache.

`cargo check -p bun_sys` passes for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-unknown-freebsd`.

#36229 and #41682 touch the same function for other reasons and will need a small rebase against this. #39713 fixes the `--compile --outfile` caller on its own by staging in the output directory.

Self-reviewed. Review feedback addressed so far: the temp file is `fsync`ed before the rename (bun's `close()` only reports `EBADF`, so deferred write errors on NFS would otherwise pass unseen), the FreeBSD/`ENOSYS` gap is closed by the sad-path reorder, and the test no longer fills a shared mount where a private one is possible.
</details>

items.title: Overhaul admin/: per-feature root-once scripts (userns incl. Ubuntu AppArmor, linger, ports, ...)
items.body:
`admin/enable-userspace.sh` is the one root step sudo-less has: the admin runs it once so a user can build views (user namespaces). Everything sudo-less does without root (dpkg in the install view, the run view, services and their sandbox) stands on it. It has fallen behind the rest of the repo; this issue tracks overhauling it into the per-feature layout planned in `docs/admin-features.md` ("Layout").

## What it does today

1. Writes `/etc/sysctl.d/99-userns.conf`: `kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone = 1`, `user.max_user_namespaces = 14030`, then `sysctl --system`.
2. Puts `~/.local/bin` on `PATH` for all users (`/etc/profile.d/50-local-bin.sh`).
3. Makes `~/.local/bin` and `~/.local/lib` for the user, and checks `unshare -Ur true`.

On stock Debian (11 and later) userns is already on, so step 1 changes nothing there and step 2 is done per user without root by `scripts/setup/install-shell-path.sh`.

## What is wrong or missing

- **Ubuntu 24.04 and later:** AppArmor restricts unprivileged user namespaces (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`). The script does not handle it, though `docs/view.md` sends readers to it for exactly that case. Needs a decision: the global sysctl, or a narrower AppArmor profile allowing `userns` for the prefix's `unshare` only (preferred: it does not open userns to every program).
- **`user.max_user_namespaces = 14030` is hardcoded:** the kernel's default scales with RAM and is often higher, so this can lower it. Only raise it when it is 0 or below a floor.
- **Stale final message:** it points to `tools/prefix-run.sh --mode overlay-native` and to installing bwrap; the mechanism is now `prefix-view` (install, run and service views), which needs neither.
- **No detection, no undo:** it does not say what it will change before calling `sudo`, is not a no-op when nothing needs changing, and has no `--undo`.
- **The other root-once grants are only on paper** (`docs/admin-features.md`, "Candidates"), and several now matter for services (#35, #36):
  - `linger`: the prefix's services run at boot and after logout, not only while logged in;
  - `ports`: `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start`, for servers below 1024 (mini-httpd needed 8080);
  - socket buffers: `net.core.rmem_max`/`wmem_max` (tailscale falls back to kernel defaults);
  - `subid`, `devices`, `cgroups`, `mounts`, as listed there.

## Plan

1. `admin/features/userns.sh`: detect (`/proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone`, `/proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces`, `/proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`), print what will change, apply the minimum (Debian sysctl, or the Ubuntu AppArmor case), `--undo`; test with `unshare -Urm` plus an overlay mount, which is what a view needs.
2. `admin/features/linger.sh`, `ports.sh`, `sockbuf.sh` next, then the rest of the candidates, each idempotent, with `--undo`.
3. `admin/enable-userspace.sh` becomes a thin wrapper running `userns.sh` (and the `PATH` step only if still wanted), or goes away.
4. Detection side, no root: `sudo-less doctor` (or a `prefix-*` check) reports which features are on; `prefix-check`/`prefix-units` read the same detection (for example, tell the user a low port needs the `ports` grant instead of failing silently).
5. Docs: `admin-features.md` rows marked done as they land, `problems.md` "root, once" cells pointing at the feature scripts, `view.md`'s "What it needs" pointing at `userns.sh`.

Every change under `admin/` touches `/etc` and needs the admin's confirmation before it is run on a real host; the scripts never run the user's software as root.

items.title: Some namespace path joining errors together with user ns
Linux: agent commands can create user namespaces, which defeats nested-launch detection (Aggressive and Moderate, #766 follow-up)
items.body:
Found by the independent review of the #766 fix (Moderate nested launches), round 3.

**What:** on Linux, agent commands can create new user namespaces. Nothing denies `CLONE_NEWUSER`: there is no seccomp rule for it in `linux-sandbox/src/landlock.rs`, and bubblewrap runs without `--disable-userns`. Inside its own user namespace (`unshare -Ur …`) a process is root for files owned by the mapped user, so the `--perms 000` placeholders bubblewrap uses for denied files (owned by that user) can be opened, and with `unshare -Urm` it can mount over paths it sees.

**Effect on nested-launch detection (both protected levels):**
- Aggressive: `sandboxed_away_from` (`security-level/src/nested.rs`) probes the vault store; inside such a namespace the probe can succeed, so a nested `corbanu exec` may not be recognised as nested.
- Moderate (#766): the Moderate marker is denied with the same kind of placeholder, so `unshare -Ur corbanu exec …` pointed at another Corbanu home runs at that home's level (as before #766). With `unshare -Urm` an agent command could also mount a file over a default home's runtime folder.

The review found no way to relax a refusal with this (main's Aggressive check is defeated the same way), so it is no weaker than before #766, but it misses the owner's goal on Linux. The outer sandbox still applies to everything such a process does (Landlock/seccomp/bubblewrap mounts of the outer command).

**Options:**
- (a) Deny new user namespaces to agent commands under protected levels (bubblewrap `--disable-userns`, or a seccomp rule for `unshare`/`clone` with `CLONE_NEWUSER`). Check what breaks (tools that use user namespaces themselves, nested sandboxes).
- (b) Accept and document as a Linux limit of nested-launch detection.

Recommendation: (a), behind a test on glitch.

items.title: sys: on Linux, delete_tree enters no mounted file system
items.body:
### Problem
- `bun install`, `bun remove` and `bun patch` delete the files of a volume mounted on or in a package folder. `Dir::delete_tree` (`src/sys/dir.rs:128`) empties the mount, then fails with `EBUSY` at its `rmdir`.
- Of 18 routes, main deletes the host's files in 16 (volume in a package) and 10 (volume on the folder). bun 1.4.2: 7 and 4. #44968, unreleased, added most.

### Fix
- On Linux, `delete_tree` opens its directory, and each one below, from the parent with `openat2(RESOLVE_NO_XDEV)`. A mount point answers `EXDEV`: the result is `EBUSY` as before, with nothing in it deleted.
- Without `openat2` (kernel before 5.6, seccomp, Android), `rmdir` is asked first. Only a directory with entries is opened.
- Verified: `test/cli/install/mounted-volume.test.ts` (30 rows on real mounts, 0 of 28 pass on main). Both matrices: 0 of 18.

### Background
- A mount point is a directory with another file system on it (a volume, a bind mount). `RESOLVE_NO_XDEV` makes `openat2` refuse to cross one.
- #44968's review set the rule: "A mount point is left alone with its content". No user reported this.
- Considered a check in `move_aside`'s `EXDEV` arm: 3 of 16 routes, collides with #45572.

### Downsides
- The walk stops at the mount point, as before. What it did not reach stays. A linker writes the new copy into a folder that stays.
- `bun pm cache rm` keeps a volume mounted on a cache entry such as `<cache>/links`. Exit code 1, as before.
- Release text +2,048 B. Per deleted directory: same syscalls, +39 user instructions. macOS, FreeBSD, Windows: unchanged.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

**Where the rule comes from.** https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/44968#discussion_r4241280415, the test "a mount point stays, ..." in `isolated-install.test.ts`, and the comment on `move_aside` ("what is in a mount point (EBUSY) is not bun's to delete"). This PR puts that rule into the one walker that every package-manager delete uses. It was found in a self-review of another draft, not by a user. It also changes released behaviour (1.3.13 and 1.4.2 delete in some routes). That is safe for callers: a walk that crossed a mount never returned `Ok`, it ended with `EBUSY` at the same entry.

**Repro** (Linux, needs `unshare` with user namespaces):

```sh
mkdir -p app/dep volume && cd app && touch ../volume/host.js
echo '{"name":"dep","version":"1.0.0"}' > dep/package.json
echo '{"name":"app","dependencies":{"dep":"file:./dep"}}' > package.json
bun install --linker hoisted
unshare -Urm sh -c 'mkdir node_modules/dep/vol && mount -o bind ../volume node_modules/dep/vol && bun install --linker hoisted --force'
ls ../volume   # 1.4.2 and main: empty. This branch: host.js
```

**The two matrices.** 9 commands, each on a plain directory and on an overlay lower layer (a package of an image layer): With the hoisted linker: another version, `--force`, a failing postinstall, the dependency dropped, `bun remove`, `--linker isolated`. With the isolated linker: another version, `--force`, `--linker hoisted`. The number is the count of rows that delete the host's file.

| Volume mounted | 1.3.13 | 1.4.2 | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| in a package, at `node_modules/<pkg>/vol` | 6 | 7 | 16 | 0 |
| on the package folder, `node_modules/<pkg>` | 3 | 4 | 10 | 0 |

Exit codes and messages are the same on main and on this branch in all 36 rows. npm 11.16 keeps the files in both layouts. It does so through Node's async `fs.promises.rm`, which asks `rmdir` before it opens a directory. Node's `fs.rmSync` and GNU `rm -rf` do enter a mount.

**Route, call line, test row.**

| Route | `delete_tree` call | Row |
|---|---|---|
| hoisted, another version | `PackageInstall.rs:1101` (the name it was moved to) | hoisted on a directory, another version |
| hoisted, a failing script | `PackageInstall.rs:1041`, `PackageInstaller.rs:531`, `:538` | a script that fails (directory, overlay, on the folder) |
| hoisted, package of an image layer | `PackageInstall.rs:2127` (in place, after `EXDEV`) | hoisted on an overlay, another version |
| dependency dropped, `bun remove` | `prune.rs:2637`, `updatePackageJSONAndInstall.rs:534` | the dependency is dropped, bun remove (also scoped, also on the folder) |
| linker switch | `isolated_install.rs:1650`, `Symlinker.rs:141`, `prune.rs:3112` | `--linker isolated`, `--linker hoisted` (directory, overlay) |
| isolated `--force` | `isolated_install/Installer.rs:746` | isolated `--force` (directory, overlay, global store, on the folder) |
| `file:` folder installed again | `prune.rs:2917` | a file: dependency is installed again |
| `bun patch <pkg>` | `patchPackage.rs:1334` | bun patch |
| `bun pm cache rm` | `Dir::delete_children` | bun pm cache rm empties a volume at the cache directory, and not one on an entry of it |

**All callers get the rule.** `Dir::delete_tree` has 72 call lines: 51 in `src/install`, the rest in `bun upgrade`, `bun link`, `bun unlink`, `bun pm cache`, the standalone compile and helpers in `src/sys`. No JS API and no shell builtin uses it. A caller that wants to empty a directory that is a mount point opens it and calls `Dir::delete_children`, as `bun pm cache rm` does for the cache directory.

**What this PR does not change.**
- A linker writes the new copy into a folder that stays. That is the case for a package of an image layer (linked in place after `EXDEV`) and for a package folder that is the mount point. With the volume over a directory that the package ships, the host's file of the same name is replaced in 4 of 18 rows (main: files deleted or replaced in 16). No file is deleted in those 4.
- `remove_placed_package` deletes `package.json` and `.bun-tag` through a handle of its own (`PackageInstaller.rs:535`). After a failing postinstall, a package folder that is a volume loses its `package.json`. The test row records that.
- Code that opens a package directory itself does not pass through `delete_tree`: the `file:` re-sync where the volume covers a directory that the source folder has (`prune.rs:2921`), `lay_links_below` (`PackageInstall.rs:634`), and the mover of `bun patch` (`patchPackage.rs:1427`). These need a mount test that is not tied to a delete. #45572 adds one (`sys::is_mount_point`), so that is a follow-up.
- `node:fs` `rm` and the shell's `rm -rf` are separate walkers and still enter a mount.
- On a plain directory the rename aside moves the mount with the folder: the volume ends at `node_modules/.old-<hex>/...` with its files (npm: `.<pkg>-XXXX/...`).
- `error: failed to remove node_modules/<pkg>: EBUSY` prints once, with exit code 0, when the folder of a dropped package holds or is a mount point. Main prints the same line. A second `bun install` prints nothing (the rows check both).

**Limits of the path without `openat2`.** `rmdir` is the test there. Linux looks for a mount after the permission checks and before it looks for entries. `EBUSY` ends the walk at that entry, and "has entries" opens it. Any other refusal is not an answer about a mount: a parent that is not writable says `EACCES` before the mount test, and sshfs says `EPERM` for a directory that has entries. For those, `statx` says whether the entry is the root of a mount (`STATX_ATTR_MOUNT_ROOT`, Linux 5.8). If it is, the walk ends with `EBUSY`, the same error as with `openat2`. Before 5.8 the walk compares `st_dev`, which does not see a bind mount of the same file system. A kernel whose `rmdir` looks for entries before it looks for a mount is not covered (not measured). A seccomp policy that kills on `openat2` and is not taken for Android's (#39060) now kills bun in the delete walk as well. Before, it did so in bin linking, which already calls `openat2`.

**Other platforms.** macOS and FreeBSD run the same walk with `openat` and are not changed. They have no `openat2`, and an `rmdir` before each open would be a cost to every delete. Nothing was measured off Linux.

**Cost, measured on release builds of the merge base (017b2439a7) and this branch at ec4576f8da.** The later commits add code only on the path without `openat2` and on the retry after `ENOTEMPTY`, and were not measured again.
- `size`: text 106,738,870 to 106,740,918 (+2,048 B), data and bss equal.
- Syscalls (ptrace counter) for one hoisted package of 20 directories and 60 files that is replaced: 577 and 577. 21 `openat` become 21 `openat2`. Without `openat2`: +21 `unlinkat`.
- A `delete_tree` call whose path has more than one component (the isolated linker) costs one `openat(O_PATH)` of the parent and one `close` more, per call.
- `instructions:u` (perf_event_open, 10 interleaved runs) for a package of 200 directories: median 1,938,542 to 1,946,284 (+7,742, +0.40 %). Base against base differs by 425.

**Open PRs that touch the same code.**
- #45572 rewrites `move_aside` and adds `empty_in_place`, which calls `Dir::delete_children`. With this PR that remover stays out of a volume below the folder it empties. A volume on that folder is its own to test.
- #45347 edits two other hunks of `delete_tree` and `delete_children`. No reader name is added here.
- #41750 edits the `openat2` availability check in `src/sys/lib.rs`, which this PR moves into `openat2_if_available`.
- The keep-going delete for overlays that take no overlay xattrs is not here. It belongs in the in-place remover of #45572.

**Self-review.** 33 concerns raised, 26 addressed. 7 are stated above as limits and left for a follow-up: a mount test for the walkers that open a package directory themselves (4), a mount-identity check after the fallback's open, todo rows for the in-place linkers, and a tracking issue for `node:fs` `rm`.

**Tests.** `mounted-volume.test.ts`: 30 pass here. 28 of them were run on a build of main, where none passes. The other 2 pin the `EBUSY` line for a mount point in a parent that is not writable. `bun-install-android-seccomp.test.ts`: 4 pass here, the mount row fails on main. Both run bun under the existing Android seccomp helper (now in `android-seccomp.ts`) for the rows without `openat2`, so a call to `openat2` kills the row. One row there preloads a shim that makes `rmdir` say `EPERM` for a directory with entries, as sshfs does. It fails when any refusal ends the walk. The mount rows are skipped where `unshare -Urm` does not work, and the two rows that drop `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE` are skipped where `setpriv` has no `--bounding-set` (BusyBox). The rows are in a file of their own because they need their own probes (user namespace, overlay, `setpriv`, the seccomp helper) and a registry, and because `isolated-install.test.ts` already has about 300 tests that run at once. Also run on a debug build: `isolated-install`, `bun-install-staging`, `bun-prune`, `bun-remove`, `bun-link`, `bun-install-patch`, `bun-install-backends`, `bun-workspaces`, `bun-install-cache-publish`, `bun-pm`, `bun-pm-cache-pack`, `isolated-relink`, `bun-patch`, `bun-upgrade` (no failed assertion, and this machine times out some 5 s tests on main as well), the source lints, `cargo clippy -p bun_sys` and `bun run rust:check-all` (12 targets).

</details>

<!-- robobun:evidence:begin -->

---

**no test proof** · iteration 0 · platform-specific test(s) that do not run on this machine, deferring to CI, which covers all platforms: test/cli/install/mounted-volume.test.ts, test/cli/install/bun-install-android-seccomp.test.ts

<!-- robobun:evidence:end -->

items.title: Desktop: kept-offline files stay open after the network has been down

labels.name: needs-coordinator
labels.description: touches a path outside the arm allowlist: the coordinator reviews and arms it

items.body:
## Summary
Kept-offline files stayed open only for five seconds after the network dropped, because rclone re-lists when `--dir-cache-time` expires and has no stale-on-error (rclone#1963). The mount now caches listings for 24h, and the fill loop calls `vfs/refresh` only while storage answers, including kept and recently-opened folders.

## Verification
Four passes on this branch. Pass 1 ran on `799bc36`; pass 2 re-merged `origin/main` and re-proved on `287480b`; pass 3 merged the newer `origin/main` (Rewind/undo and the fill read deadline, drive#742) and re-proved on the current PR head `6f18b99`. Pass 4 merged `origin/main` again after it moved once more, then GitHub accepted this PR into its merge queue, which locked the branch, so that last merge is local-only and covers none of this diff's files.

### Pass 3 — final PR head `6f18b99` (this head is what the merge queue tests)

- `gofmt -l cmd` → empty; `go build ./...`, `go vet ./cmd/drive/` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./cmd/...` → exit 0.
- `unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -count=1 -race -short -timeout 900s`
  ```
  ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	114.412s
  ```
- `unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -count=1 -run TestStandinOfflineProof -v -timeout 15m`
  ```
  --- PASS: TestStandinOfflineProof (316.37s)
  ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	316.376s
  ```
  This is the issue's finish line: the test waits 5m2s after cutting the stand-in, then lists, creates and opens in the kept folder (`cmd/drive/offline_e2e_test.go`). It skips in `-short` mode, so CI's `-short` race suite pays no 5-minute floor.
- `go test ./cmd/drive/ -run 'TestVfsRefresh|TestVFSDirCache|TestFill|TestRefreshDirs|TestConflictGuard|TestVFSArgs|TestMountRC|TestPickRCAddr|TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSaves|TestReadCtxChunked'` → `ok 17.251s`.
- `node --test test/two-mount-sync.test.mjs test/own-words.test.mjs test/docs.test.mjs` → 42 pass, 0 fail (after `npm run docs:build`); `npx biome check test/two-mount-sync.test.mjs` → clean.
- `semgrep --config p/default --baseline-commit "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)" --quiet --metrics=off` → exit 0.

### Pass 4 — local-only merge of the newer `origin/main` (#706, FTS5 search)

`origin/main` moved again after pass 3. I merged it (clean auto-merge, no conflict), and it changed none of this diff's files (`git diff --name-only 6f18b99~ 6f18b99` and the merge's own file list contain no fill/conflict/config/offline/vfs/mount file), so the pass-3 Go evidence stands. The re-run was: `-race -short` ok (103.933s), `TestStandinOfflineProof` PASS (326.44s), the same targeted tests ok (18.813s), `node --test` 44 pass, semgrep exit 0. That merge could not be pushed: `git push` was rejected with `GH006 ... A pull request for this branch has been added to a merge queue. Branches that are queued for merging cannot be updated.` So this PR's head stays at `6f18b99`, which carries every authored change in this branch; the local tree was reset to it.

### Passes 1 and 2 (earlier heads)

Pass 2 (`287480b`, after merging `origin/main` once):

- `unshare -Urm go test -race ./cmd/drive/ -short -count=1` → `ok 99.293s`
- `unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -run TestStandinOfflineProof -v -count=1 -timeout 15m` → `--- PASS: TestStandinOfflineProof (316.39s)`
- `unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -run TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSaves -v -count=1 -timeout 300s` → PASS 6.31s
- `npm test` (typecheck, Biome, docs build, full JS suite, search proof) → exit 0
- `gofmt -l cmd` → empty; `node --test test/docs.test.mjs test/own-words.test.mjs` → 38 pass, 0 fail.

Pass 1 (`799bc36`):

- `unshare -Urm go test -race ./cmd/drive/ -short -count=1` → `ok 99.085s`
- `unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -short -count=1` → `ok 69.047s`
- `unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -run TestStandinOfflineProof -v -count=1 -timeout 15m` → `--- PASS: TestStandinOfflineProof (316.48s)`
- `unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -run TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSaves -v -count=1 -timeout 300s` → PASS 6.09s
- `unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -run 'TestRefreshDirs|TestFill|TestVfsRefresh|TestVFSDirCache|TestVFSArgsPins|TestMountRC|TestPickRCAddr' -count=1` → `ok 12.093s`
- `node --test test/two-mount-sync.test.mjs` → 4 pass, 0 fail (A→B 5.2s, B→A 5.1s: a 24h cache cannot see the other machine's save without the refresh, so the 5s propagation is the refresh working)
- Full JS suite (search proofs excluded from concurrency, then run once) → 1807 pass, 0 fail; `npm run check` exit 0; semgrep exit 0.

## Acceptance
1. The directory cache is long (five minutes or more) and freshness is driven by `vfs/refresh` over the rc from the fill loop.
   - `vfsDirCacheTimeValue = "24h"` at `cmd/drive/config.go`.
   - `fillPass` probes storage with `reachable` (a non-cached `operations/list`) and, only when it answers, refreshes the root and `listingDirs` (kept folders and parents of recently-opened files). A dead backend is left alone because rclone forces the cache stale before it re-lists.
   - Tests: `TestVFSDirCacheTimeIsAtLeastFiveMinutes`, `TestFillRefreshesRootWhenNothingOpened`, `TestFillRefreshesAKeptOfflineFolder`, `TestFillSkipsRefreshWhenStorageIsDownAndStillKeepWarms`, `TestFillSkipsRecentOpensWhenStorageIsDown`, `TestFillFillsRecentOpensWhenStorageAnswers`.
2. The e2e test waits more than five minutes after cutting the network, then opens, lists and creates a file in the kept folder.
   - `TestStandinOfflineProof` PASS 316.37s, output above.
3. A `vfs/refresh` reply is only success with a result object, and the probe's blind window is tested, not just named.
   - `vfsRefreshReplyError` (`cmd/drive/fill_run.go`) returns a named error for a reply with no `result`, or a null result, instead of reading it as OK.
   - `TestFillRefreshFailureIsNamed` and `TestConflictGuardNamesTheRefreshFailureAfterAClaim` prove the store can answer the probe and then fail the refresh: the pass names it with the backend's own message, does not report a refreshed cache, does not half-refresh the named folders, and still lands the conflict copy.

## Review findings, rounds 1 and 2

### Round 1: named directories
The in-run reviewer called the `dir2` parameter key invented and asked for one call per directory. rclone v1.75.1 documents the opposite (`vfs/rc.go`: "Any parameter key starting with dir will refresh that directory, e.g. `rclone rc vfs/refresh dir=home/junk dir2=data/misc`"). `TestRefreshDirsAsksForEveryFolderInOneRequest` now proves the keyword names on the wire: the real `rcClient.call` goes through the rclone shim and the test reads the forwarded form, which carries `dir=photos` and `dir2=photos/2026` in one request. `TestRefreshDirsSurfacesTheSecondFoldersFailure` proves the second folder's error is not swallowed.

### Round 2
Fixed:
- The missing `result` case of `vfsRefreshReplyError` returned nil (success). A changed remote-control shape would have hidden a failed refresh behind a 24h-stale listing. Now a named error, with the case added to `TestVfsRefreshReplyError`.
- The reviewer's Critical (the probe→refresh race is a TOCTOU that stock rclone cannot close) and its companion Warning asked for the untested half: a failure *after* a passing probe. Two tests now cover it (`TestFillRefreshFailureIsNamed`, `TestConflictGuardNamesTheRefreshFailureAfterAClaim`): named error, no refreshed-cache claim, no half-refresh, conflict copy still lands, next pass's probe/refresh is the recovery.

Adjudicated, unchanged:
- *Probe failure silent.* A down backend is the expected state while offline, and the mount log is customer-facing; a line per ~10s pass is noise. The pass's own unexpected failures already surface on the loop's `errs` channel, and `drive doctor` reads rclone's backend log for link health.
- *`namedDirNotFound` substring matching.* rclone is pinned to v1.75.1 (`PINNED_RCLONE_VERSION`), and the accepted family (`not found`, `not a directory`, `is a file`) is exactly what rclone itself treats as a tolerant named-dir result; anything else is returned. A wire-level pin against the pinned binary is a follow-up, not a rename risk on this PR.
- *Root refresh each pass reverses drive#568's minimization.* Intentional and required by #541's acceptance (freshness driven by the fill loop's `vfs/refresh`); it is non-recursive, one directory.
- *`refreshDirs` has no folder cap.* A kept set with hundreds of parent folders is not a measured case; the call is bounded by the kept set the user chose, and `listingDirs` already de-duplicates and sorts.
- *5-minute sleep floor.* Already skips in `-short` mode (`cmd/drive/offline_e2e_test.go`), so the unit suite is unaffected and only the full proof pays it.

## In-run review
`in-run review: litellm/worker-capable; 2 findings fixed` (the missing-`result` OK and the untested probe→refresh failure path; the round-2 items above are the full adjudication).

## Scope
- `cmd/drive/fill_run.go` — the fill loop must skip `vfs/refresh` when storage is down, refresh kept/nested listings while it is up, and never read a reply without a result as OK.
- `cmd/drive/fill_test.go`, `cmd/drive/rc_test.go` — reachability, nested-folder refresh, the multi-directory rc request, the named refresh failure, and rclone's 24h dir-cache minimum.
- `cmd/drive/conflict_guard.go`, `cmd/drive/conflict_test.go`, `cmd/drive/conflict_e2e_test.go` — the conflict guard's refresh shares the down-storage rule and names a failure after a passing probe.
- `cmd/drive/config_test.go`, `cmd/drive/prefetch_test.go`, `cmd/drive/windows_test.go` — mount plans pin `--dir-cache-time` to the constant.
- `cmd/drive/offline_e2e_test.go` — the #541 proof.
- `docs/build-spec.md`, `docs-site/how-it-works.md`, `docs-site/changelog.md` — spec and docs match the product.
- `test/two-mount-sync.test.mjs` — the proof pins the spec's `--dir-cache-time` and drives the refresh.

Closes #541

items.title: [Bug]: Steam Space fails its sandbox requirements under Docker AppArmor on Ubuntu 24.04 (1.4.11)
items.body:
## Investigation disclosure

The technical investigation, source analysis, local patch, and test results below were produced by an AI coding assistant working on my machine with my authorization. I am passing along its findings, not claiming to have independently verified the source-level conclusions. I have no further contributions to add beyond this report and am not committing to further investigation or a pull request. Please treat the proposed diagnosis and fix as material for independent review.

## Describe the bug

A configured Steam Space displays a first-run error saying user namespaces must be enabled, although they are enabled on the host and a basic user namespace works inside the worker. The failing operation is a sandbox mount/root-propagation operation blocked under the worker's `docker-default` AppArmor confinement.

Polaris 1.4.11 supplies a Steam seccomp policy but, in the inspected release, no dedicated Steam AppArmor selection mechanism. On this Ubuntu host, simply changing AppArmor to `unconfined` is not a complete solution either.

## Environment

- Original installation: official Polaris **1.4.11** Ubuntu DEB, after downgrade from 1.4.13.
- Inspected base source: `v1.4.11`, commit `9b2020f4315cafde8f59944a0099ee5a0befed7e`.
- Host: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, x86-64; Docker Engine 29.6.1; AppArmor enabled.
- GPUs: 2 × NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition; driver 615.71.09; AMD Raphael iGPU also present.
- Driver-pinned Steam runtime: `steam-nvidia-cb1dd831b125de6c`.
- Client: Android Moonlight (exact app/device version not recorded).
- Runtime path: configured containerized Steam Space in the headless streaming setup, not the ordinary native Steam tile.
- Worker: UID/GID 1000, all outer capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, read-only root, exact packaged Steam seccomp policy, `docker-default` AppArmor.
- These are historical findings from the version above; a fresh reproduction on the latest public release has not been performed for this report.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On the described Ubuntu/AppArmor host, keep host user namespaces enabled and Ubuntu's unprivileged-userns restriction enabled.
2. Configure and launch a Steam Space using the driver-pinned runtime and upstream 1.4.11 Docker security configuration.
3. Accept Steam's first-run installer dialog.
4. Observe the generic namespace requirements error; compare a basic user namespace with a user-plus-mount namespace or minimal Bubblewrap sandbox inside the worker.

Expected: Steam can create its nested sandbox without disabling host-wide security protections or making the outer container privileged. If prerequisites are missing, setup should identify the actual AppArmor limitation.

Actual: first-run fails with a misleading namespace-enablement message.

## Relevant diagnostics

Recorded host settings:

```text
kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone = 1
kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1
user.max_user_namespaces = nonzero
```

Inside the original worker:

```text
unshare -Ur true
# succeeds

unshare -Urm true
# fails changing root filesystem propagation: Permission denied

bwrap --ro-bind / / --unshare-user --uid 0 --gid 0 /bin/true
# Failed to make / slave: Permission denied
```

The packaged Steam seccomp policy already permits the relevant user-namespace and mount operations. Editing it in place is not a solution: Polaris verifies the packaged policy hash.

## AI investigation and controlled tests

Disposable, resource-limited containers used the same Steam image, exact packaged seccomp policy, UID/GID 1000, zero outer capabilities, no-new-privileges, read-only root, no network, and no GPU/host-data mounts. Temporary explicit-profile probes had anonymous scratch tmpfs.

| AppArmor configuration | Recorded result |
|---|---|
| `docker-default` | User-plus-mount namespace denied at root propagation |
| `unconfined` | Denied writing `uid_map` under Ubuntu's unprivileged-userns restriction |
| Temporary explicit profile allowing user namespaces and sandbox mount operations | User-plus-mount namespace and minimal Bubblewrap both pass |

The temporary diagnostic policy was unloaded after testing; it was not used as a production policy.

A subsequent local, opt-in implementation selected a fixed enforced `polaris-steam` profile only for Docker Steam media workers. Recorded comparisons with that candidate policy:

| Check | `docker-default` | Candidate `polaris-steam` |
|---|---|---|
| User-plus-mount namespace | Exit 1 | Exit 0 |
| Minimal Bubblewrap | Exit 1 | Exit 0 |
| Installed `steam-runtime-check-requirements`, Steam volume read-only | Exit 71 | Exit 0 |
| Outer mount namespace without a new user namespace | Denied | Still denied |

The candidate probe retained `CapEff: 0000000000000000`, `NoNewPrivs: 1`, and enforced AppArmor. Host namespace restrictions stayed enabled. The recorded multiseat suite passed 315 tests including three new tests; a broader platform suite was not fully passing and is not claimed clean.

## Requested outcome and security boundary

Please provide a supported, narrowly scoped AppArmor integration or an actionable prerequisite error for Steam Spaces on Ubuntu. The local proof of concept used a fixed opt-in profile, checked both requested and effective confinement for recovery, and failed launch if the profile was missing rather than falling back to unconfined.

Allowing nested sandbox mounts exposes additional kernel mount code and requires security review. Please do not resolve this by globally disabling AppArmor/userns restrictions, weakening Docker defaults for unrelated containers, disabling seccomp, or adding outer `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`/privileged mode.

The operator subsequently confirmed Steam worked after the local AppArmor change. Passing requirements and that confirmation are not a complete gameplay/controller/streaming acceptance test. The active setup later migrated to native Steam; this report concerns the original containerized failure, not native Steam's AppArmor profile.

Source-only policy, patch, and regression helpers are retained locally but are not attached to this issue body. No private configuration, raw logs, or account data are included.

items.title: pm cache prune: rmdir only what the walk left empty, keep index links whose package is cached
items.body:
### Problem
- `bun pm cache prune` prints `EROFS: Read-only file system: Could not delete @scope/ (unlink)` for each scope and index directory of a read-only cache, and exits 1. One scope directory that root made gives the same with `EACCES: Permission denied`.
- `Prune::remove_if_empty` (`src/runtime/cli/pm_cache_prune_command.rs:141`) called `rmdir` on each and read ENOTEMPTY as "keep". The kernel answers EROFS or EACCES before it looks inside.
- Index links are absolute. In a cache at another path (a container volume) each one looks dangling.

### Fix
- The walk counts what it leaves in each directory and calls `rmdir` only at 0. An empty directory that cannot be removed is still an error.
- An index link is removed only when its package is not in the cache. ENOENT from an open, an unlink or `rmdir` means gone.
- Verified on Linux x64: `test/cli/install/bun-pm.test.ts`, 29 new tests, 22 fail on canary 1.4.4-canary.1+963452075.
- Self-reviewed: 24 concerns raised, 18 addressed, 5 in part. Rejected: silent index clean-up, which hides a real failure.

### Background
- The cache holds packages (`name@version@@@1`), scope directories (`@scope/`) and index directories (`name/`, a symlink for each cached version).
- Considered a second listing after a failed `rmdir` (GNU `rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty`). It keeps one failing `rmdir` for each kept directory.

### Downsides
- A directory that another process empties after the walk read it stays until the next prune.
- Where access times are recorded, a package that cannot be deleted is an error in the first run only.
- Release `.text`: +1,280 bytes. A 200-package cache: 210 fewer syscalls for each run.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

No issue reports this. `bun pm cache prune` is in no release: no tag contains #44968, which added it. The read-only mount work of #45694 found it, and that PR names this case as a different fix.

**What changes, for a port**

| | main | this PR | lines that fix it | tests that fail on main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. A directory that the prune keeps, where bun may not remove directories | `Could not delete <dir>`, `N failed`, exit 1 | no `rmdir`, no message | the two `emptied && self.remove_empty(..)` gates in `prune_dir`, and the `bool` results that feed them | 6 read-only mount cells, 10 permission cells |
| B. A cache that is not at the path where it was filled | read-only: one line for each link and one for each directory. Writable: every index link and index directory is deleted | the links stay, no message | `is_index_link_package_in_cache` and its call in `remove_dangling_links` | 2 `not at the path where it was filled` cells, the `bun install` test |
| C. An entry that is gone when the prune reaches it | `Could not open` or `Could not delete`, exit 1 | counted as gone | the ENOENT arms at the scope open, the index open and the link unlink | 3 cells of `another process changes a directory` |

A works without C, but then a directory whose last entry another process removed stays until the next run.

**Repro** (Linux x64, kernel 6.1.155, release builds of main ea6a2c7b7c and of this branch, built in the same directory)

```sh
export C=/tmp/p/cache BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/p/cache
mkdir -p $C/new-pkg@2.0.0@@@1 $C/new-pkg $C/@scope/new-scoped@1.0.0@@@1 $C/@scope/new-scoped
ln -s $C/new-pkg@2.0.0@@@1 $C/new-pkg/2.0.0@@@1
ln -s $C/@scope/new-scoped@1.0.0@@@1 $C/@scope/new-scoped/1.0.0@@@1
unshare -Urm sh -c 'mount -o bind $C $C && mount -o remount,bind,ro $C && bun pm cache prune'
```

| Cache, nothing old in it | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| writable | `Done! Checked 2 packages`, exit 0 | the same |
| read-only bind mount | 3 `EROFS ... Could not delete` lines, `3 failed`, exit 1 | `Done!`, exit 0 |
| cache root mode 555, other user | 2 `EACCES` lines, exit 1 | `Done!`, exit 0 |
| the user's own cache, `@scope` made by root | `EACCES ... Could not delete @scope/new-scoped`, `1 failed`, exit 1 | `Done!`, exit 0 |
| read-only, one more empty index directory | 4 lines, exit 1 | `EROFS ... Could not delete gone-pkg`, `1 failed`, exit 1 |
| read-only, 200 packages, at another path | 410 lines, exit 1 | `Done!`, exit 0 |
| writable, 200 packages, at another path | 200 of 200 index links deleted | 200 of 200 kept |

`rmdir(2)` on Linux: `do_rmdir` asks for write access to the mount before it looks up the name (EROFS). `vfs_rmdir` checks the permission on the parent (EACCES, EPERM) and for a mount point (EBUSY) before the file system looks at the entries (ENOTEMPTY). The gate reads no errno, so the tests use EROFS and EACCES for the class.

**Where `rmdir` runs now**

| Directory | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| kept, has an entry | `rmdir`, ENOTEMPTY | no `rmdir` |
| emptied by this run, or already empty | `rmdir` | `rmdir` |
| dry run | no `rmdir` | no `rmdir`: `prune_dir` returns false. The `if !self.dry_run` guard is gone |
| its listing failed | `Could not read`, then `rmdir` | `Could not read`, no `rmdir` |

**ENOENT means gone** at five system calls: the `lstat` of a package and the `rmdir` (as before), and now also the open of a scope directory, the open of an index directory and the unlink of an index link. It does not at `getdents64`: a directory that is removed while the prune reads it still gives `Could not read`, in `read_entries` and in `Dir::delete_tree`. So two prunes at the same time can still exit 1. #45347 ends such a listing.

**Index links.** `ExtractTarball::extract` and `cache_pack::unpack` write the link `<name>/<link>` with the absolute path of the package as target. `<link>` is the folder name less `<name>@` (npm) or `@GH@` (GitHub), or the whole folder name (tarball). The new function looks for those three folders by name. ENOENT and ENAMETOOLONG mean that the folder is not there: `<name>@<link>` of a GitHub or tarball link can be longer than a file name. Any other answer keeps the link. The function runs only for a link whose target is missing, so a cache at its fill path pays nothing. The `bun install` test installs an npm package, a scoped npm package, a GitHub package and a tarball, renames the cache, and expects all four links after a prune.

**The `rmdir` after a failed unlink** of an index link is now Windows only, where a link can be a directory junction. `src/install/prune.rs` `remove_link` does the same. On POSIX an `rmdir` of a symlink cannot succeed, so the fallback could only replace the errno of the unlink.

**Tests** (`bun-pm.test.ts`, under `bun pm cache prune`)

- `a cache that cannot be written to`: 8 cells on a read-only bind mount and 12 cells as a user without write permission (mode 555). The mount cells need `unshare -Urm`. `canMount()` in `test/harness.ts` is the same hunk as in #45694, so the two merge in either order. The permission cells run on every POSIX system and need no mount.
- `another process changes a directory after the prune read it`: 6 cells. An `LD_PRELOAD` library removes or adds one entry at the end of one directory listing. Linux with a C compiler.
- Two writable tests, and one test with a real `bun install`.
- 22 of the 29 fail on the unfixed canary. The other 7 guard clauses that behave as main does:
  - the writable test and the two `--dry-run` cells: the dry run `return false` in `prune_dir`
  - `a package is removed before the prune checks it`: ENOENT from the `lstat`
  - `an empty index directory is removed before the prune removes it`: ENOENT from the `rmdir`
  - `an entry is added to an empty index directory`: the ENOTEMPTY arm, which no other test reaches now
  - `removes a dangling index link whose name does not fit in the name of a package`: ENAMETOOLONG from the lookup by name. It fails on the first commit of this PR
- Mutation check on a temporary build: 29 single changes to the count, the gates, the ENOENT arms and the three link names. 28 fail a test. The one that passes changes nothing: `prune_package` returns true in a dry run, where `prune_dir` returns false before it reads the count.
- On a debug build, some tests of this file time out at 5 s with and without this change (`bun pm ls lists what's on disk`).

**Measurements** (release builds of main ea6a2c7b7c and of this branch, same directory. `strace`, `perf` and `valgrind` are not on the build machine: a ptrace program counted the syscalls and the instructions)

- Writable cache, 200 fresh packages (200 index and 10 scope directories): `unlinkat(AT_REMOVEDIR)` 210 -> 0, all syscalls 1,646 -> 1,437. No other row of the table changes.
- The same cache on a read-only mount: `unlinkat` 210 (EROFS) -> 0, false `Could not delete` lines 210 -> 0, exit 1 -> 0. With one empty index directory: 1 failed.
- A copy of a real cache (1,391 packages, 69 scope and 1,188 index directories): `rmdir` attempts for each prune 1,257 -> 0, all syscalls 9,277 -> 8,018.
- Allocator calls for each prune of 200 fresh packages (gdb breakpoint hit counts): `mi_malloc` 1,484 -> 1,274, `mi_free` 1,308 -> 1,099. Each failed `rmdir` boxed its path.
- Instructions of the main thread in user mode for the same prune (single-step count, two runs each, alternated): 1,086,651 and 1,088,718 -> 1,063,468 and 1,060,050.
- A cache at another path, 200 packages, read-only: `unlinkat` 610 -> 0, `newfstatat` 401 -> 601 (one lookup by name for each link).
- Size: `.text` 81,695,461 -> 81,696,741 (+1,280). `.rodata`, `.data` and `.bss`: +0. `prune_dir` 3,928 -> 4,587, `remove_if_empty` 351 -> `remove_empty` 361, `exec` 2,544 -> 2,557, the new link function 594.
- A directory that another process empties after the prune listed it (the `LD_PRELOAD` library removes `new-pkg/2.0.0@@@1`): main prints `ENOENT ... Could not delete new-pkg/2.0.0@@@1`, exits 1 and removes `new-pkg` in the same run. This PR prints `Done!`, exits 0 and leaves the empty `new-pkg` for the next run.

**Not changed**

- On a cache that bun may not write to, an empty directory that another process fills or removes between the listing and the `rmdir` still gets one `Could not delete` line: EROFS and EACCES come before ENOTEMPTY and ENOENT. `removal_target_is_missing` of #45694 can close the ENOENT half.
- `prune_package` lists a package for its size before it deletes it, and the listing refreshes the access time. With the cache root at mode 555 and one old package, run 1 reports it and exits 1, and run 2 prints `Done! Checked 3 packages` and exits 0 with the package still there. On main run 2 exits 1, but only through the two false lines. On a read-only mount the access time cannot change: each run reports the package and exits 1 (main: the same line and 3 false ones).
- On a read-only mount a read does not refresh the age of a package. So `Done!` holds there only while every package is newer than `--max-age`.
- A prune that removes an empty `@scope/` can fail an install that has made the scope and has not yet renamed its package into it: `StagedEntry::publish` renames again and does not make the parent again (read in code, not run). main removes the same directories.
- Index clean-up failures stay errors. I found no reader of the index on main, so a maintainer can decide to make them silent or to retire the index.
- No tracking issue is filed for the items above.

**Not run**: Windows and macOS. `bun run rust:check-all` compiles `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `aarch64-apple-darwin`. On Windows 2 of the 29 new tests run: the writable test, which passes without the fix, and the `bun install` test. On macOS the 12 permission cells run too.

**Self-review**: 24 concerns. Addressed: the lookup by name for a cache at another path, ENOENT narrowed to five system calls, the cells for a partial removal and for a failure below a scope, the failure cells on every POSIX system, the compile of the C library inside its own `describe` with a 30 s limit, `canMount()` from the harness, no musl gate (bun-musl is dynamically linked), one-line comments, and the facts in these Notes. In part: 5 concerns ask for a tracking issue, and none is filed. Rejected: silent index clean-up, because an empty directory that cannot be removed must stay an error.

</details>

<!-- robobun:evidence:begin -->

---

**no test proof** · iteration 0 · platform-specific test(s) that do not run on this machine, deferring to CI, which covers all platforms: test/cli/install/bun-pm.test.ts

items.title: the onboarding script cannot complete keytocard as instructed, and leaves an unprotected export behind

labels.name: security
labels.description: Exposure, privilege or trust is affected

items.body:
## Observed

`yubikey-onboard.sh` tells the operator to run `gpg --edit-key ... keytocard` from a second terminal. From there the key is not found, the script only warns, and it finishes by shredding the master key and reporting success with an empty card. The subkeys export stays on the backup medium untouched. `--from-backup` cannot read the backup the default run leaves behind. A re-export truncates the only backup before gpg runs. Factory PINs survive a default run. A dry run writes the key's serial next to the public checkout. shellcheck never runs on the script in CI.

## Mechanism

The script re-executes under `unshare -Urm` and mounts `GNUPGHOME` on a ramfs that no other shell can see. `phase_age_backup` encrypts and shreds `master-secret.key` only. `--from-backup` accepts a plaintext file only. The re-export uses `>` on the target. Both PIN prompts default to no, and the PIV applet is never touched before `--generate`. The summary falls back to `$PWD`. Nothing builds `packages.yubikey-onboard`, which is where shellcheck runs.

## Fix shape

- Run `keytocard` from inside the script and make the key-on-card check a hard failure.
- Put the subkeys export through the same encrypt, verify and shred sequence.
- Accept and decrypt the `.age` backup, export to `.new` and move after verification.
- PIN changes default to yes, refuse factory PINs without `--allow-default-pins`, change PIV credentials first.
- Never write the summary to `$PWD`, write nothing on a dry run.
- Helpers before the parser, serial-less keys handled, prompted names reject newlines, the guide states what `shred` cannot promise on flash and CoW.

## Acceptance

- `checks.yubikey-onboard-builds` builds the package so shellcheck runs in CI.
- A dry run under `unshare -Urm` in a VM asserts the summary path.

items.title: test: cover exact-byte local response acceptance boundaries
items.body:
Ordinary response byte literals already decode exact bytes, but acceptance coverage did not pin the decoded-size boundary, transactional config rejection, or binary body framing through EOF.

Add tests for exactly 4,096 decoded bytes versus 4,097, invalid/truncated hex escapes, a separated `b` prefix, and the backward-compatible raw spelling of ordinary string bodies. Loader negatives start with a valid route and require no partial routes or response bodies to be published. Extend the JIT/real-socket witness to compare all 13 bytes containing LF, CR, tab, backslash, quote, NUL and 0xff, together with Content-Length and actual EOF. No compiler/runtime behavior changes.

Fixes #279 (RUT capability and acceptance coverage). This makes no nginx escape-semantics or converter support claim; any future converter use still needs its separate pinned nginx baseline.

Validation with Clang 22 Release/JIT:
- Full frontend: 1,076 tests, 17,658 checks passed.
- Full serve loader: 64 tests, 44,659 checks passed.
- Focused real-socket binary-body case: 1 test, 22 checks passed.
- Affected-file clang-format and `git diff --check` passed.

Tests that write temporary files ran with a private tmpfs via `unshare -Urm` because the host `/tmp` user quota is exhausted. Host networking was retained. Full integration and sanitizer suites were not rerun for this tests-only change; CI remains pending.

items.title: The installed mount runs drive mount --foreground, so the conflict guard, offline keep-warm and queue report fire at login

labels.name: needs-coordinator
labels.description: touches a path outside the arm allowlist: the coordinator reviews and arms it

items.body:
The login item now runs `drive mount --foreground` (systemd, launchd, Windows), so the conflict guard, the offline keep-warm and the queue report start at login. Agent-tool items stay stock rclone. `--rclone` carries the path this run already resolved, because a login item has no shell PATH.

This repo has AGENTS.md and no CLAUDE.md.

## What changed

- `cmd/drive/mount.go` `productArgs` is `mount --foreground --home … --rclone <resolved>`.
- `cmd/drive/mount.go` `productArgv` is this CLI for the device mount and rclone for an agent path (`EnvPath`).
- `cmd/drive/mount.go` launchd and systemd ExecStart follow that vector. Device systemd still has ExecStartPre to clear a dead FUSE entry. launchd still wraps with the NFS umount script, then execs the product.
- `cmd/drive/mount.go` `--foreground` returns before `startLoginItem`, so the item cannot register itself again.
- `cmd/drive/windows.go` the scheduled task Command/Arguments come from `productArgv`, so they cannot disagree.
- `cmd/drive/installed_mount_e2e_test.go` `drive init` writes the real unit, two devices keep both saves, and a pinned file stays readable after storage is stopped. The child env drops `DRIVE_S3_*`.
- `docs/scoreboard.md` offline-pinning row names the installed-unit proof and the wall clock this run measured.

Two commits on top of the merge came out of this run's own checks:

- `c464766` — `TestWindowsTaskXMLCarriesAWorkingDirectory`, main's drive#544 invariant, failed after merging main (it was added by #700, after this branch's last merge). The task action is now the product, so the vector no longer carries rclone's own `--config`/`--cache-dir`/`--log-file`: the product derives all three from the one `--home` it is handed. The test now asserts the same invariant on the vector that is written — the plan's three paths are what the product derives from that home, and no value on the action's command line is relative, because an action that starts in System32 cannot open a relative path.
- `203b506` — the offline-pinning row carried a 9.2 s figure dated 2026-10-06 that no run of mine produced. The table's own rule is that our side is never guessed, so the row now carries the 61.8 s this run measured, and says the number is the proof's run time rather than a speed figure, because the test reports no benchmark numbers.
- `ca36bb2` — three comments that misdescribed what is beneath them.

## Verification

Login item is the product, not rclone (systemd, launchd and Windows vectors):

```
$ go test ./cmd/drive -count=1 -timeout 60s -run 'TestProductArgs|TestLaunchdPlistRunsTheProduct|TestSystemdUnitRunsTheProduct|TestWindowsTaskCommandLine|TestWindowsTaskXMLCarriesThePlan|TestDevicePlanIsNotAnAgent' -v
--- PASS: TestDevicePlanIsNotAnAgent (0.00s)
--- PASS: TestProductArgsKeepsForegroundOnEveryPlatform (0.00s)
--- PASS: TestLaunchdPlistRunsTheProduct (0.00s)
--- PASS: TestSystemdUnitRunsTheProduct (0.00s)
--- PASS: TestWindowsTaskCommandLineCarriesThePlan (0.00s)
--- PASS: TestWindowsTaskXMLCarriesThePlan (0.00s)
PASS
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	0.058s
```

Installed-unit e2e (acceptance bullet 2: `drive init` writes the real unit, two devices, a conflict copy, a pinned file still cached after storage stops):

```
$ unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive -count=1 -timeout 180s -run 'TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSavesThroughTheInstalledUnit' -v
    installed_mount_e2e_test.go:177: installed unit: conflict=report (conflict, mac).txt, pinned file stayed cached after storage stopped
--- PASS: TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSavesThroughTheInstalledUnit (65.51s)
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	65.528s
```

The whole package, as CI runs it (this host needs `unshare -Urm` for the FUSE tests):

```
$ unshare -Urm go test -race ./cmd/drive/ -short
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	112.304s
```

CI's two non-short runs:

```
$ unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive -count=1 -run 'TestStandinMountProof' -timeout 300s -v
--- PASS: TestStandinMountProof (10.54s)
--- PASS: TestStandinMountProofStrayFile (5.68s)
--- PASS: TestStandinMountProofKillNineRecoversQueuedSave (6.09s)
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	22.335s

$ unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive -count=1 -run 'TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSaves' -timeout 300s -v
--- PASS: TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSaves (5.97s)
--- PASS: TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSavesThroughTheInstalledUnit (61.84s)
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	67.817s
```

Also run: `gofmt -l cmd` clean, `go vet ./cmd/...` clean, `GOOS=windows go vet ./cmd/...` clean, `GOOS=windows go test -c` compiles, `staticcheck 2025.1.1 ./cmd/...` clean, `go build ./...` clean.

`npm run check`: the host's default Node is 22, which `precheck` refuses, so it ran on Node 24.21.0 from `~/.nvm`. Exit 0. biome reports 17 warnings and 11 infos, none of which fail the check. `node --test test/scoreboard.test.mjs` (6 pass), `test/speed-ratchet.test.mjs` (7 pass, 2 skipped needing a Worker build), `test/docs.test.mjs` (32 pass after `npm run docs:build`), `test/benchmarks.test.mjs`, `test/docs-drift.test.mjs`, `test/evals.test.mjs`, `test/version-1-claims.test.mjs` and `test/installer.test.mjs` all pass. `node_modules/` and `public/docs` are gitignored; `git status --porcelain` is empty.

Diff-scoped semgrep against `origin/main`: exit 0, no findings.

in-run review: litellm/worker-capable against `docs/quality-bar.md`, exit 0, 6 findings. Acted on 3 in `ca36bb2` — the `withProductBin` comment that called the install paths something else, a three-sentence comment where one sentence would do, and the derivation switch that asserted `--config` by falling through a case. Dismissed with reasons: (a) `productArgv` builds this CLI's vector and `args` builds rclone's, so they cannot share a builder, and `isAgent` is one line on the only field that sets it; (b) the installed-unit e2e is acceptance bullet 2 written out, so narrowing it would break the finish line; (c) the Windows test calls the same exported path helpers the product calls, which checks the plan still agrees with the derivation rather than duplicating it.

CI on the merged head `84827f5` (ubuntu-latest):
- `go` job PASS (4m15s) — `-short` unit tests incl. `TestLogoutStopsALiveMount` live under `CI=true` (drive#501), the stand-in mount proof, the two-device conflict proof, plus gofmt/vet/staticcheck/goreleaser/Windows-cross-build.
- `verify` job PASS (7m44s) — `npm run check` + `npm test`.
- `arm` graceful-skipped (this repo has no NISHFLEET worker App secrets; its workflow note arms on the opener).
- `review-risky` dispatch errored on litellm auth (`FLEET_TASK_ID` not resolved in this env), posted no review, and is non-required (mergeStateStatus is UNSTABLE, not BLOCKED).

This run (2026-10-08) merged main again and re-proved on the merged head:

- Merge of `origin/main` (`#834`, `#855`, `#858`, `#860`) into `claim/issue-515` is clean; those commits touch only the Node side, so `cmd/drive/` is unchanged by the merges (`go build ./cmd/drive/` OK).
- Diff-scoped semgrep against `origin/main`: exit 0, no findings.
- The installed-unit proof re-ran green on the merged head:

```
$ unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive -count=1 -timeout 15m -run 'TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSavesThroughTheInstalledUnit' -v
```

items.title: fix(http): reject transfer encoding on HTTP/1.0 requests
items.body:
HTTP/1.0 requests carrying `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` passed the existing final-chunked admission check and could connect upstream. Reject all HTTP/1.0 transfer-encoded requests before routing, returning HTTP/1.0 400 with connection close. HTTP/1.1 transparent final-chunked forwarding keeps its existing behavior.

Extend the epoll/io_uring real-socket tests with an unsupported/ambiguous TE matrix. Every vector includes a possible pipelined successor and requires exact rejection bytes, EOF, zero upstream accepts, and settled connection ownership. Update the runtime contract and stale parser comments.

Refs #284. This addresses a remaining admission gap; it does not promote a converter compatibility row or claim nginx-equivalent 400/501 behavior across all unsupported codings.

Validation on Clang 22 Release/JIT:
- Before the fix, the real-socket HTTP/1.0 case connected upstream; the deterministic version-admission test also failed.
- Network request admission: 11 tests / 1,064 checks passed, including transparent final-chunked pipeline preservation.
- Full HTTP parser: 215 tests / 3,847 checks passed.
- Real-socket request framing and request-body upload regressions: 18 tests / 1,027 checks passed, including both live epoll and io_uring matrices.
- Affected-file clang-format and git diff checks passed.
- Separately probed the repository-pinned nginx 1.29.7 digest: HTTP/1.0 chunked returned 400 with EOF and no backend accept. Other ambiguous TE probes were rejected with 400 or 501; they are baseline observations, not a new paired converter differential.

items.title: Unconfine virt-launcher compute container AppArmor/seccomp for passt sandbox (COMP-4086)
items.body:
COMP-4086 (staging-supply passt pilot blocker, subtask of COMP-4082/COMP-4083)

## Problem

PasstBinding VMs crashloop on staging-supply: the `passt` child of QEMU exits
`Failed to remount /: Permission denied / Failed to sandbox process, exiting`
(libvirt SyncVMI failure; VMI stuck in Scheduled).

passt sandboxes itself before forwarding: unprivileged user namespace, then
remount of `/` inside a fresh mount namespace. The runtime default
confinement denies both barriers — seccomp gates `unshare(2)` behind
CAP_SYS_ADMIN, the default AppArmor profile (`cri-containerd.apparmor.d`)
denies `mount(2)`. Verified live in the compute container:
`/proc/self/attr/current = cri-containerd.apparmor.d (enforce)`, `Seccomp: 0`,
`CapEff: 0`; `unshare -U` succeeds, `unshare -Urm` + remount fails (exact
passt sandbox repro). Raising pod privileges does not help: passt drops root
before sandboxing, so it never holds CAP_SYS_ADMIN when it needs it.

Upstream: kubevirt/kubevirt#12333 (Ubuntu Noble + containerd),
kubev2v/forklift#8581 (same failure, same two independent barriers: "with
both profiles, passt completes its sandbox").

## Change

When the `PasstBinding` feature gate is enabled, the virt-controller now sets
`appArmorProfile: Unconfined` + `seccompProfile: Unconfined` on the
virt-launcher **compute** container (new `WithPasstSandboxPermissions()`
renderer option, wired in `newContainerSpecRenderer`). Explicit Unconfined
seccomp future-proofs against nodes that start enforcing seccomp.
Gate-off environments (dev/prod today) see no pod spec change.

## Tests

- `rendercontainer_test.go`: option sets both profiles; absent by default.
- Full services suite: 339/339 passing (337 pre-existing + 2 new).
- `gofmt` clean; `go build ./pkg/virt-controller/...` clean.

## Rollout

New image tag `v1.8.4-memlock-viommu1-apparmor` via the build-hive-images
workflow (build triggered from this branch); staging-supply-only ops image
bump follows (KubeVirt CR `imageTag` + virt-operator pin). Dev/prod unaffected
until the gate is enabled there.

Follow-ups (tracked in COMP-4086): tighten to Localhost seccomp/AppArmor
profiles for the production rollout; cherry-pick to the v1.9.1 line (COMP-3399).

items.title: test: reap forked controls across process-group changes
items.body:
Forked differential controls could leave zombie grandchildren behind: cleanup ignored zombies and signaled only the original process group. Native compiler children can also create their own process groups.

Run each control inside a dedicated subreaper supervisor. It adopts, terminates and reaps all owned descendants, including children that changed groups, without collecting unrelated harness child statuses. Cleanup remains bounded; unproven cleanup is reported separately. Preserve unexpected exit codes and signals, and reject an otherwise expected exit if descendants were left behind. Daemon-owned containers are still removed separately. The #546 readiness failure path now uses the existing bounded child-log diagnostic.

Fixes #551.

Validation:
- Built `test_forked_control_tree`, `test_nginx_differential` and `rut` with Clang 22 Release/JIT.
- Six process/socket unit cases passed; CTest repeated them 50 times without failure. Cases cover a stalled tree, unexpected exit, signal exit, expected-status resource leaks, clean expected exit, independent child status preservation, changed process groups, zombie absence and port rebind.
- The six unit cases passed ASan/UBSan/LSan (15 checks).
- Real Docker cleanup and child-exit readiness diagnostic CTests passed.
- The pinned nginx #546 converter-generated differential passed, including its exact expected-exit control and original wire/lifecycle assertions.
- Targeted bugprone/performance clang-tidy, changed-file formatting and diff checks passed.

The initial #546 run failed before readiness because the host `/tmp` quota was exhausted. Its retained diagnostic identifies LLVM output failure, not an io_uring failure. Final container/differential validation used a private tmpfs through `unshare -Urm`, retaining the host network; no timeout or semantic assertion was relaxed. Full repository CI remains to run on this PR.

items.title: Overlay layers can show files that locked mounts hide
items.body:
Inside a child user namespace, an overlay layer that has a locked mount at or below it shows the files that mount hides, because clonePrivateMount clones each layer without its submounts (pkg/sentry/fsimpl/overlay/overlay.go). A layer from another mount namespace, passed as /proc/self/fd/N, shows what that namespace hides, and a detached tree cloned by open_tree(2) in a more privileged user namespace shows what its own submounts hide.

Linux refuses all three in clone_private_mount(), the first two with EINVAL and the third with EPERM.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer for the first case (as root under runsc do, it prints secret, where Linux refuses the mount)</summary>

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/t && mount -t tmpfs t /tmp/t
mkdir -p /tmp/t/layer/hidden /tmp/t/other /tmp/t/merged
touch /tmp/t/layer/hidden/secret
mount -t tmpfs mask /tmp/t/layer/hidden
unshare -Urm sh -c 'mount -t overlay overlay -o lowerdir=/tmp/t/layer:/tmp/t/other /tmp/t/merged && ls /tmp/t/merged/hidden'
```

</details>

Proposed fix in #15531.
