labels.name: needs-coordinator
labels.description: touches a path outside the arm allowlist: the coordinator reviews and arms it

items.body: The required `go` check failed for two reasons, both visible in the cited run. 1. Test bug, not a conflict-guard bug, on the first arm of https://github.com/Nishfleet/drive/actions/runs/37506210076: the guard claimed (`kept the save that landed first: report (conflict, linux).txt`) and device A listed both files, but the proof read the plain path from the losing mount, whose VFS cache still served that device's own write. Both reads were linux's bytes. 2. Product gap on the same-instant PUT: rclone serve s3 answers `corrupted on transfer: sizes differ` and retries in 10s. The other device had already declared a win after 20 polls (10s), so the retry overwrote with no conflict copy. That is the PR-head fail (https://github.com/Nishfleet/drive/actions/runs/37532475674) and the offline arm of the cited main fail (`Dir.Remove not empty` is rclone's leftover, not the cause). The proof now reads objects from the stand-in. The guard pins the VFS cache inode at first sight, confirms a cheap win with a downloaded hash, and watches 40 polls (20s) so one write-back plus one rclone retry still claims. Two saves in the e2e are 1s apart, still inside the 5s write-back window, so they do not hit rclone's same-instant PUT. ## Scope - `cmd/drive/conflict_e2e_test.go` because that is the test the `go` job runs. - `cmd/drive/conflict_guard.go` because the 10s retry overwrote after the winner stopped watching. - `cmd/drive/conflict_test.go` because the new pin, retry-window and stale-hash cases live next to the existing guard tests. ## Verification Cause (CI logs, not a guess): - fail https://github.com/Nishfleet/drive/actions/runs/37506210076 `conflict_e2e_test.go:146: both saves are the same bytes` with `conflict="report (conflict, linux).txt"` and `drive: conflict guard: kept the save that landed first` - fail https://github.com/Nishfleet/drive/actions/runs/37532475674 `neither save survived ... listing=[report.txt]` with no `kept the save` line - this host, first arm then offline: `corrupted on transfer: sizes differ src 53 vs dst 56` then `will retry in 10s` Object-store read and guard unit tests (this host, FUSE not required): ``` $ go test ./cmd/drive/ -count=1 -timeout 60s -run 'TestWaitForBothSavesInStorageReadsTheObjectStore|TestConflictGuardClaimsAfterTheVFSCacheFileIsGone|TestConflictGuardClaimsAfterTheVFSCacheFileIsReplaced|TestPinKeepsTheHoldWhenTheCacheFileIsGone|TestConflictGuardKeepsASaveThatLandsAfterARetry|TestConflictGuardClaimsWhenTheCachedHashIsStale' -v --- PASS: TestWaitForBothSavesInStorageReadsTheObjectStore (0.00s) --- PASS: TestConflictGuardKeepsASaveThatLandsAfterARetry (0.00s) --- PASS: TestConflictGuardClaimsWhenTheCachedHashIsStale (0.00s) --- PASS: TestConflictGuardClaimsAfterTheVFSCacheFileIsGone (0.00s) --- PASS: TestPinKeepsTheHoldWhenTheCacheFileIsGone (0.00s) --- PASS: TestConflictGuardClaimsAfterTheVFSCacheFileIsReplaced (0.00s) ok github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive 0.031s ``` Two-device proof on this host (`unshare -Urm`, FUSE up): ``` $ unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -count=1 -timeout 180s -run 'TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSaves' -v drive: conflict guard: kept the save that landed first: report (conflict, mac).txt (the other device saved report.txt) conflict_e2e_test.go:150: two devices, one save window: storage=stand-in, plain="B: this save was made second, on the device named linux\n", conflict="report (conflict, mac).txt" drive: conflict guard: kept the save that landed first: offline (conflict, mac).txt (the other device saved offline.txt) conflict_e2e_test.go:183: after the reconnect: plain="B: the save made while the device could not reach storage\n", conflict="A: the save made while the device could not reach storage\n", both saves kept --- PASS: TestTwoDevicesKeepBothSaves (21.31s) ok github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive 21.320s ``` Acceptance: 1. Cause: test read the losing VFS cache; same-instant PUT plus a 10s rclone retry lost the watch window. Not a flake of the runner. 2. Fixed in the files above. No skip. 3. The `go` job on this PR head is the remaining proof for main after merge. semgrep: `semgrep --config p/default --baseline-commit e17a253089b64f17c735947055c8d150a1354878 --quiet --metrics=off` exit 0. in-run review: litellm/worker-capable; 2 findings fixed (pin no longer Removes the hold before a failed re-link; a failed fresh hash no longer skips a win) Closes #797 --- Need help on this PR? items.title: TSI-4326: fix(fuse): 目录改名后立即失效旧投影名
items.body:
Closes TSI-4326

Issue: https://multica.tsic.top/issues/01a17467-13bf-7789-91ab-773ee46df9b3

## 设计依据

tsic/torrentfs-design@5b622b6

## 设计实现

| 设计要求 | 代码落点 |
|---|---|
| 02-contracts §C-1.3.4：daemon 单方移除的条目必须主动失效内核缓存，改名后立即可见，不等 entry TTL | `src/fuse/fs_service.rs:1623` · `rename` 目录分支落库成功后调用 `inval_data_entry(dir_parent, dir_name)` |
| 02-contracts §C-3.3.8：改名成功后主动失效旧名的投影目录项 | 同上；旧路径经 `split_data_dir_parent(&old_source_path)` 拆成（旧父目录 inode，旧名），顶层、嵌套与跨父目录的旧路径都落在旧父目录下 |
| 03-acceptance §A TC-ingest-03 / AC-03：改名旧名消失、新名出现；目录改名带动子树 | 由 TSI-4317 的挂载载体 `tests/acceptance/tc_ingest_03.sh`（分支 head `c7d7fb6`）验证；本 PR 不改该文件 |
| 测试证据：目录改名的失效目标必须可断言 | `src/fuse/fs_service.rs:108` · `EntryInvalidator` 注入点；`src/fuse/fs_service.rs:5876` · `rename_dir_invalidates_the_old_projection_entry` 断言跨父改名、移到根、根级改名三例只失效「旧父目录 + 旧名」 |
| 01-scope 禁项：`data/` 接受变更操作 | 未引入：未给 `data/` 增可写路径，新增抽象只承载内核失效通知 |

## 验证

### 单测判别力

`cargo test`（跳过沙箱 tmpfs 配额不足的 1 GiB 用例）：

| 变体 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 修复态 | 631 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored，新用例 ok |
| 探针 A：删掉失效调用 | 456 passed / **1 failed** — `left: []`，`right: [(4432243, "tree")]` |
| 探针 B：改传 `&new_source_path` | 456 passed / **1 failed** — `left: [(4750922, "sub")]`，`right: [(4432243, "tree")]` |

items.title: install.sh fails with "the downloaded binary does not run on this machine" when TMPDIR is mounted noexec
items.body:
**Version**
Output of `ai-memory --version`: not reached. `install.sh` as published with 3.2.2 (`main` at a387263c).

**What happened**
On a host whose `/tmp` (or `TMPDIR`) is mounted `noexec`, `install.sh` stops after the checksum passed:

```
ai-memory install: downloading ai-memory-linux-x86_64.tar.gz (latest)
ai-memory install: checksum verified
ai-memory install: error: the downloaded binary does not run on this machine
```

Nothing is installed. The release runs fine on that machine: it only cannot be executed from the directory the script picked for its smoke test.

`install.sh` unpacks the archive under a `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ai-memory-install.XXXXXX"` work directory and runs the binary from there (`install.sh:192-194`):

```sh
    "$work/release/ai-memory" --version >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
        die "the downloaded binary does not run on this machine"
```

A `noexec` mount refuses every `execve` of a file on it (`mount(8)`: "Do not permit direct execution of any binaries on the mounted filesystem"), so the shell gets `EACCES`, exits 126, and the script reads that as a binary for the wrong machine. The release is moved to `~/.local/lib/ai-memory` only afterwards (`install.sh:196-199`), where it would have run.

Mounting `/tmp` with `noexec` is a common hardening step (the CIS Linux benchmarks list it under the `/tmp` partition options), so the one-step install is unavailable on such hosts unless the user knows to set `TMPDIR` to an executable location first, which no message suggests.

**What I expected**
Either the smoke test runs the binary from beside its install location (`$lib_dir.new.$$` is already created on the same filesystem as `~/.local/lib/ai-memory` before the final move), so a `noexec` work directory does not matter, or the error names the directory it tried so the user can point `TMPDIR` elsewhere.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. On Linux, make a `noexec` temporary directory. Without root, a user namespace does it:

   ```sh
   mkdir -p /tmp/noexec
   unshare -Urm sh -c 'mount -t tmpfs -o noexec tmpfs /tmp/noexec && TMPDIR=/tmp/noexec sh ./install.sh'
   ```

   (or run the installer on a host whose `/tmp` is mounted `noexec`.)
2. The script prints `checksum verified`, then `error: the downloaded binary does not run on this machine`, and exits 1.
3. Run the same `install.sh` with `TMPDIR=$HOME` (an executable location): it installs and links `~/.local/bin/ai-memory`.

**Environment**
- OS: Linux x86_64 (any distribution with `/tmp` mounted `noexec`)
- Docker? no
- Agent: not applicable
- Transport: not applicable

**Relevant logs**
```
ai-memory install: downloading ai-memory-linux-x86_64.tar.gz (latest)
ai-memory install: checksum verified
ai-memory install: error: the downloaded binary does not run on this machine
```

With the `2>/dev/null` on that line removed, the shell shows the real cause: `sh: /tmp/noexec/ai-memory-install.AbC123/release/ai-memory: Permission denied`.

items.title: Hibernation fixture readiness depends on the default Bash user prompt
items.body:
At Mesh runtime source 913e0b20d8c057b046d06edc6581d42f01125b41, Linux and Go 1.27.0, the unchanged hibernation integration fixture failed in a private user/mount namespace mapped to UID 0. The namespace exposed a disposable SSD scratch directory at /tmp and used a private HOME/config/state. It retained the host network namespace and reached the real fixture daemon normally.

Command structure:

```sh
bun /work/platform-production/heavy/current/run.js --class suite "issue121 full verification mount only" -- env PATH="$PATH" unshare -Urm bash /work/tmp/i121/verify.sh
```

The script ran `./scripts/verify.sh` after the passing full race/vet checks. Integrations passed 61/62 scripts. The failure was:

```text
FAIL: hibernation.sh (exit 1)
RuntimeError: terminal did not print b'$' within 4s
```

The fixture daemon had already reported successful idle-agent hibernation. No socket bind failure appeared. `integration/helpers/hibernation.py:38-43` starts `/bin/bash --norc -i`; line 58 waits for a literal dollar prompt. Bash's default interactive prompt depends on the effective UID, so UID 0 uses `#`.

Bounded control retained the same short SSD bind mount and private configuration but preserved the normal fixture UID:

```sh
bun /work/platform-production/heavy/current/run.js --class suite "issue121 normal UID integration acceptance" -- env PATH="$PATH" unshare -Ucm --keep-caps bash /work/tmp/i121/verify-integration.sh
```

The harness printed `Fixture UID 1000` and the complete integration suite passed all 62 scripts, including hibernation. The hibernation source and its four-second expectation were unchanged. The failure was observed once under UID 0 and the control passed once under UID 1000.

This is separate from #121's Unix socket path/runtime readiness fixes. The fixture should own a deterministic shell readiness marker so effective UID and default prompt text cannot select whether the scenario runs.

items.title: Native overlay, zero third-party: unshare + mount -t overlay (needs a real machine)
items.body:
## Idea

The current `overlay` tier needs `bwrap`. With root/sudo it doesn't have to:
`unshare -m` + `mount -t overlay` are **util-linux (base)**, and overlayfs is
the **kernel** — zero third-party tools. This is the "native" overlay, and it
fits the repo's extreme-path ethos.

Needs a real machine to verify (Termux can't do unprivileged overlayfs or a
mount namespace), hence this issue.

## The method

```sh
unshare -m --propagation private -- bash -c '
  ovl="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sudo-less-overlay.$$"
  mkdir -p "$ovl/up-usr" "$ovl/wk-usr"
  mount -t tmpfs -o mode=0700 tmpfs "$ovl"
  mount -t overlay overlay \
    -o "lowerdir=$PREFIX/usr:/usr,upperdir=$ovl/up-usr,workdir=$ovl/wk-usr" /usr
  if [ -d "$PREFIX/etc" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$ovl/up-etc" "$ovl/wk-etc"
    mount -t overlay overlay \
      -o "lowerdir=$PREFIX/etc:/etc,upperdir=$ovl/up-etc,workdir=$ovl/wk-etc" /etc
  fi
  export PATH="$PREFIX/sbin:$PREFIX/bin:$PREFIX/usr/bin:$PATH"
  exec "$@"
' _ your-command
```

### How it works

- The **real** `$PREFIX/usr` is the top `lowerdir` (used in place, not copied);
  the host `/usr` is the bottom fallback. Leftmost wins in overlayfs, so the
  prefix shadows the system only for files it actually has.
- Writes go to a **tmpfs upper** — nothing lands in the prefix or the host; it's
  ephemeral and gone when the namespace exits.
- The overlay mount lives in a **private mount namespace** (`unshare -m`), so
  the host's real `/usr` is untouched.
- Overlay, not bind: `--bind $PREFIX/usr /usr` would *hide* the system's glibc
  and libs; overlay stacks.

## Variants / requirements

| who | namespace | kernel needs |
|---|---|---|
| root/sudo | `unshare -m --propagation private` | overlayfs |
| no root | `unshare -Urm --propagation private` | unprivileged userns + overlayfs >= 5.11 |

## Gotchas

- **`lowerdir` order is the reverse of bwrap's `--overlay-src`.** Kernel:
  leftmost = highest priority. So it's `$PREFIX/usr:/usr`, not `/usr:$PREFIX/usr`.
- As root the whole host `/` is writable (bwrap's base was `--ro-bind / /`). That
  is inherent to "I have sudo" — document it, don't pretend otherwise.
- `$PREFIX` must not be under `/usr` (overlayfs forbids one layer being an
  ancestor of another).
- tmpfs upper is what bwrap's `--tmp-overlay` does, so xattr support is fine.

## Proposed change

- `tools/prefix-run.sh`: the current `overlay_ok()` is bwrap-specific. Add a
  sibling `native_overlay_ok()` probe (a throwaway overlay mount in a namespace)
  and a native runner; choose bwrap when present, else native. Optionally
  `--mode overlay-native` to force it.
- Keep it in the **experimental** bucket (`docs/standard.md`); this does not
  change the supported (floor) tier.
- Update the mode table in `docs/paths.md`.

## Acceptance / verification (on a real Debian or Mobian box)

- Install a package that reads a baked-in `/usr/share/...` path, run it via the
  native overlay, confirm the prefix copy is read.
- Confirm the host `/usr` is unmodified after exit (`find`/checksum spot check).
- Test both root (`unshare -m`) and, if enabled, the `unshare -Urm` path.

## Related

- `tools/prefix-run.sh`, `docs/paths.md` (tier model), `docs/standard.md`.
- #22 (bare-Debian test env) — the same real-machine need.

items.title: [Engine] an opt-in filter that redacts — or refuses to execute — model output and tool calls matching a configurable blocklist
items.body:
This is a **suggestion for a mitigation, offered for discussion**. The feature
described here is opt-in, and whether it belongs in Strata (and in what form) is
what the discussion is for.

The open issues were searched for cohere / exfiltration / blocklist / blocked-strings
(2026-10-26); no open thread covers this. The audit-findings collector #544 has since
closed, so this stands alone and can be linked from a future collector.

### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### What do you want to do?

Run the shipped model behind MCP tools with a guardrail on what it actually emits.
Cohere's disclosure today ("Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model")
shows the exact model Strata ships — Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — attempting, in rare cases
(under 1 in 100,000 calls in their runs), to inventory the machine and upload a probe
file to an Alibaba Cloud bucket in Beijing, probe cloud metadata endpoints, and reach
for `unshare -Urm` to get root inside a namespace. Their first recommendation is to
"enforce on the actual tool call before it runs. A reasoning trace is not a security
boundary."

The docs describe MCP tools as running "with your user's rights, and the model decides
when to call them", and [README.md](README.md) promises "Nothing leaves your PC". That
promise holds for the engine, but the moment a model's output drives a tool — MCP
servers the run config starts, or a coding agent on the client side — the weights have
a keyboard, and today nothing in `serve/server.py` looks at what the model wrote before
it goes out or into a tool.

The goal: a filter between the model and every consumer of its output, configured by a
plain JSON list of strings, that redacts matches — or, for tool calls, refuses to run
them. Whether it belongs in Strata (and in what form) is the discussion wanted here,
before any pull request.

### What do you do today instead?

An external patch, applied locally and working: three small hooks in `serve/server.py`
plus a stdlib-only `serve/blocked.py` (details under "The proposed implementation"
below).

### The proposed implementation

Three small edits to `serve/server.py` plus one new module, `serve/blocked.py`
(stdlib-only, ~250 lines):

1. an import next to the other `from serve ...` imports;
2. `blocked_api.wrap(svc)` right after the single `svc = Service(...)` in `main()` — it
   wraps the instance's `run` generator, which every endpoint consumes (chat SSE and
   non-SSE, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses`, the web app, and `run_with_mcp`);
3. a one-line gate on `run_with_mcp`'s `run_them` line so a blocked MCP call is not
   executed.

The filter:

- redacts strings from a configurable list in the model's `content`, `reasoning` and
  streamed tool-argument deltas, with a hold-back buffer so a match split across two
  streamed deltas is still caught (verified by test);
- rewrites each complete tool call's name and arguments (as a copy) before any consumer
  sees them — including `run_with_mcp`, so an MCP tool never receives blocked arguments;
- two modes, per config: `"block_action": "redact"` (default — the call runs with
  redacted arguments) or `"skip_call"` (the call is not executed at all; it takes
  `run_with_mcp`'s existing "skipped, not run" path, so nothing new in the client
  protocol);
- reads the list from `~/.config/strata/blocked.json` (or `$STRATA_BLOCKED_CONFIG`),
  re-checked by mtime on every request — editing the list needs no restart.

The config is a plain JSON file: `{"enabled": true, "case_insensitive": true,
"replacement": "[blocked]", "block_action": "redact", "on_error": "open", "strings":
["rm -rf ", "sudo rm"]}`. With no config file the filter is off.

This is Cohere's "enforce on the actual tool call": the check runs on what the model
actually emitted, not on the reasoning trace. The trace passes through the same filter,
so a command it "said" it would not run is still caught if it writes one.

### What it does not do

- It does not stop egress. Cohere's "deny agent egress by default" lives at the
  network layer; this patch sees only strings. A model that encodes a URL (hex,
  base64, `$'\x72\x6d'`, variables) walks around a substring filter. It is not claimed
  that this stops a determined model — it is a guardrail against the specific, rare,
  accidental call-home pattern in the disclosure and similar accidents, not a security
  boundary.
- It does not police incoming prompts, the engine spawn, `before_load`, or image
  generation; those commands come from the run config, not the model.
- It cannot see what a client-side agent (Codex, Claude Code) executes with its own
  tools after receiving redacted output — but it does redact that output first, which is
  the right enforcement point for what the model wrote.
- In `"redact"` mode a matched *shell-ish* tool call still runs, with mangled arguments.
  For tools that run commands, `"skip_call"` is the recommended mode; see the risks
  below.

### The default path stays byte-identical (per the contributing rules)

The feature is opt-in: no config file, no filtering. With the filter disabled the
wrapper passes events through unchanged; the check was a mock-engine e2e run with
filtering off, comparing the served answer byte-for-byte with the pre-patch
server, plus a 27-case unit suite against the real `serve.frontend` types (a match
split across two deltas, complete tool-call argument redaction, `ToolCall.namespace`
preserved, unknown event kinds passed through, disabled passthrough). The only added
work on the disabled path is one `stat()` per request.

One question for maintainers: if no config file exists, should `wrap(svc)` be a no-op
entirely? That is a one-line change and makes the unconfigured path literally the last
release's code path; the wrapper is left in place so that dropping a config file into
`~/.config/strata/` works without a restart.

### New risks the patch itself introduces

Listing these up front, because a mitigation that overstates itself is its own hazard:

1. **False confidence.** The biggest risk is a user treating the server as safe
   because a filter is on. Substring matching is the weakest kind of check; the
   disclosure's own trigger (`curl ... -o`) is only catchable if the exact spelling is
   on the list.
2. **Redacted commands can still run, mangled.** In `"redact"` mode, `rm -rf [blocked]`
   still executes `rm`. For anything that runs shell commands, `"skip_call"` is the
   safer mode; `"redact"` fits text and read-only tools.
3. **Fail-open default.** `"on_error": "open"` (the default) passes a completion
   through unfiltered after one internal filter error, with a single stderr warning —
   an adversarial output that breaks the filter could turn it off for its own request.
   `"closed"` fails the completion instead. Input would be useful on which should be the
   default, and on surfacing filter errors in `/api-monitor` rather than stderr only.
4. **A race in `"skip_call"` under `"parallel": 2`.** The raw-match record lives in one
   module-level registry, cleared wholesale at 4,096 entries; with parallel streams a
   concurrent clear can drop the record for a pending call, and the gate then falls
   back to matching the already-redacted arguments — which no longer match — so a
   blocked call could execute. Fix is straightforward (per-stream registry or FIFO
   eviction); flagged because it exists in the locally applied version.
5. **Evidence loss.** Redaction happens before anything is stored or shown, so the
   monitor never shows what the model actually wrote — the operator alerting on
   "unexpected tool calls" sees `[blocked]` with no original for incident response.
   Worth discussing whether to log matched-call metadata (which list entry, which tool)
   somewhere durable.
6. **A small oracle.** A visible `[blocked]` tells an attacking prompt which strings
   the operator blocks, which helps iterative evasion. `"skip_call"` reveals nothing in
   the output; the replacement text is configurable.
7. **Re-chunked streams.** The hold-back buffer re-chunks SSE deltas (never drops
   text). Clients that reassemble deltas are unaffected — all of Strata's own
   consumers are — but a client assuming one JSON token per chunk would notice.
8. **It is an untracked local patch.** Applied outside the repo, an upgrade silently
   reverts it while the config file stays behind. `apply.sh check` reports this, but
   nothing enforces it at startup; if the feature lands upstream, this whole class of
   problem goes away — which is the main reason for opening this discussion rather than
   keeping the patch private.

### Questions for maintainers

1. Should this land in Strata, and as a run-config feature (next to `mcp_servers`) or
   as-is with a JSON config file?
2. Should `wrap()` no-op when no config file exists (literal byte-identical default
   path), or keep the wrapper so the feature can be turned on without a restart?
3. Default `"block_action"`: `redact` (availability, matches today's web app behavior)
   or `skip_call` (safety for command-running MCP tools)?
4. Should filter errors be visible in `/api-monitor`, and should the server log
   blocked-match metadata for incident response?
5. Related and out of scope here, but Cohere's list also suggests alerting on
   unexpected cloud URLs and blocking unprivileged user namespaces in agent
   containers. The first might fit `run_with_mcp`'s existing "call" event; the second
   belongs in docs/AI_SETUP.md rather than the server. Separate discussions if wanted.

### References

- Cohere, "Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model" (2026-10-26):
  https://cohere.com/blog/concerning-behaviour-popular-open-weight-ai-model

items.title: Oldest Mac we support: run the mount test on older macOS and Intel, publish the real minimum
items.body:
## What this changes

The drive mount proof now runs on macOS. `drive mount` already resolved
`rclone nfsmount` on darwin (macOS's built-in NFS server), but the proof's
helpers waited with `findmnt` and cleaned up with `fusermount`, neither of which
exists on a Mac, so on a Mac the test waited for a command that is not there
and then reported the host as refusing the mount.

- `cmd/drive/mount.go` splits `Mounted()` into `Mounted()` + `MountedDir()`, so a
  caller holding the mount point itself asks the same question `drive mount`
  asks. One platform switch, not two.
- `cmd/drive/e2e_test.go` `mountIsLive()` now calls `MountedDir()`; the proof
  and the product cannot drift on what "mounted" means.
- `unmountForCleanup()` picks `umount` on darwin and `fusermount3`/`fusermount`
  on Linux, and the caller logs only when the kernel still reports the mount,
  so a mount rclone already took down is not reported as a failure.
- The skip message names the host's own constraint, not the other platform's.

No macFUSE, no kernel extension, no approval prompt: rclone's own docs say the
`nfsmount` path starts the NFS server and mounts it for you, and that path needs
passwordless sudo, which GitHub's Mac runners grant the default user.

## The Mac CI job

The worker token cannot write `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so the job YAML is
posted as a comment on issue #116 for the orchestrator to push. It adds a
`changes` gate (runs the Mac legs only when `cmd/drive` changed) and a `mac`
matrix of `macos-15-intel`, `macos-15` and `macos-26`. Those labels are read
from the actions/runner-images README: macOS 13 is gone, macOS 14 is deprecated
and retires 2026-11-02, so today's oldest Intel image is `macos-15-intel` and
Apple silicon is 15 and 26. The big file shrinks to 16 MiB per leg, which keeps
each leg short; the streaming assertion is the one the 64 MiB Linux proof
makes. The same comment also carries the three PR #120 review findings for the
`go` job: pin rclone, drop `fetch-depth: 0` where it is not needed, and run the
proof once per platform rather than twice.

## Status (as of this PR)

**not started** on the published minimum. Mac minutes are 10x on a private repo
and no Mac image has a green run yet, so I did not publish a minimum. The row
on `docs/scoreboard.md` stays `not yet measured` and now says the proof runs on
macOS through `nfsmount` and that the publishable minimum is the oldest Mac
image with a green run. `docs-site/limits.md` says the same.

Closes #116

## Verification

Proof this test is now platform-aware — it passes on this Linux host through the
shared `MountedDir()` helper (inside `unshare -Urm`, the user-namespace fallback
this host needs, rclone v1.75.1):

```
$ unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -run TestStandinMountProof -v -timeout 300s -count=1
    e2e_test.go:128: mounting through rclone mount on linux
    e2e_test.go:140: first 64 KiB of a 64 MiB file at 0.007s
    e2e_test.go:156: full 64 MiB object over the same loopback in 0.205s
--- PASS: TestStandinMountProof (9.99s)
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive  10.001s
```

The other three proofs that drive a mount through the same helpers
(`TestOpenTimeColdAndWarm`, `TestBackgroundFillFillsThroughTheCappedCache`,
`TestBackgroundFillDoesNotSlowAForegroundOpen`) all pass: `PASS
github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive 199.867s`.

The macOS side compiles for both Mac architectures (Go 1.24.0, the same version
CI pins):

```
$ GOOS=darwin go vet ./cmd/...            # ok
$ for a in amd64 arm64; do GOOS=darwin GOARCH=$a go test -c -o /tmp/dt-$a.test ./cmd/drive/; done
darwin/amd64 test binary OK
darwin/arm64 test binary OK
```

The Go suite and the touched Node tests:

```
$ go test ./cmd/drive/ -short -count=1
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive  4.170s

$ node --test test/scoreboard.test.mjs test/docs.test.mjs test/pr-gate.test.mjs
# pass 36
# fail 0

$ test -z "$(git ls-files scripts bin tools ops '*.sh')"   # no new helper scripts
```

Diff-scoped semgrep against `origin/main`'s merge base: exit 0, no findings.

Live fleet state:

```
$ XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u) systemctl --user list-units --state=failed   # empty
$ curl -s 127.0.0.1:4000/health/readiness   # {"status":"healthy","db":"connected"}
```

### What was not proven here

- No Mac has actually run the proof in CI. The orchestrator pushes the workflow
  (comment on #116), and a green run per image is the evidence for the published
  minimum. That is why the minimum is still `not yet measured`.
- A failed command, named: `gh run list` for CI run links returned
  HTTP 403 `Resource not accessible by integration` (the worker token has no
  Actions read), so this PR carries no run URLs.

## in-run review

`in-run review: unavailable - <the reviewer call printed nothing on the first
attempt and I did not retry beyond a single extra pass; the second pass's
findings are fixed above>`

The reviewer's findings that were acted on: gofmt (this PR was unformatted),
the second platform switch in `mountIsLive` (now `MountedDir`), the
unconditional `umount` on Linux (now platform-selected, with the
already-unmounted case not reported), the scoreboard cell's prose (shortened to
the status plus the pointer to #116), and the limits page's promise with no
owner (#116 now named).

items.title: docs(status): 26 Sep entry — 2e CI feasibility, the budget record, #83 and #84
items.body:
Appends the 26 Sep 2026 session entry to `docs/STATUS.md` **"Agent-reported, unverified"** per `AGENT-RULES.md` §10. Nothing was moved between sections.

## Observed

- **2e**: no code, no attack list, no branch, no issue. The hole is live — `atrium-shell run --root … --cwd / -- cat /etc/passwd` → `stdout=2943 bytes` (the real host file); `hand-test-2b.sh` reproduces `78/0/5`.
- **CI feasibility — answered.** On `ubuntu-latest` (Ubuntu 24.04.5 / kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure) unprivileged user namespaces are **blocked** (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`): `unshare -Urm` → rc=1, `bwrap` → `setting up uid map: Permission denied`. **One `sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0` fixes it** and holds for the job. After it, the §2e requirement holds end to end: `/etc/passwd` absent inside, virtual root at `/`, writes land in the root, host untouched, `python3` runs. Run [36244899076](https://github.com/ItzMuff1n/atrium/actions/runs/36244899076); **branch and run deleted, `main` untouched** (`41f567b` before and after).
- **A defect in the required `hand-tests` check → #83.** `hand-test-2a`'s outside-directory fingerprint uses `ls -laR`, which prints the `..` entry — so it includes **/tmp's own size**. items.title: fix(automation): honour the switch inside a user-namespace sandbox
items.body:
## What

The automation switch now opens the door for apps running inside a user-namespace sandbox, such as a Kora workspace or any other bwrap sandbox that doesn't map root.

Until now, an app inside a workspace kept its door shut even with `/etc/iced/automation-enabled` in place. Inside the sandbox:
- root's files show up as the kernel's overflow uid (65534);
- `/` and `/nix` are folders bwrap made, owned by the user;
- `/etc` and `/nix/store` are read-only mounts of the machine's.

The switch walk insists on root from `/` down, so it failed at its first step.

## How

`Trust::root()` reads `/proc/self/uid_map`. When the namespace doesn't map the root outside it:
- **Overflow uid as root:** the overflow uid also counts as root.
- **Mounts restore trust:** a mount root (`STATX_ATTR_MOUNT_ROOT`, through rustix's `statx`) counts as root's wherever it is mounted.
- **Walking through the sandbox's own folders:** a folder that isn't root's (`/`, `/nix`) is walked through without trust. No link in it is followed and no file in it counts, until a root-owned mount restores trust.

Outside a sandbox nothing changes. Only root counts, there is no mount rule, and the walk still requires root from `/` down.

### Why mounts can be trusted

- **Nothing inside can change the mounts.** A process inside a bwrap sandbox has no capabilities, so it can't mount, unmount, or move a mount point. Moving a mount point fails with EBUSY.
- **Nested namespaces don't help.** A nested namespace (`unshare -Urm`) can mount, but only in a copy that the apps already running never see. The door was never meant to stop someone driving an app they started themselves.
- **No root-owned objects can be forged.** The user owns the sandbox's own folders, but can't create anything owned by root or the overflow uid in them. Moving someone else's directory into a new parent needs write access to that directory.
- **Outside processes are no new risk.** A same-uid process outside the sandbox can enter its namespaces, but as the namespace's owner it can already ptrace everything inside.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** `cargo test -p iced_automation` passes 41 tests. New ones cover the uid-map check, and the walk through a folder others can write down to a "mount" (via an injected predicate). Nothing directly in that folder counts, whether a file or a link.
- **Real sandbox test:** the new `#[ignore]`d `in_a_real_sandbox_roots_files_count_and_mine_do_not` passes inside a Kora workspace. It checks that `/etc/os-release` (a NixOS link through `/etc/static` into the store) counts and that a file of the user's doesn't.
- **Lint:** `cargo clippy -p iced_automation --all-features --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p iced_winit --features automation -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.
- **On a Kora laptop:** I built `examples/counter` with `automation` and its switch set to an empty root-owned store file, on master and on this branch. Each run opened the door, asked for `info`, clicked "Increment" and read the tree back.

| | machine plane | inside the `default` workspace |
|---|---|---|
| master `f965ff35` | door opens, click works (0 → 1) | **no socket** |
| this branch | door opens, click works (0 → 1) | door opens, click works (0 → 1) |

Inside that workspace, `uid_map` is `1000 1000 1`. `/` and `/nix` are owned by 1000, and `/etc` and `/nix/store` by 65534.

items.title: Install apps from GitHub releases and keep them updated
items.body:
## What

`sudo rime install --allow-unsigned github:OWNER/REPO` installs the `.rpm` attached to a GitHub repository's latest release into the system extension, and `rime update` follows that repository's later releases.

Until now, software published only as GitHub release assets could be installed as a local `.rpm` (pinned: `rime update` never moves it) or an AppImage (also pinned). Neither keeps an app current.

## How

- `rime-pkg`: new `github_fetch` / `github_refresh`. The package is an ordinary `local:<NAME>` (NAME from the rpm header, not the repo name); the followed repository is a side file `local/<NAME>.github`, so cache GC, rollback and older engines handle it without changes.
- Exactly one `.rpm` for this arch (or noarch) on the latest non-draft, non-prerelease release; zero or several is a refusal. Asset and checksum URLs must be downloads from that repository's releases.
- Checked against GitHub's published sha256 `digest` and the release's `SHA256SUMS` when present. On `rime update`, an unchanged digest downloads nothing; a failed fetch or check is a warning and keeps the installed build; a release whose rpm changes package name is not installed.
- Trust is stated, not borrowed: `--allow-unsigned` is required before anything is downloaded, and it accepts the repository's future releases. `state.json` gets `github_sources`; `rime pkg list` and `rime pkg verify` name every followed repository. These are never reported as vendor-verified.
- `rime resolve github:…` and `rime remove github:…` work. CLI help and `docs/packages.md` updated.

## Tests

- `tests/test-rime-pkg.sh` 153/0: routing, repo validation (incl. `..`, injection), refusal without the flag, digest and SHA256SUMS mismatches, zero/two candidates, foreign asset URL, prerelease, unreachable API, and `github_refresh` against real rpm fixtures in an `unshare -Urm` namespace (unchanged / newer / renamed package / offline).
- Mutants (5), each caught: no flag gate, no URL-origin check, no name check on refresh, no digest short-circuit, no SHA256SUMS compare.
- deb 162/0, appimage 170/0, resolve 91/0, legacy-ext 25/0, alternatives 15/0, etc-label 21/0, pkg-update 26/0. shellcheck -S warning clean.
- `cargo test -p rime`: 673/1, the one failure being the pre-existing `blueprint::an_inert_converger…`.
- Live, unprivileged: `github_fetch` against six real repositories resolved, checked and downloaded each rpm; one with a matching digest downloaded nothing.

## Release note

Software published as GitHub releases can now be installed with `sudo rime install --allow-unsigned github:OWNER/REPO`, and `rime update` keeps it on the latest release. The packages are not signed, so Rime asks you to accept the repository once and lists it in `rime pkg list` from then on.

## Summary by Sourcery

Enable installation of unsigned RPMs from GitHub releases and keep them updated from the accepted repository.

New Features:
- Install RPMs from a GitHub repository’s latest eligible release and follow subsequent releases during updates.
- Support resolving and removing GitHub release sources through the CLI.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent invalid, unverifiable, or mismatched GitHub release assets from being installed or replacing an existing package.

Enhancements:
- Record accepted GitHub sources and distinguish their unsigned packages from vendor-verified packages.
- Add release asset digest and optional SHA256SUMS validation, architecture-aware asset selection, and unchanged-release download avoidance.

Documentation:
- Document GitHub release installation, update behavior, trust requirements, and related CLI commands.

Tests:
- Add coverage for repository validation, trust gating, asset selection, checksum verification, refresh behavior, package renames, and offline updates.

items.title: fix(linux): stop the AppImage asking for a root password
items.body:
Stacked on #6108 (same `appimage.files` map, so it would conflict otherwise). Retarget to `main` once that merges.

## The prompt

Every new AppImage blocks on a modal at first launch and then asks for the root password through `pkexec`. That is the bundler's `fix-namespaces.hook`: distros like Ubuntu 24.04+ set `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`, the hook sees `unshare -Urm` fail, and offers to install an AppArmor profile granting `userns`. The profile it writes is keyed to the AppImage's *exact path*:

```
profile readest-appimage /home/user/Desktop/Readest_0.12.6-2026090706_amd64.AppImage flags=(unconfined) {
```

so every nightly is a new file and asks again.

## Why it is pointless here

Readest doesn't use the Chromium sandbox. `tauri-runtime-cef` sets `CefSettings.no_sandbox = !cfg!(feature = "sandbox")`, and this build compiles it without that feature. Every child process of the shipped `0.12.6-2026090706` AppImage:

```
pid 1567277: --type=zygote  --no-sandbox
pid 1567301: --type=utility --no-sandbox
```

and the app starts and runs normally on a machine where `unshare -Urm /bin/true` is denied and no profile is installed. The hook is boilerplate for Chromium apps that *do* sandbox; for this one it buys a root prompt and nothing else.

## Fix

An AppRun hook that sorts ahead of it (`AppRun` does `for hook in $APPDIR/bin/*.hook`) and stubs the two helpers it prompts through. Both come from `AppRun.lib` and nothing else in the bundle calls them, so the rest of `fix-namespaces.hook` still runs — its checks just can't reach the user.

It ships through `appimage.files` from `tauri.conf.json` rather than the workflows, so local Linux builds get it too; the CI staging step now merges into that map (`+=`) instead of replacing it, and the guard fails the build if the hook does not reach the packed AppDir.

## Verification

Against the extracted `0.12.6-2026090706` bundle, headless, on a host where unprivileged userns is denied:

| | result |
|---|---|
| stock hooks | blocks on the dialog — 3 lines of log, app never starts |
| with this hook | app starts normally, 117 lines, no `zenity`, no `pkexec` |

Also verified in an `ubuntu:22.04` container that a file placed through `appimage.files` survives quick-sharun and lands in `bin/` ahead of the bundler's own hooks:

```
### bin/ after bundling:
00-no-userns-prompt.hook
01-path-mapping-hardcoded.hook
fix-namespaces.hook
vulkan-check.hook
```

## Scope

This leaves the AppImage exactly as sandboxed as it is today — which is also what the WebKitGTK builds before it were, since Tauri never enabled WebKit's bubblewrap sandbox. Actually sandboxing the renderer on Linux is a separate piece of work: it needs the CEF `sandbox` feature, plus `/etc/apparmor.d/readest` shipped in the deb/rpm the way Chrome's package does, and this hook would then have to go — the hook file says so.

items.title: linux: a sandboxed command stays in the namespaces made for it
items.body:
On Linux, a sandboxed command that runs under the seccomp helper stays in the namespaces the sandbox made for it: it cannot create a user namespace or a mount namespace of its own, join another, or change a mount tree. The sandbox's denies are mounts, and a mount holds in the namespace it was made in.

**On by default, and a change of behaviour.** See "Who sees a difference".

**This branch now holds #617 too,** which was stacked on it and has been merged into it (`75b39fe`: four files, +219). So merging this PR lands both. See "With no helper" below, and #617 for its own description and review.

## What changes

- **A second seccomp filter, `namespaces`, is stacked on the command.**
  - `unshare` and `clone` with `CLONE_NEWUSER` or `CLONE_NEWNS`, `setns`, `mount`, `umount2`, `pivot_root` and the fd-based mount calls answer `EPERM`.
  - `unshare` with `UNSHARE_EMPTY_MNTNS` (Linux 7.1) too. To `clone` that bit is `CLONE_PARENT_SETTID`, which threads need, so it is left alone there.
  - `clone3` answers `ENOSYS`, so libc falls back to `clone`.
  - The generator fails rather than write a filter that lacks a call it cannot name.
- The helper sets `user.max_user_namespaces=0` in its user namespace.
- The helper is non-dumpable before its first fork, and its outer half takes the filter too.
- **New option `allowNestedUserNamespaces` (default `false`) lifts all of it,** for the session or for a single wrap (in the configuration passed to `wrapWithSandbox`, as `allowPty` is). It reaches the helper from the configuration. A variable in the caller's environment does not.

## Who sees a difference

**Whatever sandboxes itself with namespaces fails inside the sandbox, unless the option is on:**

| | what it says |
|---|---|
| `unshare -r`, `unshare -Urm` | `unshare: unshare failed: Operation not permitted` |
| a nested `bwrap` or `srt` | `bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace…` |
| Chromium, Electron, Playwright, Puppeteer | `No usable sandbox!` (works with `--no-sandbox`) |
| rootless podman, buildah | `EPERM` |

- Threads, worker threads, forks and pipelines work as before.
- A command started by uid 0 also loses `mount`, `umount`, `setns` and `unshare -m`.
- **Whoever builds or embeds the helper from `vendor/seccomp-src` gets the limit only with a rebuild.** An older helper ignores the setting: everything starts, and nothing is limited.

## Testing

- Each build with a helper built from its own sources, real bubblewrap, Bun and Node: the table above; with the option on, all of it works; a write-denied file stays as it was.
- Twelve wraps at once from one session, every other one given the option: each as given. A wrap with the option keeps its file, network and socket limits. Nothing but `true` lifts the limit.
- As uid 0 of a user namespace: `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)`, `clone(CLONE_NEWNS)` and the 7.1 flag answer `EPERM`, and a thread still starts.
- A live test asks each call so that the kernel, asked, would say something other than `EPERM`. It fails with a helper built from the commit before.
- The generator's test; config validation; the container suite as uid 0.

## Not covered

- **A wrap with no helper in its chain** (`allowAllUnixSockets: true`, or no helper for the architecture): nothing limits namespaces there. #617, stacked on this, does.
- An older helper imposes no limit, and nothing reports that.

## With no helper (#617)

A wrap with no helper in its chain (`allowAllUnixSockets: true`, or no helper for the architecture) gets none of the above. It now gives bubblewrap `--disable-userns`, unless `allowNestedUserNamespaces` or `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` is on.

- The option needs bubblewrap 0.8.0 or later, not setuid. Where it cannot be used, one warning per process says that nothing keeps the command from creating a user namespace.
- Never passed beside the helper, which makes a namespace of its own.
- There `unshare -r` and a nested `bwrap` fail with `ENOSPC` ("No space left on device"), not `EPERM`.

items.title: conflict guard: hash saves where they lie, bound each pass

labels.name: needs-coordinator
labels.description: touches a path outside the arm allowlist: the coordinator reviews and arms it

items.body:
The conflict guard hashes each save from rclone's VFS cache file instead of keeping a second copy, takes 100 saves per pass, and `drive status` names a backlog as "conflict guard behind by N saves".

rclone stores that cache as `drive{XXXX}` when the remote has extra config. The guard looks that folder up, and a missing prefix is an empty listing, not a failed pass. A claim copies from the cache file so a reconnect cannot replace this device's bytes with a download.

## Finish line

1. Bounded work per pass (N paths), continuing where it left off; hash from the VFS cache file instead of copying; skip the remote hash when one parent listing shows the path never existed.

items.title: drive pause and resume with rclone's own remote-control API
items.body:
`drive pause` holds rclone's own upload queue (`vfs/queue-set-expiry`) and caps the file already in flight (`core/bwlimit` `1KiB:off`). `drive resume` releases that queue and sets the rate to `off`. `drive status` prints each file's name, percent and time left, plus bytes left, from `vfs/queue` and `core/stats`. The first-run page uses the same Paused / Resumed words through `uploadLine`.

Looked at: rclone.org/rc `core/bwlimit`, `vfs/queue`, `vfs/queue-set-expiry`, `core/stats` on rclone v1.75.1. rclone treats rate `0` as off, so pause is `1KiB:off`, not zero.

Remainder: #308 (the first-run status endpoint and the usage page do not yet carry live rclone progress).

scope: `cmd/drive/pause.go` because pause and resume are new commands
scope: `cmd/drive/rc.go` because they talk through the mount's existing rclone remote control

items.title: feat(backup-store): store trait with filesystem and S3 implementations [backup/restore 2/4]
items.body:
**Backup/restore series** (design: #396): #384 restore fidelity (merged) · #393 store · #394 format · #395 SnapshotEngine (stacked on #394) · next: PITR surface (#335 rebased), catalog index, backup job, restore job.

## What

New crate `crates/backup-store`: one trait, `BackupStore` (`put`, `get`, `head`, `list`, `delete_prefix`, `validate`), with a filesystem implementation and an S3 implementation on `aws-sdk-s3`. The backup job and the restore path (later PRs) write and read portable backups through it; #396 section 2 is the design. One commit, squashed with #336's work (Lee is co-author); supersedes #336. Rebased onto main after #384 and #338 merged.

Keys are `/`-separated component paths bounded at 1024 bytes; empty components, `.`, `..`, backslashes and control characters are rejected, with the same rule on both stores so a backup written through one reads through the other. Prefix matching is component-aligned. `put` returns `ObjectMeta` (bytes written, ETag where the store has one) so the manifest writer needs no second `head`. A failed put never leaves a partial object under its key; an object that was there before may remain.

**Filesystem store.** Every key is resolved one component at a time with `symlink_metadata`; any symlink, in-root or escaping, is refused on `put`, `get` (which also opens with `O_NOFOLLOW`) and `head`. `list` and `delete_prefix` resolve their prefix with the same walk, so a symlink above the final prefix component is refused too; a symlink at the prefix itself is nothing there; below the prefix, `list` skips symlinks and `delete_prefix` removes them as links without following.

Those checks are path-based and can be raced by a process that can write under the root, so the store requires that only the owner can reach the tree, and enforces it on Unix: `open()` and `validate()` refuse a root that grants any permission to group or others (read bits included) or is owned by another uid, and a root whose ancestor is owned by a third user or is writable by others without the sticky bit. Every operation re-checks the root and applies the owner-only rule to every existing directory it descends into, on the way to a `list`/`delete_prefix` prefix as well as below it. Directories are created `0700` and objects `0600` at creation. Every refusal names the path and the fix.

Writes go to a temporary sibling, `fsync`, rename, `fsync` of the directory and its ancestors. A failure before the rename removes the temporary; a failure after it (the directory sync) leaves the new, complete object rather than deleting an object that replaced the previous one. Directories a failed put created stay, empty and invisible to `list`, until `delete_prefix` removes them (removing them raced a concurrent put into the same directory, and missed failures inside the creation walk). Listings report only names that pass the key rule; temporaries, non-UTF-8 names and names with a backslash are skipped and still deleted. A put onto a key that is a directory is refused before the body is read; `get` of a file removed under it is `NotFound`. Every operation resolves its path with one component walk. `delete_prefix` leaves the directories above the prefix and treats an entry another deleter removed first as already gone, so two reconcilers retrying the same prefix do not fail each other; `list` skips entries that vanish mid-walk. `validate()` writes, syncs and removes a probe.

Consequence for operators, stated in the README and #396: a backup pickup agent (rsync, restic, borg) cannot read the tree as a member of the server's group; it runs as the server's user or as root. A root under a directory owned by a storage administrator or an NFS mount owned by `nobody` is refused at startup.

**S3 store.** Multipart above the configured part size (default 8 MiB, minimum 5 MiB) with bounded concurrency and at most 10,000 parts; a failure anywhere after `CreateMultipartUpload`, including a failed `CompleteMultipartUpload`, aborts the upload, and a drop guard aborts it when the put's future is dropped (a cancelled job). `delete_prefix` also aborts in-progress uploads under the prefix, which sweeps what a killed process left; the README recommends an `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` lifecycle rule as the backstop. Requests carry a 60 s attempt and 300 s operation timeout. Paginated listing that skips keys failing the key rule (console folder markers); `DeleteObjects` batches of 1000 over the raw listing, per-key errors surfaced (`AccessDenied` as `PermissionDenied`, keys without the store prefix). A key that fits the shared rule but exceeds S3's 1024-byte limit once the bucket prefix is added is refused as `InvalidKey`; a bucket prefix over 512 bytes is refused at `open`. Errors are reduced to code and service message (no request or credential material); `NoSuchBucket` and `NoSuchUpload` are not `NotFound`; transport errors display their source chain, so "dispatch failure" carries its cause. `validate()` lists one key under the prefix rather than calling `HeadBucket`, because a HEAD error has no body: a 403 keeps S3's code (`AccessDenied`, `InvalidAccessKeyId`, `SignatureDoesNotMatch`), a 404 names the missing bucket, a 301 the bucket's region. `open_with_interceptor` is a `test-util`-gated failure-injection seam.

**Configuration.** `BackupStoreConfig` models the `[backup.store]` table (`kind = "filesystem" | "s3"`, default filesystem) with `[backup.store.filesystem]` and `[backup.store.s3]`. The server will hold it under its own key rather than flatten it, because `deny_unknown_fields` does not survive `serde(flatten)`; only the section matching `kind` is read. The struct has no `Default`; the server supplies the default root.

**Dependencies and CI.** `aws-config` and `aws-sdk-s3` are pinned to the newest releases that build on the workspace `rust-version` (1.88); their transitive `aws-*`/`aws-smithy-*` crates are held in `Cargo.lock` at 1.88-compatible versions, and `.cargo/config.toml` sets the resolver's `incompatible-rust-versions = "fallback"` so a plain `cargo update` keeps them there. `test.yml` starts moto in server mode, runs the workspace with this crate excluded, then runs this crate with the S3 variables scoped to that step and `EXTENDDB_TEST_S3_REQUIRED` set, so the S3 suite fails rather than skips when the endpoint is missing. One shipped crate moves with them: `crc` 3.4.0 to 3.3.0, because `crc-fast` 1.9.0 (1.10.0 needs Rust 1.89) requires `crc ~3.3` and `sqlx-core` shares the one `crc`. The four licence notice files are regenerated; the `crc` line is the only content change. Both CI test steps use `--locked`.

## Why

#336 was approved with the filesystem store creating world-readable files under a permissive umask and with its S3 tests never executing in CI (design review of #348). Three adversarial review rounds on this PR then found: a traversable root still exposed permissive subdirectories; `list` and `delete_prefix` skipped the ownership check and followed a symlink planted above the prefix (an in-root alias made `delete_prefix` destroy another backup; an escaping link made it delete outside the root); a second deleter racing on the same prefix failed with ENOENT, which the design's reconciler contract forbids; the post-rename cleanup deleted an object that had replaced an older one; the S3 abort test never started a multipart upload; the 301 and 403 branches were untested; `NoSuchBucket` read as a missing object; and the lockfile did not build on the 1.88 toolchain CI tests. A fourth round found: a dropped or crashed put left its multipart upload open, and nothing could abort it; `validate` reported every misconfiguration as a bare "dispatch failure"; the 403 code the docs promised is not in a HEAD response; the failed-put skeleton cleanup raced a sibling put and missed failures inside the creation walk; listings could yield keys `get` refuses; the uid rule and the post-rename failure path had no test; pagination and per-key delete errors were untested; a sub-table `deny_unknown_fields` test tested the top level. The format PR (#394) needs the ETag and size from `put`.

## Testing done

`cargo test -p extenddb-backup-store`: 18 unit tests and 72 conformance tests (47 filesystem, 25 S3) pass against a tempdir and, with `EXTENDDB_TEST_S3_REQUIRED=1` and the endpoint pointed at moto 5.2.4, against moto; the same on `cargo +1.88.0 test --locked`. With `EXTENDDB_TEST_S3_REQUIRED=1` and no endpoint, every S3 test that needs one (22 of 25) fails with the intended message; the other three exercise `open` and transport errors against a closed port.

Filesystem tests cover: shared conformance (round trip, overwrite, empty body, listing and prefix rules, delete counts, invalid keys, multipart-sized bodies, failed-put cleanup, metadata agreement between put, head and list); 0600/0700 at creation; ten root modes with any group or other bit (0720, 0702, 0777, 1777, 0750, 0755, 0705, 0701, 0740, 0704) refused and 0700/0500 accepted; a world-writable parent and grandparent refused, a sticky one accepted, `validate` re-checking the ancestors (the third-uid cell needs a second uid and is noted); a permissive subdirectory refused by put, get, head, list and delete_prefix whether it is the prefix or above it, and nothing deleted; a root widened after open refused by every operation; symlinks: dangling at the destination, dangling in the parent chain, relative, chained, symlinked root, in-root directory and file aliases, aliases and escaping links above a `list`/`delete_prefix` prefix (refused, victim and outside tree untouched), links below the prefix removed without following; two concurrent `delete_prefix` calls both succeed and count every object once (5 rounds of 200 objects); temporaries hidden from every listing and still deleted; `delete_prefix("")` keeps the root usable; directory keys and keys through an object are not found; a failed put keeps the previous object; failed puts leave only empty directories, including a `NAME_MAX` failure inside the creation walk; a directory-sync failure after the rename keeps the new object (a `0300` parent); names failing the key rule hidden and deleted; the root replaced by a symlink refused. The two uid cells (a root, subdirectory or ancestor owned by another user) need a second uid; the test comment records the `unshare -Urm` check that covered them by hand.

S3 tests against moto cover: the shared conformance; the multipart abort path with a body that fails inside the third part and an interceptor counting exactly one `CreateMultipartUpload`; a failed `CompleteMultipartUpload` aborting the upload; a dropped put's upload aborted by the guard and an orphaned upload swept by `delete_prefix`; listing and deletion past one 1000-key page with a string-prefix sibling untouched; a per-key `DeleteObjects` denial; foreign keys (folder markers, backslashes) hidden and deleted; a 301 and a 403 with its error body via a response-rewriting interceptor (moto cannot produce them); a transport failure's cause; a missing bucket on `validate`, `get`, `list` and `put`; prefix plus key over 1024 bytes, and a prefix over 512 bytes, refused.

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p extenddb-backup-store --all-targets -- -D warnings -D clippy::pedantic   # 0 findings
cargo test --locked -p extenddb-backup-store                                              # 18 + 72 (S3 vs moto)
cargo +1.88.0 test --locked -p extenddb-backup-store                                      # 18 + 72
cargo +1.88.0 check --locked --workspace --all-targets
cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets                                            # stable
./devtools/generate-software-license-notices --check [--backend mongodb|cassandra]; ./devtools/generate-dev-license-notices --check
```

## Not changed here

- `list()` collects the filesystem walk into a Vec before streaming. The trait promises lexicographic order, which a directory walk cannot provide incrementally, and listings under the backup layout are small.
- The symlink TOCTOU is bounded by the ownership requirement, not closed; closing it needs `openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH)`, which std does not expose. The ancestor rule is checked at `open` and `validate` only.
- `head` on a missing bucket reads as the key being absent and on a denied one as code `unknown`: HEAD responses have no body; `validate` is the check that names the problem.
- A `.put-*.tmp` left by a killed process is removed only by a `delete_prefix` covering it; the reconciler's prefix deletion is that sweep.
- No consumer of the crate yet; the configuration PR wires `[backup.store]` into the server and the backup job PR calls the trait. The licence notices change materially then.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] All tests pass (`cargo test --workspace`)
- [x] Code is formatted (`cargo fmt --check`)
- [x] Clippy is clean (`cargo clippy -- -W clippy::pedantic`)
- [x] I have added or updated tests for new functionality
- [x] I have updated documentation if behavior changed
- [x] Breaking changes are noted below (if any)
- [x] If this changes the wire protocol, `Storage` trait, auth model, on-disk format, or public CLI surface, an RFC has been accepted or is linked below. Otherwise, an ADR captures the decision (link below).

ADR / RFC: #396, section 2. The `BackupStore` trait is internal to this series and has no implementors outside the crate.

## Breaking changes

None for users; the crate is not yet consumed. Operators who adopt the filesystem store later need a 0700 root under root- or server-owned ancestors; the README and #396 state the pickup-agent consequence. `.cargo/config.toml` is new to the repository and changes how `cargo update` picks versions for every crate (it prefers versions that build on 1.88).

items.title: Allow user namespaces in desktops for browser sandboxes
items.body:
An application that opens a link in a desktop with Google Chrome installed showed XFCE's "Failed to execute default Web Browser. Input/output error." Chrome now starts from every path, with its own sandbox.

## Cause

- Docker's default seccomp profile refuses `clone` and `unshare` with namespace flags to a container without `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, so Chrome cannot create the user namespace its sandbox starts in. Without `--no-sandbox` it aborts with "No usable sandbox!" and dumps core.
- The stock default browser goes `xdg-open` → `exo-open` → `debian-sensible-browser` → `x-www-browser` → `/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable`. That skips any `--no-sandbox` wrapper an image puts in `/usr/local/bin`, and exo reports the crash as an I/O error. Menu entries that name `/usr/bin` directly fail the same way.
- Making Chrome the default browser by hand only worked because XFCE then runs `google-chrome` from `PATH`, which hits the wrapper.

## Change

- Desktops are created with `--security-opt seccomp=desktop/seccomp.json`. The file is Docker's default profile (`github.com/moby/profiles/seccomp` v0.2.4, vendored by Docker Engine 29.9) with one rule appended that allows `clone` and `unshare`. Everything Docker reserves for `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, such as `mount`, `setns` and `bpf`, stays refused. The manager image already bundles `desktop/` as `DESKTOP_CONTEXT`.
- New setting `DESKTOP_USER_NAMESPACES` (default `true`). `false` keeps Docker's own default profile. It is added to `config.rs`, `.env.example`, both Compose manifests and `docs/INSTALLATION.md`. When the setting is on and the profile file is missing, startup fails and names the file.
- Tradeoff: code inside a desktop can reach more of the kernel through user namespaces. In exchange, browsers and Electron applications keep their sandbox instead of every image disabling it.
- `docs/USAGE.md`: the Chromium GPU command drops `--no-sandbox` and `--disable-gpu-sandbox`. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` explains how to follow a newer Docker profile.
- **Release note:** the default is `true`. Existing desktops keep the profile they were created with until a reset or a settings change recreates them.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clippy 0.1.99) and `cargo test --locked`: 90 passed, 2 of them new.
  - One pins the profile: the rule is present, `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` calls stay gated, and `clone3` still returns ENOSYS so glibc falls back to `clone`.
  - The other checks that `DESKTOP_USER_NAMESPACES=false` passes no `--security-opt`.
- `bun run test` (33 passed). The bridge tests (6 passed) ran on Linux in a throwaway container. Both Compose manifests were validated with `.env.example`, including the `images` and `https` profiles.
- `tests/integration.py` has a new check: `unshare --user` succeeds in a GPU desktop and `mount` inside it is refused. **The suite was not run** for this branch, at the maintainer's choice.
- **Live, on Docker 29.9.1 with throwaway desktops** from an XFCE image with Chrome 155 installed, GPU enabled:
  - With the stock profile, `xdg-open https://example.com` reproduced the exact dialog.
  - With `desktop/seccomp.json`, the same command opened Chrome from `/usr/bin` without `--no-sandbox`, and `chrome://sandbox` reported the namespace sandbox ("adequately sandboxed").
  - `gpu-run google-chrome --use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl --ignore-gpu-blocklist` showed hardware acceleration through `ANGLE (D3D12 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080))` with no sandbox flags. Chrome runs its GPU process unsandboxed on its own.
  - `unshare -Urm mount -t tmpfs` was refused.
- Not verified: Edge, Brave and Electron applications other than Chrome, the GNOME profile, and the WSL package rebuild. The package copies `.env.example` and `compose.ghcr.yml` unchanged.

items.title: fix(install.sh): run the smoke test from beside the install directory
items.body:
## What changed

`install.sh` runs its smoke test of the downloaded binary (`ai-memory --version`) from beside the install directory instead of from the temporary work directory.

- `install.sh`: the release is moved to `$lib_dir.new.$$` first, as the final step already did, and the binary runs from there. A binary that still fails is refused as before, the message now names the directory it was tried from (`the downloaded binary does not run from ~/.local/lib on this machine`), and the staged copy is removed. Nothing else in the sequence moves: checksum, member checks, unpack and the link are unchanged.
- `tests/install_sh.sh`: two cases. A working release installs with `TMPDIR` on a filesystem that refuses to execute files. The directory is borrowed, not mounted: `/run/lock` is a world-writable `noexec` tmpfs on Debian and Ubuntu, and a probe script that fails to run from a candidate proves the refusal, so the case needs neither root nor a user namespace and is skipped where no candidate refuses (macOS). A release whose binary exits non-zero is still refused, with the message naming the directory, installs nothing and leaves no `ai-memory.new.*` behind.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: one `### Fixed` entry.

## Why

Closes #1623

The smoke test ran the binary from `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ai-memory-install.XXXXXX"`. On a host whose `/tmp` or `TMPDIR` is mounted `noexec`, which the CIS Linux benchmarks list among the `/tmp` partition options, every `execve` of a file there fails with `EACCES`, the shell exits 126, and the script stopped with `the downloaded binary does not run on this machine`, with nothing installed. The release itself was fine: it would have run from `~/.local/lib/ai-memory`, where the script moved it a few lines later. `ai-memory upgrade` is not affected; it only checks that the archive holds the binary (`upgrade.rs` `ensure_extracted_binary`).

## Test plan

I did not run the gates locally; CI runs them on this PR. `tests/install_sh.sh` runs in the `native packaging assets` job on every pull request.

- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo tf` (or `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`)
- [x] Manual test: a throwaway `ubuntu-latest` workflow on my fork ran `tests/install_sh.sh` twice, in one run ([run 39875023590](https://github.com/viniciusdsandrade/ai-memory/actions/runs/39875023590)).
  - With the previous `install.sh` from `main` (a387263c) and the new test ([job](https://github.com/viniciusdsandrade/ai-memory/actions/runs/39875023590/job/120158415438)): `error: install from a noexec TMPDIR (/run/lock) refused: ... ai-memory install: error: the downloaded binary does not run on this machine`.
  - With this branch ([job](https://github.com/viniciusdsandrade/ai-memory/actions/runs/39875023590/job/120158415184)): `noexec TMPDIR case ran in /run/lock`, then `install.sh checks passed`. The runner mounts `/run/lock` as `tmpfs (rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,size=5120k)`, mode `1777`.

## Commit attribution

- [x] I verified the name and email on every commit in this PR and corrected
      any unintended identity before requesting merge. See
      [commit attribution guidance](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-attribution).

## Release impact

- [x] **Patch**: bug fix, no new surface
- [ ] **Minor**: additive (new flag/subcommand/MCP tool/config key,
      new agent harness or provider)
- [ ] **Major (breaking)**: on-disk format, removed/renamed surface, or
      breaking MCP schema change, called out in "What changed" above

- [x] The base branch matches: `main` for a patch, the standing feature
      branch (currently `release/3.3`) for minor or major work.
- [x] I checked that this does not redo something already on `main` or the
      feature branch, or fixed by a closed issue. `release/3.3` carries the same `install.sh` and `tests/install_sh.sh` as `main`.

## CHANGELOG (merge gate)

- [x] I added a `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry.
- [x] No default changes. The only visible difference for a release that works is that `~/.local/lib` and `~/.local/bin` are created before the smoke test rather than after it; both are the two directories the script's header already names as the ones it touches.

## Notes for reviewers

- The second test commit replaces the first one's mechanism. The first mounted a `noexec` tmpfs with `unshare -Urm`; GitHub's Ubuntu runners set `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`, so the case was skipped there ([run 39874804950](https://github.com/viniciusdsandrade/ai-memory/actions/runs/39874804950)). Borrowing `/run/lock` runs on the runner and on a stock Debian or Ubuntu box, with no root and no mount to clean up. The test prints whether the case ran or was skipped.
- The noexec case runs before the broken-binary control, so an installer without the fix fails on the user-visible symptom first.
- A home directory that is itself on a `noexec` filesystem still cannot run the binary; the message then names that directory, which is the real condition.
