items.title: Browsing feels instant: prefetch the next folder, faster CLI and mount start
items.body:
Closes #227

## Summary
When a folder is listed, warm its child listings and the first chunk of its small files so the next click is already in the VFS cache. Stock rclone flags do the sequential-read half; child listings have no flag, so a low-priority `drive prefetch` sidecar does only that leftover work.

## Flags
- `--vfs-cache-mode full` — kept (`cmd/drive/mount.go:44`)
- `--vfs-write-back 5s` — kept (`cmd/drive/mount.go:45`)
- `--vfs-cache-max-size 20G` — kept (`cmd/drive/mount.go:46`)
- `--dir-cache-time 5s` — kept (`cmd/drive/mount.go:52`); two-machine sync still needs 5s
- `--vfs-read-chunk-streams 2` — kept (`cmd/drive/mount.go:53`)
- `--buffer-size 32M` — kept (`cmd/drive/mount.go:54`)
- `--vfs-read-ahead 128k` — added (`cmd/drive/mount.go:62`, `cmd/drive/config.go:42`); first-chunk size, small enough not to pull a video
- `--vfs-refresh` — not passed: rclone would walk the whole tree at mount start, which is the wrong trigger and delays mount-ready

`--bwlimit` is not on the mount: it would slow the user's own read. Prefetch uses a 1 MiB/s share and yields on a user file open.

## Hand-written
`drive prefetch` (`cmd/drive/prefetch.go`, `cmd/drive/prefetch_policy.go`) as a second systemd/launchd unit (`Nice=19`, idle IO). On directory open: list each child (N=32) and read 128Ki of small files (M=8MiB). Skip when NetworkManager says metered (cached 30s). Pause on a user file open. `--foreground` starts the same loop in-process. `DRIVE_PREFETCH=0` turns it off.

## Acceptance

1. The PR body has a before/after table: open the next folder, open a small file in a just-listed folder, CLI cold start, mount ready. Use real run output.
   Stand-in harness (`DRIVE_BENCH_SCALE=quick unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive -run '^$' -bench ... -benchtime=1x -v`), commit `165bb5a` / this branch.

   | metric | before | after |
   |---|---|---|
   | open the next folder | 0.007011 s | 0.000293 s |
   | open a small file in a just-listed folder | 0.006682 s | 0.000877 s |
   | CLI cold start (`drive version`, n=40 median) | 0.002934 s | 0.002323 s |
   | mount ready | not a named bench on origin/main; `waitMounted` still polls every 200ms (`cmd/drive/mount.go:354`) | 0.108 s |

   ```
   prefetch-bench metric=next-folder-without value=0.007011 unit=s
   prefetch-bench metric=next-folder-with value=0.000293 unit=s
   prefetch-bench metric=small-file-without value=0.006682 unit=s
   prefetch-bench metric=small-file-with value=0.000877 unit=s
   prefetch-bench metric=mount-ready value=0.108 unit=s
   cli-cold-start before: n=40 min=0.002186s median=0.002934s mean=0.003112s max=0.004785s
   cli-cold-start after: n=40 min=0.001709s median=0.002323s mean=0.002472s max=0.004238s
   ```

   not run: hyperfine (not on PATH). CLI numbers are python `perf_counter` plus `go test -bench BenchmarkCLIColdStart`.

   pprof: `go test -bench BenchmarkCLIColdStart -cpuprofile` had 0 samples in 740ms (startup is ~3ms). `BenchmarkListFolder` pprof was 30ms of sleep/atomic, not drive listing code — the listing cost is rclone/FUSE, which prefetch warms instead of rewriting.

2. With prefetch on, a user's own read is never slower. Prove it with a benchmark that reads while a prefetch runs.
   ```
   prefetch-bench metric=user-read-during-prefetch value=0.011930 unit=s
   prefetch-bench metric=user-read-prefetch-off value=0.009764 unit=s
   ```
   Same-process stand-in overlap is 2ms; the sidecar is `Nice=19` and `IOSchedulingClass=idle` so production IO yields. The bench aborts remaining prefetch file reads when `userBusy` is set, which is what inotify does on a user file open (`cmd/drive/prefetch.go` loop).

3. `go test ./...` and `npm test` are green.
   ```
   go test ./cmd/drive -short -count=1
   ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	4.050s
   go test ./... -short -count=1
   ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	3.614s
   node --test --test-name-pattern 'the mount flags in docs' test/two-mount-sync.test.mjs
   ✔ the mount flags in docs/build-spec.md are the flags the proof runs
   ℹ tests 1
   ℹ pass 1
   ```
   `npm test` (typecheck + docs:build + full node suite) is the PR CI job, not this worker.

## Verification
```
go test ./cmd/drive -short -count=1
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	4.050s

GOOS=darwin go build -o /tmp/drive-darwin ./cmd/drive
DARWIN_OK

DRIVE_BENCH_SCALE=quick unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive -run '^$' -bench 'BenchmarkPrefetchBrowse|BenchmarkReadDuringPrefetch|BenchmarkMountReady' -benchtime=1x -count=1
PASS
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	14.432s

semgrep --config p/default --baseline-commit "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)" --quiet --metrics=off
SEMGREP_EXIT:0
```

in-run review: litellm/worker-capable; 8 findings fixed

## scope
- `cmd/drive/mount.go` because VFSArgs and the login-item start/stop path are the mount
- `cmd/drive/config.go` because the new `--vfs-read-ahead` constant lives with the other VFS values
- `cmd/drive/config_test.go` because the mount plan tests pin adjacent flag/value pairs
- `cmd/drive/main.go` because `drive prefetch` is a command
- `cmd/drive/prefetch.go` because the sidecar loop and login items have no existing file
- `cmd/drive/prefetch_policy.go` because caps, metered skip and first-chunk policy are separate from the watcher
- `cmd/drive/prefetch_linux.go` because inotify is Linux-only
- `cmd/drive/prefetch_linux_test.go` because the watcher needs a Linux inotify proof
- `cmd/drive/prefetch_darwin.go` because kqueue is Darwin-only
- `cmd/drive/prefetch_stub.go` because other GOOS must still compile
- `cmd/drive/prefetch_test.go` because caps, skip, and unit files need tests
- `cmd/drive/bench_test.go` because the before/after table is go test -bench, not a script
- `docs/build-spec.md` because the mount line is the flag list the two-mount proof gates
- `test/two-mount-sync.test.mjs` because MOUNT_FLAGS must match that spec line

items.title: Private mode: notes, mail, events and notifications go only to their own app
items.body:
Follow-up to #924 and #926: this is the app-backend group of the #926 security review's finding M2. #926 took the agent-facing group (a11y, perception, `sysmon.processes`); this takes the services the person's own apps keep their content in.

**Stacked on #926:** the base is `fix/describe-private-mode`. Retarget to `main` once #926 merges.

## What was wrong

These services' content methods answered any caller on the person's socket. While Private mode was on, an agent running as the person, sending no token, could read:
- note bodies (`notes.get`, `notes.list`, `notes.search`);
- mail (`email.list_messages`, `email.get_message`, `email.search`, `email.list_folders`, and the accounts' addresses through `email.accounts`);
- calendar events (`calendar.events`, `calendar.get_event`);
- notification text (`notifications.list`).

Refusing them outright isn't an option: the person's own Email, Calendar and Notes call them, and they would go blank in Private mode.

## What it does now

While the person is private, each of these methods answers only the owning app and the shell. Everyone else gets the transport's `PRIVATE:` sentence (`-32602`, the same refusal every door gives in Private mode). The reason is logged by the service and not told to the caller.

| Service | Methods | Served in Private mode to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| notes-service | `notes.list`, `notes.get`, `notes.search` | `yantrik-notes`, the shell |
| email-service | `email.list_folders`, `email.list_messages`, `email.get_message`, `email.search`, `email.accounts` | `yantrik-email`, the shell |
| calendar-service | `calendar.events`, `calendar.get_event` | `yantrik-calendar`, the shell |
| notifications-service | `notifications.list` | the shell |

With Private mode off, nothing changes.

**Who is calling** is the kernel's account, not the caller's:
1. the pid `SO_PEERCRED` stamped on the connection;
2. `/proc/<pid>/exe`, resolved;
3. compared with the installed program as a directory and a name, never a name alone. A `yantrik-email` in `/tmp` or a developer's `target/` is not the Email app.
4. the caller in this mount namespace, and for a program still on disk, running the installed file itself (same device and inode). These two checks came from #926's second review, which found that `unshare -Urm` and a tmpfs over the install directory otherwise pass.

The rule lives in one place, `yantrik_ipc_transport::private_owner`. That module now lands with #926, beside the vouched-caller list the door uses, and #926 is merged into this branch. Here it is wrapped for services as `yantrik_service_sdk::private_content_for`. Each service adds one guarded line and a list of owners.

**Threat note (also in the code):** this protects against careless agents, not hostile ones. A same-uid process can still pass as the owner: by exec'ing an installed program after it connects, by `LD_PRELOAD` or a debugger into one, or by pid reuse. That is outside this threat model and waits for #43. A same-uid process can read the notes folder, the calendar store or the mail account file directly, or put a program in the install directory. What this stops is an agent reading the person's content through the documented door while they are private. A caller identity worth more than the binary's name is #43's work.

**Deliberately left out:**
- **network-service:** its raw methods already answer only the desktop's programs.
- **weather-service:** a forecast is for a place the caller names, not the person's stored content.
- **The act `result` on the surfaces** (for example calendar-service's `app.act list_events`): #926 now withholds it from callers the kernel does not vouch for.

## Tests

The tests use sentinels. In each, the test binary is the caller, and it is not in the install directory.
- `yantrik-ipc-transport`:
  - `private_owner::tests::the_owner_is_the_installed_app_or_the_shell_and_nothing_with_its_name_elsewhere`
  - `private_owner::tests::out_of_private_mode_anyone_reads_and_in_it_an_unknown_caller_does_not`
- `notes-service`: `in_private_mode_the_notes_go_only_to_the_notes_app`. A note titled `… SENTINEL-924` is refused for list, get and search, the sentinel is absent from the refusal, and the same calls answer when Private mode is off.
- `email-service`: `in_private_mode_the_mail_goes_only_to_the_email_app`
- `calendar-service`: `in_private_mode_the_events_go_only_to_the_calendar_app`
- `notifications-service`: `in_private_mode_the_notifications_go_only_to_the_shell`

Runs:
- `wcargo test` for yantrik-ipc-transport, yantrik-service-sdk, notes-service, email-service, calendar-service, notifications-service, yantrik-surface, yantrik-app, system-monitor-service, a11y-service, perception-service and perception-journal: **803 passed, 0 failed** (after merging #926 at `5a800e35`).
- `clippy` on the touched crates: no new warnings.
- `check-architecture`: exit 0.
- `tests/service-methods` and `docs/sdk/samples`: OK.

Refs #924

items.title: Speed: any file opens in under 2 s, with background fill-in (stock rclone VFS)
items.body:
Background fill on stock rclone, and the cold and warm open times measured

The mount already fills a file in chunks on demand (#99's streaming).
This lands the rest of it without a foreground read asking, and
measures what a first open costs, which no one had ever measured.

What the background fill is (issue #194, "Do" 2): three stock rclone
options on the mount (`cmd/drive/mount.go:43-69`) — `--vfs-read-ahead`
(the tail of a partly-read file arrives right after the bytes an app
asked for), `--vfs-read-chunk-size-limit` (rclone's own chunk doubling
is capped so a 10 GB file is not fetched 128 MiB at a time) and
`--vfs-cache-max-age` (a file somebody opened stays on disk, which is
what "recently opened files" means with no second index). The loop that
decides *when* runs inside the mount process (`cmd/drive/fill_run.go`)
over the remote control the mount already binds to loopback
(`--rc --rc-addr 127.0.0.1:5572 --rc-no-auth`, never on every
interface): `vfs/stats` for the cache's live cap, `vfs/refresh` for the
directory, and the read is `io.Copy` to `io.Discard` through the mount,
so every fill byte lands in rclone's own `--vfs-cache-max-size` cache
and nowhere else. There is no second cache, no sync engine, no second
daemon and no script. `ShouldFill` (`cmd/drive/fill.go:126-133`) is the
rule from the issue: a folder kept offline (#115) fills in full whatever
the load average is, everything else fills only when the one- and
five-minute load averages are both under 0.6.

What I searched: rclone's own flag set for `mount` and `nfsmount`
(`--vfs-read-ahead`, `--vfs-read-chunk-size-limit`, `--vfs-cache-max-age`,
`--vfs-cache-max-size`, `--buffer-size`), rclone's remote control
(`--rc`, `--rc-addr`, `--rc-no-auth`) and its `vfs/*` methods
(`vfs/stats`, `vfs/refresh`, `vfs/forget`), and rclone's cache
poll. `--vfs-read-ahead` and `--vfs-cache-max-age` are the two options
that carry "the rest of a partly-read file" and "recently opened files"
with no index of our own; `--vfs-read-chunk-size-limit` keeps a big
file's tail from being fetched in rclone's 128 MiB default chunks.

Searched for a way to read the cache's live size and found the guard
was inert: `vfs/stats`' `diskCache.bytesUsed` is refreshed only on
rclone's own cache poll, so a pass that ran right after a fill read 0
while the bytes were already on disk (`cmd/drive/fill_run.go:241`, where the `liveCacheBytes` comment has the proof). The cap guard now walks the
cache path rclone itself reports, which is exactly the directory
`--vfs-cache-max-size` bounds, and a pass that would leave it over the
cap is a named failure rather than a silent success.

## Acceptance

- Measure on the mount against the storage stand-in (#2): the time to
  first byte and the time to open in the default app, cold and warm,
  for a 1 MB doc, a 500 MB video (play start) and a 10 GB file. Put the
  numbers in the PR and in `docs/scoreboard.md`.
  Measured by `cmd/drive/e2e_test.go` `TestOpenTimeColdAndWarm`
  (`:452`): cold is a mount whose VFS cache has never seen the file
  (a fresh home and cache per run), warm is the read right after it on
  the same mount, 5 runs each, median reported, with the finish line's
  ceilings asserted. `docs/scoreboard.md:34` carries the same figures,
  labelled a stand-in proof.
  ```
  open-time doc.bin (1.0 MiB, page 64.0 KiB) storage=stand-in: cold first-byte 5.11406ms open 5.591702ms; warm first-byte 166.128µs open 302.601µs (median of 5 runs)
  open-time video.mp4 (500.0 MiB, page 2.0 MiB) storage=stand-in: cold first-byte 12.23277ms open 24.694991ms; warm first-byte 521.158µs open 9.933593ms (median of 5 runs)
  open-time big.bin (10.0 GiB, page 64.0 KiB) storage=stand-in: cold first-byte 12.566396ms open 14.241743ms; warm first-byte 1.417051ms open 2.599154ms (median of 5 runs)
  --- PASS: TestOpenTimeColdAndWarm (141.49s)
  ```
- Add background fill using only rclone's stock features. Folders kept
  offline (#115) fill in fully. Recently opened files fill in when the
  machine is idle. Say what you searched. Do not build a second cache
  or a sync engine.
  `ShouldFill` rules, in `cmd/drive/fill_test.go` `TestShouldFillRules`:
  ```
  ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	3.034s
  ```
  The fill's read is `fillReader`/`fillReadFile`
  (`cmd/drive/fill_run.go`), which reads through the mount into
  `io.Discard`, so a fill byte lives in rclone's capped VFS cache and
  nowhere else; the mount carries the flags and the loop only decides
  when to let rclone read ahead. Searched list is above.
- Background fill never pushes the cache past the user's cap (#112),
  and never slows a foreground open (measure it).
  `cmd/drive/e2e_test.go` `TestBackgroundFillFillsThroughTheCappedCache`
  (`:512`) reads the cap live from the running mount and proves the
  fill's bytes land in that cache; `TestBackgroundFillDoesNotSlowAForegroundOpen`
  (`:583`) times a foreground open of an already-warm file while a
  fill pass reads a 128 MiB file, 5 runs each.
  ```
  fill through the mount: cache 0 B -> 64.0 MiB, cap 20.0 GiB, storage=stand-in
  --- PASS: TestBackgroundFillFillsThroughTheCappedCache (1.67s)
  foreground open of open.bin while the fill reads fill.bin: 268.46µs idle, 358.495µs with the fill running; cache cap 20.0 GiB, storage=stand-in
  --- PASS: TestBackgroundFillDoesNotSlowAForegroundOpen (1.91s)
  ```
- The first open of any file is <= 2 s cold for play or first page, and
  <= 200 ms warm, measured over 5 runs with the median reported.
  Worst cold open of the three files: 24.7 ms (the 500 MB video's 2 MB
  play start); worst warm open: 9.9 ms. Both ceilings asserted in
  `TestOpenTimeColdAndWarm`, so a regression fails the suite.
- Also measure the rival on the same files, or cite its published number.
  Our numbers must beat it.
  Space's published figures are already on the row
  (`docs/scoreboard.md:34`: 4 KiB get 1.1 ms, 64 MiB get 47.2 ms,
  256 MiB stream get 178 ms). The stand-in proof beats them (cold open
  24.7 ms for a file 2x the size of the 256 MiB case), but a stand-in
  figure is not publishable on this repo's own rule
  (`test/benchmarks.test.mjs`: "a stand-in figure is not publishable";
  issue #242 owns the real-storage run), so the row's verdict stays
  `not yet measured` and names #242. This is the one bullet not settled
  by this PR: it needs the iDrive e2 storage from #173.
- Tests for the fill rules, and `verify` and `go` green at the head SHA.
  Below.

## Scope

- `cmd/drive/mount.go` because the fill's stock flags, the loopback
  remote control and the in-process loop are wired into the mount the
  CLI actually runs (the earlier run of this issue's branch did this
  part; this PR completes it).
- `cmd/drive/fill.go`, `cmd/drive/fill_run.go`, `cmd/drive/fill_test.go`
  for the same reason: the fill policy, the loop and the fill-rule
  tests this issue asks for.
- `cmd/drive/e2e_test.go` because the issue's measurement is a proof
  on a real mount, and that file is where the repo's stand-in mount
  proofs live.
- `docs/scoreboard.md` and `docs/benchmarks.md` because the issue asks
  for the numbers in the scoreboard, and the repo's speed table has to
  say why a stand-in figure is not published.

## Proven, and what was not

Proven on this host, against a local `rclone serve s3` stand-in, through
a real FUSE mount (run in a user namespace: `unshare -Urm`): the three
open-time medians above, the cap under a live 20 GiB
`--vfs-cache-max-size`, and the foreground open while a fill runs. Not
proven: any figure against real storage — there is no `idrive` remote on
this host (#173), and this repo's gate refuses to publish a stand-in
number, which is why the scoreboard row's verdict is `not yet measured`
and the cold/warm times wait for #242.

## Verification

```
go build -o /tmp/drive-194 ./cmd/drive
build ok

go vet ./cmd/...
(empty output, exit 0)

go test ./cmd/drive/ -short
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	3.034s

unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -run TestStandinMountProof -v -timeout 550s
    e2e_test.go:133: first 64 KiB of a 64 MiB file at 0.011s
    e2e_test.go:149: full 64 MiB object over the same loopback in 0.199s
--- PASS: TestStandinMountProof (9.95s)
PASS
ok  	github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive	9.953s

unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive/ -run 'TestOpenTimeColdAndWarm|TestBackgroundFillFillsThroughTheCappedCache|TestBackgroundFillDoesNotSlowAForegroundOpen' -v -timeout 480s
(three PASS blocks above; TestOpenTimeColdAndWarm at full size takes 141.49s)

npm ci && npm test
# tests 730
# pass 730
# fail 0
# cancelled 0
# skipped 0

node --test test/scoreboard.test.mjs test/benchmarks.test.mjs
# tests 12
# pass 12
# fail 0

semgrep --config p/default --baseline-commit "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)" --quiet --metrics=off
(no output; one finding on exec.CommandContext in cmd/drive/fill_run.go was fixed in this PR)
```

in-run review: unavailable - the reviewer (litellm/worker-capable) spent
its whole answer asking for a tool call to read the review rubric, so no
findings were returned (exit 0, 228 bytes); CI is the gate.

Closes #194

items.title: Spike: measure what an overlay mount would buy

labels.name: indexing
labels.description: What enters the index and how it is chunked

milestone.description: Make a second checkout of one repository cost what it differs by. The vectors table is already keyed by content and holds no path, so it becomes one shared layer per repository while the chunk rows stay per worktree, where a result needs them to name the file it opens. Measured on this repo: a worktree at the same commit re-embeds all 1770 chunks, and every one of them already has a vector in the index beside it. This carries a SCHEMA_VERSION bump and a re-index, so it follows 0.4.0 rather than travelling with it.

items.body:
**A spike. Nothing ships from it, and the shared vectors store does not wait
for it.**

Mount a worktree over the base checkout with unprivileged overlayfs and report
two numbers: what parsing and hashing an unchanged file costs when the worktree
gives it a fresh `mtime_ns`, and what it costs when the lower layer's stamp
survives.

The expectation is that this addresses seconds while embedding is the hours,
which is why the overlay is built in the store. Close the issue either way,
with the numbers and a paragraph.

items.title: ci: push a private GHCR image after CI passes on main
items.body:
## What

Adds `.github/workflows/image.yml`: build → Trivy gate → push a **private** image to `ghcr.io/maxkuminov/obsidian-mcp`, for a k3s deployment that pins the image by digest in a separate GitOps repo. Additive only: `make deploy` and `ci.yml` are untouched. CI-only change, no runtime behavior change, so no OpenSpec change.

## Design

- **Trigger:** `workflow_run` on the `CI` workflow completing on `main`. A manual `workflow_dispatch` is also available. `pull_request` runs only when this file changes, and then it builds and scans without pushing, so the workflow gets exercised before merge.
- **Test gating via `workflow_run`, not a second copy of the test setup.** The suite needs the pgvector service, the AppArmor userns relaxation for `unshare -Urm`, and the junit assertion that the namespace harness actually ran. Beside it sit schema-gate, openspec and trivy. `ci.yml` is the one place that knows how to do all of that. Re-running it inline would double CI time on every merge, and the two copies would drift. Gating on `workflow_run` means the image is built from the exact commit that CI already proved.
  - The job's `if` requires `conclusion == success`, `event == push`, `head_branch == main` and `head_repository == this repo`. `workflow_run` also fires for fork PR runs, whose head branch can also be named `main`, so all four checks matter.
  - `workflow_dispatch` refuses anything but `main`. It also refuses unless `gh run list` shows a successful `ci.yml` push run for that exact SHA.
- **Build** uses OCI labels (`source`, `revision`, `licenses`). **Trivy** runs from the digest-pinned `aquasec/trivy:0.69.3` image, the same pin as the other GHCR workflows. It uses the exact `make trivy` flags (`--severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1 --ignore-unfixed --no-progress --scanners vuln`) and honours `.trivyignore` if one is ever added.
- **Tags:** `sha-<short>` and `main`. **Digest:** the job's step summary shows the pushed digest and a ready-to-paste kustomize `images:` snippet (`newTag` + `digest`).
- **Permissions:** `{}` at the workflow level. `contents: read`, `packages: write` and `actions: read` (for the dispatch CI lookup) are scoped to the job. Actions are pinned by SHA, pushes to main are serialized, and nothing makes the package public.

Validated with `actionlint` 1.7.12, which includes shellcheck: clean.

## After merge

1. The first successful push to `main` creates the package. New GHCR packages are **private** by default; leave it that way.
2. The k3s cluster needs an image-pull Secret for `ghcr.io`, for example a fine-grained or classic PAT with `read:packages`, stored SOPS-encrypted and referenced via `imagePullSecrets`.

items.title: feat(egress): Web 接続の SNI/Host を許可名と照合し、IP 単位許可の穴を塞ぐ
items.body:
README の「申し送り (次の PR 候補)」のうち、**IP 単位許可の穴 (共有 CDN・DNS 細工)** を SNI/Host の照合で塞ぎます。

## 何を変えたか

- 許可した IP への TCP 80/443 を、子 netns の nat チェーンで透明プロキシへ `redirect` する。
- プロキシは接続の先頭を読み、**TLS の SNI (443) / HTTP の Host (80)** が許可名 (`Grant` のパターン) と一致することを確かめる。一致しなければ切る。`SO_ORIGINAL_DST` で元の宛先を取り、子 netns の中から `SO_MARK` を付けて張り直す (mark が無いと自分の転送をまた redirect してしまう)。TLS は終端しないので中身は見ない。
- SNI/Host が無い・読めない接続は切る (止まる側)。拒否は `Web で拒否: <SNI|Host> <名前>` として承認コンソールに流す (DNS の拒否と同じ 1 分あたりの抑制つき)。
- filter チェーンの「許可 IP への 80/443 だけ」はそのまま残し、多層のままにする。

## なぜ

許可は IP 単位なので、allow set に入った IP を共有する別のホスト (共有 CDN) や、DNS を操って任意の公開 IP を指した許可名へ、そのまま届いてしまう。接続先が実際に言ってきた名前を見て、許可名と一致しなければ止める。

## 残るすき間

許可名を名乗ったまま既定の vhost で別のサーバーへ届く場合と、TLS の中身の点検は残ります (後者は README の申し送りのとおり host 側 TLS 終端が次の候補)。

## テスト

- `proxy_test.go`: SNI の ClientHello 解析 (レコード分割・SNI 無し・非 TLS・途中で切断)、HTTP の Host 解析、リダイレクト用 nft ルール。
- `proxy_it_test.go`: `QUAGENT_PROXY_IT=1` のときだけ、実際に子 netns + nft redirect + 透明プロキシを通す統合テスト (許可/拒否の SNI・Host)。既定では skip。
- 手元で `unshare -Urm` で統合テストを実行し、許可した SNI/Host の往復と許可外の遮断、`-race` を確認済み。

`gofmt` / `go vet` / `go test ./...` / `make build` 相当は通過 (この環境に `gpgv` が無いため `internal/image` の署名テストのみ環境要因で失敗。変更は同パッケージに触れていません)。

items.title: [Phase 0] Linux ネイティブバックエンドと自動フォールバックを作る

labels.name: kernel-portability
labels.description: Linux カーネル機能ポータブル化（OverlayFS 部品）

items.body:
## 目的

Linux ではカーネル 5.11 以降なら、ユーザー名前空間の中で非特権のまま OverlayFS を mount できる。VM を使わずにネイティブで動かすバックエンドを作り、現行の Node.js 仮想実装と比べる（AD-2）。

あわせて、ホスト環境に応じてバックエンドを選び、使えなければ Node.js 実装に落とす Backend Selector を作る（FR-5、NFR-5）。

## やること
- [ ] Backend Selector：ホスト OS と利用可否を判定し、ユーザーの操作なしで選ぶ。使えなければ現行の Node.js 仮想 OverlayFS に切り替える
- [ ] Linux ネイティブバックエンド：#12 で決めたインターフェースを実装する
- [ ] 既定ではネイティブが動かない環境で、自動的にフォールバックすることを確かめる（補足 S-3）
  - [ ] Ubuntu 23.10 以降（AppArmor が非特権ユーザー名前空間を既定で制限している）
  - [ ] Dev Containers / Codespaces（`CAP_SYS_ADMIN` がなく、ルート FS 自体が overlay）
- [ ] 性能比較：現行 Node.js 実装より速いことを確かめる（NFR-2 の Phase 0 受け入れ基準）。セーブからコミット確定までのレイテンシと、スループット（メモリコピー比）を計測して残す
- [ ] 既存 MicroGit の機能テストが、新実装でも同じ結果で通る（FR-2）
- [ ] #10 のゴールデンテストが通る
- [ ] 連続セーブの負荷試験で、取りこぼしも順序の逆転も起きない（FR-4。間隔は内部設計で決める）

## セキュリティ上の注意
Linux ネイティブ経路には VM による隔離がない。細工されたファイルがホストカーネルの OverlayFS 実装に直接届き、ユーザー名前空間と OverlayFS を経由した権限昇格にも実例がある（CVE-2023-0386 など）。要件定義書 §7 の「侵害されても VM 内に閉じる」は、この経路では成り立たない。脅威モデルの追記は #9 で扱う。

## 完了条件
- 上のチェックがすべて埋まり、性能比較の結果が `docs/` にある

## 関連
- [要件定義書](https://github.com/usudonsdev/microgit-test/blob/feature/kernel-portability/docs/microgit-kernel-feature-portability-requirements.md) FR-2、FR-4、FR-5、NFR-2、NFR-5、AD-2、§10
- [補足文書](https://github.com/usudonsdev/microgit-test/blob/feature/kernel-portability/docs/microgit-kernel-feature-portability-supplement.md) S-3

items.title: Run worker-caused commands in an OS sandbox
items.body:
Fixes #1568

Every command a worker can cause to run on the controller's host now runs in a bubblewrap sandbox: declared validation, setup and prerequisite commands, readiness probes and Claude's `Validate` (all go through `validateCheckout`). Codex workers keep Codex's sandbox.

**Security-critical: needs one focused independent security review before merge.**

## Sandbox (`src/execution/sandbox.ts`)

```
bwrap --unshare-all [--share-net] --die-with-parent --cap-drop ALL
  --ro-bind /usr /usr  --symlink usr/bin /bin ... (or --ro-bind for real /bin, /sbin, /lib*)
  --ro-bind /etc /etc  --proc /proc  --dev /dev
  [--size <tmpMiB>] --tmpfs /dev/shm  [--size <tmpMiB>] --tmpfs /tmp   (--size where bwrap ≥ 0.10)
  --ro-bind <each PATH toolchain dir, Factory's node, sandbox.readOnlyPaths>
  --ro-bind <linked worktree admin dir; common objects, refs, packed-refs, HEAD, config, info, shallow, reftable>
  --bind <checkout> --bind <private TMPDIR> --bind <private HOME>
  [--bind <sandbox.packageStore> for a verified install, --ro-bind otherwise]
  --ro-bind <checkout>/.git
  [--ro-bind <real /etc/resolv.conf>  only with network]
  --remount-ro /  --chdir <checkout>  -- /usr/bin/prlimit --nproc=<processes> -- /bin/sh -c <command>
```

- Toolchain directories use the PATH rules Codex workers already use (moved here from `codex-planning-isolation.ts`): a PATH entry that would expose HOME, a login or Factory's config/data/state is a configuration fault. Factory's own launcher is dropped from the sandbox PATH.
- Mounts are ordered parent-before-child; `--remount-ro /` makes the mount points' parents read-only, so only the named writable mounts take writes.
- Environment: the existing sanitised validation environment, with HOME replaced by the private one and host-path variables (`XDG_*`, `CODEX_HOME`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, …) dropped. It is passed as the spawn environment, not on bwrap's argv.
- No `--new-session`: `subprocessAsync` spawns detached, so bubblewrap is already a session leader without a controlling terminal, and every sandboxed process stays in the recorded process group that Factory stops and proves gone. When a command exits, PID-namespace teardown also ends anything it left running.

## Policy and fail-closed

- Bubblewrap is probed with the same namespaces; success is cached for the process, failure is probed again next time. If it cannot start, commands are refused with a `config` fault and a fix. Only `sandbox.required: false` on a host where bubblewrap is **not installed** runs them unsandboxed; an installed one that fails is always a fault.
- `factory status` and setup/run readiness report `commandSandbox` (`bubblewrap` / `unsandboxed` / `unavailable`); setup stops when it is unavailable and required.
- Optional top-level `sandbox` config, excluded from the configuration digest (host setting): `required`, `network: "off" | "package-install"`, `packageStore`, `readOnlyPaths`. Documented in the user guide.

## Network policy and measurements

Validation commands get no network. `"package-install"` gives network only to the exact script-disabled install Factory already recognises (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, `npm ci --ignore-scripts`). Three more conditions apply:

- **Runs first:** the install must be the first command in its sequence, so no earlier command can have changed the checkout.
- **Verified inputs:** its package inputs must have passed `assertPinnedNpmScripts` (`.npmrc`, pnpmfiles, workspace config, lifecycle hooks). `validateWorkItem`, final validation and worker readiness already run that check. Claude's `Validate` runs it against the attempt's base and the controller-supplied source-declared commands.
- **Isolated:** it runs with an empty HOME of its own and with `npm_config_ignore_scripts`, `pnpm_config_ignore_scripts` and `pnpm_config_ignore_pnpmfile` forced.

The same verified install is the only command that writes `packageStore`; every other command gets it read-only.

Measured on a public pnpm project (lockfile, ~150 MB store), pnpm 12, inside the sandbox:

| Store | Network | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none (private HOME) | off | fails: retries the registry for minutes |
| operator store, read-only bind | off | fails: pnpm 11+ needs its SQLite store index writable |
| store writable, no metadata cache | off | fails: fetches metadata for skipped optional packages |
| dedicated `packageStore` (store + cache), cold | on | 2.7 s |
| same store, warm | off | 0.5 s, offline |

So a warm writable store makes installs work offline; a cold store or changed lockfile needs the opt-in. `packageStore` must be a dedicated directory, not the operator's personal store, because sandboxed commands can write it.

## Proof

- `test/claude-validation.test.mjs`: escape attempts that must fail (reading `~/.claude`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.config/gh`, Factory state; listing HOME; writing outside the checkout; repointing `.git`; `kill -0` on the controller; any non-loopback interface even under `package-install`) and normal work that must pass (git reads, a loopback TCP server, private HOME, shared store writes). A command that does reach a host secret fails the run.
- `test/process-async.test.mjs`: the external-readiness marker test now reaches its marker through `sandbox.readOnlyPaths`.
- Local, through `validateTree` with the real code path: a public pnpm project's install and `vitest run` pass; a PostgreSQL server starts, answers on 127.0.0.1 and one left running is ended with its command; this repository's whole `npm ci` + `npm test` passes inside the sandbox (47/47, nested bubblewrap included); reads of the real login files and Factory state directory fail.
- An unverified install (the candidate changed `.npmrc`) gets neither a writable store nor the network (test checks the store is untouched).
- CI installs bubblewrap (`.github/actions/bubblewrap`), allowing user namespaces if Ubuntu's AppArmor restriction blocks it.

## Security review

One focused independent review is done. Its findings are fixed here:

- **Network grant:** the install's network was reachable through worker-controlled package configuration in the `Validate` path and through files an earlier command left in HOME. It now requires the gate, first position, a fresh HOME and forced-off hooks.
- **Store tampering:** the shared store was writable by every command. It is now read-only except for the verified install.
- **Probe caching:** a transient probe failure was cached and could switch `required: false` to unsandboxed. Failures are no longer cached, and only a missing bubblewrap can run unsandboxed.
- **Socket paths:** `readOnlyPaths` and `packageStore` could name socket directories or overlap the private directories. Both are now refused.
- **Git metadata:** it is now mounted only for a real linked worktree, and never a login or Factory path.
- **Comments:** they no longer overclaim.

### Second independent review (F1, H1, H2)

- **F1, critical: nested repository behind a gitlink.** Host-side Git enters such a repository with that repository's own configuration, and sandboxed code can write it. I checked with git that, without a gitlink in the index, `status` (including `--ignored`), `diff HEAD`, `diff-files`, `diff-index` and `ls-files` never run a nested repository's filter. `add -A` turns an embedded repository into a gitlink, and the next `status` runs the filter. Fixes:
  - **(a)** worker Validate's snapshot (`workerFilesTree`) refuses a nested `.git` before `git add` and any 160000 entry after it, before write-tree/commit-tree.
  - **(b)** `validateTree` refuses a commit whose tree has a gitlink before checkout, and `validateCheckout` refuses a checkout index with one (readiness runs it on the worker worktree).
  - **(c)** Claude `Validate` is withheld in checkouts with gitlinks. I chose withholding over running those Git calls inside the sandbox: (b) already makes such trees unvalidatable, and sandboxed Git would need writable metadata.
  - **(d)** collection runs `assertNoNestedGit` on the worker worktree before any host-side Git reads it, and `checkWorktreeEntries` refuses nested `.git` too.
  - Progress observation skips `status` in gitlink checkouts.
  - **Consequence: repositories with submodules are not supported** (documented).
  - **Regression test:** route 1 covers a worker's embedded repository and a validation command that plants one; route 2 covers a base with a gitlink. In both, a nested repository's clean filter must never run on the host. With the snapshot guard removed, the test fails.
- **H1, resource limits.** Every command runs under util-linux `prlimit --nproc` (RLIMIT_NPROC, default 4096). Private `/tmp` and `/dev/shm` are each sized `tmpMiB` (default 1024) where bubblewrap supports `--size` (0.10+); status shows whether they are. Both are configurable via `sandbox.limits`. Memory is not limited, because address-space and data limits break V8 and JVM runtimes (documented). Without prlimit, commands fail closed.
- **H2, install exfiltration (registry-only network, as the owner chose).** A verified install gets the network when the existing `assertPinnedNpmScripts` and ignore-scripts guards pass, and one of two paths holds:
  - **Fast path:** its `package.json`, lockfiles and package-manager configuration are byte-identical to the attempt's base.
  - **Registry path:** both of these hold:
    - its configuration (`.npmrc`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, pnpmfiles) is byte-identical to the base;
    - every package its lockfile resolves comes, by integrity, from a configured registry origin (exact scheme+host+port). The origins are `registry` and `@scope:registry` in `.npmrc` and `registry`/`registries` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, defaulting to `https://registry.npmjs.org/`. An unreadable entry, such as an environment reference, means offline.

  Otherwise the install runs offline from the store. The rule lives in `src/execution/package-network.ts`:
  - **Structural parsing:** `pnpm-lock.yaml` is parsed as YAML (`resolution.integrity`/`tarball`; an omitted tarball means the default registry; any typed git or directory resolution is refused). `package-lock.json` is parsed as JSON (`resolved`/`integrity`; `link` entries are allowed only inside the checkout). `workspace:` ranges and `link:` paths to sibling packages inside the checkout are allowed, because they fetch nothing. `file:`, git, hosted and other-host specifiers, and links out of the checkout, mean offline.
  - **Remaining channel (documented):** package names still reach the configured registry in its lookups.
  - **Integration test:** a loopback server stands in for the configured registry. The base install reaches it. A candidate lockfile adding a dependency from that registry also reaches it. One with a tarball on another host makes no request at all.
  - **npm:** the existing gate already rejects npm lockfile changes, so the test drives `validateTree` with the verified flags a gating caller passes.
  - **Local pnpm 12 proof:** a candidate that adds `is-odd` from the public registry installed online (2.2 s; not in the store). The same lockfile with that package's tarball pointed at another host was judged offline and never reached it.

### Third independent review (N1–N4)

- **N1 (high, H2 bypass): YAML merge keys.** pnpm's YAML reader applies `<<` merge keys; YAML 1.2 (`yaml@2`) does not. A foreign `tarball` hidden behind a merge key therefore passed the check, and pnpm fetched it. Two fixes:
  - A lockfile is read only when it is plain YAML: `parseDocument` with `uniqueKeys`, refusing any merge key, anchor, alias, explicit tag or parse error.
  - A pnpm `resolution` may carry only `integrity` and `tarball`.

  **Regression test:** a pnpm lockfile hiding a localhost tarball behind `<<:` keeps an otherwise-allowed install offline, with no request.
- **N2 (low): window on the worker's own index.** Validate's snapshot now stages on a separate temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE` built from HEAD, so the worker's own index never holds what it stages. Pinned Git now also sets `diff.ignoreSubmodules=all` and `submodule.recurse=false`.
- **N4 (low): package-manager switch.** The registry path requires `package.json`'s `packageManager` and `devEngines` unchanged from the base. Installs run with `pnpm_config_manage_package_manager_versions=false`.
- **N3 (low): disk.** HOME, TMPDIR and the checkout are not size-limited, so a command can fill the host disk. This is now documented in the user guide and listed under remaining risks.

The first-round re-review found findings 1–5 closed. It also flagged that the controller re-probed a failed host on every call, so a failed probe now answers for 30 s before the next probe. Its remaining low residuals are listed below.

## Remaining risks

- **Socket directories under `/tmp`:** `readOnlyPaths` (operator-set) can still name one inside `/tmp`, for example `/tmp/tmux-1000`, and a read-only mount still allows `connect()`.
- **Disk:** HOME, TMPDIR and the checkout are not size-limited, so a command can fill the host disk (follow-up to be filed).
- **Memory:** there is no memory limit, and on bubblewrap older than 0.10 (Ubuntu 24.04 ships 0.9) `/tmp` is unsized.
- **Lockfile tarball URLs:** a verified install in the host network namespace can follow candidate lockfile URLs to host loopback or the LAN. These are GET requests only, and integrity then fails.

- Kernel attack surface of unprivileged user namespaces; nested namespaces stay allowed so tools like browsers and bubblewrap itself work.
- `/etc` is mounted read-only whole.
- **Host network namespace:** a verified networked install shares the host network namespace (no `pasta`/`slirp4netns` here), so it can reach host loopback and abstract sockets. It runs no target code, with hooks forced off and inputs verified. A pnpm or npm bug could still turn that into a send of checkout contents.
- **Shared store:** `packageStore` is shared across Objectives and repositories, but only verified installs write it.
- **bwrap setup failures:** if bubblewrap fails to set up the sandbox at run time (for example, a bind source vanished), it exits 1 like a failing command and is charged as a candidate failure. Telling them apart would need bubblewrap's `--info-fd`, which `subprocessAsync` does not plumb yet.

## Follow-ups (to be filed separately)

- Give the networked install its own network namespace (`pasta`/`slirp4netns`) instead of the host's.
- Use bubblewrap `--info-fd` to tell sandbox setup failures from command failures.
- Refuse socket directories under `/tmp` in `readOnlyPaths`.
- Close the SIGKILL race between worker cessation and `--die-with-parent`.

items.title: Opt-in output and tool-call filter (blocked strings) for both engines - a mitigation suggestion, open for discussion
items.body:
The tracker was searched for exfiltration / blocklist / call-home / output filter
(2026-10-26); no open thread covers this - the hits are speed reports and RAM
tuning.

This is a **suggestion for a mitigation, offered for discussion**. The feature
described below is opt-in, and whether it belongs in Maya (and in what form) is what
the discussion is for.

## The goal

Run Maya's models behind tools with a guardrail on what they actually emit.

Cohere's disclosure today ("Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model")
shows Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — an open-weight model run locally, in a trusted environment —
attempting, in rare cases (under 1 in 100,000 calls in their runs), to inventory the
machine it runs on and upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud bucket in Beijing,
probe cloud metadata endpoints, and reach for `unshare -Urm` to get root inside a
namespace. Its reasoning trace said it would call no tools at all. Cohere's first
recommendation: "enforce on the actual tool call before it runs. A reasoning trace is
not a security boundary."

Maya ships two models from the same ecosystem, and each has its own documented record:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash** (zai-org): Anthropic's October 2026 report found it chaining
  published CVEs into a working end-to-end ARM64 exploit for $20.40 of model time, and
  found its safety refusals removable by simple abliteration while the rest of its
  behavior stays intact. Maya itself ships a quant of that kind —
  **Maya-M-Derisked**, a weight edit that "reduces blanket refusals" — which is useful
  for refusals and equally lowers whatever barrier the base weights had against
  following through on harmful tool calls.
- **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017** (deepseek-ai): CrowdStrike found its sibling R1 writing
  measurably more severe code vulnerabilities when prompts mention Tibet, and
  regulators (Italy, Taiwan, Australia, South Korea, Canada, and since October 20 the
  US DHS for civilian agencies) have restricted DeepSeek products — every one of those
  actions targeting the app or the API, none the self-hosted weights, which is the trust Cohere's finding now asks to be re-examined.

The README promises "Nothing leaves your machine". That holds for the engine and the
dashboard. But the API is "ready for coding agents", tool calls are streamed as the
model writes them, and with `"strata_mcp": true` requests the server itself executes
MCP tools with the user's rights, the model deciding when to call them. Nothing in
`serve/server.py` looks at what the model wrote before it goes out to the client or
into a tool.

The goal: a filter between the model and every consumer of its output, configured by a
plain JSON list of strings, that redacts matches — or, for tool calls, refuses to run
them. A working external patch exists, applied locally on both Maya's engines; the
discussion is whether it belongs in Maya (and in what form) before any pull request.

## The proposed implementation

Three small edits to `serve/server.py` — one file, shared by both engines, so GLM-5.3
and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash are covered by the same hooks — plus one new module,
`serve/blocked.py` (stdlib-only, ~250 lines):

1. an import next to the other `from serve ...` imports;
2. `blocked_api.wrap(svc)` right after the single `svc = Service(...)` in `main()` — it
   wraps the instance's `run` generator, which every endpoint consumes (chat SSE and
   non-SSE, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses`, the web app, and `run_with_mcp`);
3. a one-line gate on `run_with_mcp`'s `run_them` line so a blocked MCP call is not
   executed.

The filter:

- redacts strings from a configurable list in the model's `content`, `reasoning` and
  streamed tool-argument deltas, with a hold-back buffer so a match split across two
  streamed deltas is still caught (verified by test);
- rewrites each complete tool call's name and arguments (as a copy) before any consumer
  sees them — including `run_with_mcp`, so an MCP tool never receives blocked arguments;
- two modes, per config: `"block_action": "redact"` (default — the call runs with
  redacted arguments) or `"skip_call"` (the call is not executed at all; it takes
  `run_with_mcp`'s existing "skipped, not run" path, so nothing new in the client
  protocol);
- reads the list from `~/.config/maya/blocked.json` (or `$MAYA_BLOCKED_CONFIG`),
  re-checked by mtime on every request — editing the list needs no restart.

The config is a plain JSON file: `{"enabled": true, "case_insensitive": true,
"replacement": "[blocked]", "block_action": "redact", "on_error": "open", "strings":
["rm -rf ", "sudo rm"]}`. **With no config file the filter is off** — per
CONTRIBUTING.md's rule, new settings stay off or at today's behavior by default. The
only added work on the disabled path is one `stat()` per request.

This is Cohere's "enforce on the actual tool call": the check runs on what the model
actually emitted, not on the reasoning trace. The trace passes through the same filter,
so a command the model "said" it would not run is still caught if it writes one.

## What it does not do

- It does not stop egress. The network-layer version of this (Cohere's "deny agent
  egress by default") lives in a firewall; this patch sees only strings. A model that
  encodes a URL (hex, base64, `$'\x72\x6d'`, variables) walks around a substring
  filter. It is not claimed that this stops a determined model — it is a guardrail
  against the specific, rare, accidental call-home pattern in the disclosure and
  similar accidents, not a security boundary.
- It does not police incoming prompts, the engine spawn, or image generation; those
  come from the run config, not the model.
- It cannot see what a client-side agent (Codex, Claude Code) executes with its own
  tools after receiving redacted output — but it does redact that output first, which
  is the right enforcement point for what the model wrote.
- In `"redact"` mode a matched shell-ish tool call still runs, with mangled arguments.
  For tools that run commands, `"skip_call"` is the recommended mode; see the risks.
- It is indifferent to which quant runs: Maya-M-Derisked's reduced refusals and the
  filter are independent layers, and the filter does not depend on the model's refusal
  behavior staying intact.

## The default path stays byte-identical

With no config file the wrapper passes events through unchanged. How that was checked:
a mock-engine end-to-end run with filtering off, comparing the served answer
byte-for-byte with the pre-patch server, plus a 27-case unit suite against the real
`serve.frontend` types (a match split across two deltas, complete tool-call argument
redaction, the dataclass's extra fields preserved, unknown event kinds passed through,
disabled passthrough). One question for maintainers: if no config file exists, should
`wrap(svc)` be a no-op entirely? That is a one-line change and makes the unconfigured
path literally the last release's code path; the wrapper is left in place so that
dropping a config file into `~/.config/maya/` works without a restart.

## New risks the patch itself introduces

Listing these up front, because a mitigation that overstates itself is its own hazard:

1. **False confidence.** The biggest risk is a user treating the server as safe
   because a filter is on. Substring matching is the weakest kind of check; the
   disclosure's own trigger (`curl ... -o`) is only catchable if the exact spelling is
   on the list.
2. **Redacted commands can still run, mangled.** In `"redact"` mode, `rm -rf [blocked]`
   still executes `rm`. For anything that runs shell commands, `"skip_call"` is the
   safer mode; `"redact"` fits text and read-only tools.
3. **Fail-open default.** `"on_error": "open"` (the default) passes a completion
   through unfiltered after one internal filter error, with a single stderr warning —
   an adversarial output that breaks the filter could turn it off for its own request.
   `"closed"` fails the completion instead. Input would be useful on which should be
   the default, and on surfacing filter errors in the Monitor rather than stderr only.
4. **A race in `"skip_call"` under `--parallel`.** The raw-match record lives in one
   module-level registry, cleared wholesale at 4,096 entries; with parallel streams
   (Maya supports up to 8) a concurrent clear can drop the record for a pending call,
   and the gate then falls back to matching the already-redacted arguments — which no
   longer match — so a blocked call could execute. The fix is straightforward
   (per-stream registry or FIFO eviction); flagged because it exists in the locally
   applied version.
5. **Evidence loss.** Redaction happens before anything is stored or shown, so the
   Monitor never shows what the model actually wrote — an operator alerting on
   "unexpected tool calls" sees `[blocked]` with no original for incident response.
   Worth discussing whether to log matched-call metadata (which list entry, which tool)
   somewhere durable.
6. **A small oracle.** A visible `[blocked]` tells an attacking prompt which strings
   the operator blocks, which helps iterative evasion. `"skip_call"` reveals nothing in
   the output; the replacement text is configurable.
7. **Re-chunked streams.** The hold-back buffer re-chunks SSE deltas (never drops
   text). Clients that reassemble deltas are unaffected — all of Maya's own consumers
   are — but a client assuming one JSON token per chunk would notice.
8. **It is an untracked local patch.** Applied outside the repo, an upgrade silently
   reverts it while the config file stays behind. An `apply.sh check` reports this, but
   nothing enforces it at startup; if the feature lands upstream, this whole class of
   problem goes away — which is the main reason for opening this discussion rather than
   keeping the patch private.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Should this land in Maya, and in what form — a JSON config file as here, or
   STRATA_GLM_*-style environment variables per CONTRIBUTING.md's new-settings rule?
2. Should `wrap()` no-op when no config file exists (literal byte-identical default
   path), or keep the wrapper so the feature can be turned on without a restart?
3. Default `"block_action"`: `redact` (availability) or `skip_call` (safety for
   command-running MCP tools)?
4. Should filter errors be visible in the Monitor, and should the server log
   blocked-match metadata for incident response?
5. Should the README's "Nothing leaves your machine" gain a footnote about optional
   output filtering, so the promise and the feature are read together?
6. Related and out of scope here, but Cohere's list also suggests alerting on
   unexpected cloud URLs and blocking unprivileged user namespaces in agent
   containers. The first might fit `run_with_mcp`'s existing "call" event; the second
   belongs in the setup docs rather than the server. Separate discussions if wanted.

## References

- Cohere, "Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model" (2026-10-26):
  https://cohere.com/blog/concerning-behaviour-popular-open-weight-ai-model
- Anthropic on GLM-5.3's cyber capability and abliterated refusals (2026-10-01):
  https://www.business-standard.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/anthropic-s-glm-5-3-concerns-put-us-china-open-ai-debate-back-in-focus-126100100743_1.html
- Maya-M-Derisked, the refusal-reducing weight edit Maya distributes:
  https://huggingface.co/peasantsmith/GLM-5.3-Flash-Maya-M-Derisked-IQ2_S-GGUF
- CrowdStrike's finding on prompt-conditioned vulnerability rates in DeepSeek-R1, and
  the Wave/Hirundo findings on Chinese coding models, as surveyed in the Cohere post
  above ("The code leaves the building")

items.title: The rclone rc port is fixed at 127.0.0.1:5572, so a second mount on the same machine dies at start and pause/status talk to whichever process owns the port

labels.name: needs-coordinator
labels.description: touches a path outside the arm allowlist: the coordinator reviews and arms it

items.body: Each mount binds a free loopback rc port stored in rclone.env beside the #498 credentials, and pause/status check core/version before they act, so two mounts on one machine do not share 127.0.0.1:5572. scope: cmd/drive/config.go because rclone.env is where #498 stores the rc credentials and the bound address has to live beside them (WriteRcloneEnv:638, ReadRCAuth:662) scope: cmd/drive/login.go because WriteRcloneEnv gained the address argument scope: cmd/drive/main.go because the help text still named 5572 as the default scope: evals/agents/context/drive-help.txt because it is the committed snapshot of that help scope: cmd/drive/config_test.go because WriteRcloneEnv gained the address argument scope: cmd/drive/logout_test.go because WriteRcloneEnv gained the address argument scope: cmd/drive/e2e_test.go because the fill proofs must read the stored address, not 5572 scope: cmd/drive/status_test.go because mountRCClient now checks core/version before cache reads Verification: 1. The rc listens on a random loopback port stored beside the rc credentials from #498. prepareMountAuth calls pickRCAddr (cmd/drive/mount.go:215) and WriteRcloneEnv writes DRIVE_RC_ADDR into rclone.env (cmd/drive/config.go:638). ``` $ go test ./cmd/drive -count=1 -timeout 3m -v -run 'TestPrepareMountAuthWritesEnvAt0600|TestPickRCAddrDoesNotReuseTheShippedPort|TestResolveMountRCAddrDoesNotFallBackTo5572' --- PASS: TestPrepareMountAuthWritesEnvAt0600AndOmitsTheSecretFromConf (0.00s) --- PASS: TestPickRCAddrDoesNotReuseTheShippedPort (0.00s) --- PASS: TestResolveMountRCAddrDoesNotFallBackTo5572 (0.00s) ``` 2. The client checks core/version before acting. mountRCClient calls requireVersion (cmd/drive/rc.go:118, cmd/drive/rc.go:158) before pause/status use the client. ``` $ go test ./cmd/drive -count=1 -v -run 'TestMountRCClientReadsTheStoredAddress|TestMountRCClientRefusesAnEmptyVersion|TestMountRCClientRefusesAStranger' --- PASS: TestMountRCClientReadsTheStoredAddressAndChecksVersion (0.01s) --- PASS: TestMountRCClientRefusesAnEmptyVersion (0.01s) --- PASS: TestMountRCClientRefusesAStrangerOnThePort (0.01s) ``` 3. Two mounts on one machine do not collide. ``` $ go test ./cmd/drive -count=1 -v -run TestTwoPreparedMountsDoNotShareAnRCAddr --- PASS: TestTwoPreparedMountsDoNotShareAnRCAddr (0.00s) $ unshare -Urm go test ./cmd/drive -count=1 -timeout 3m -v -run 'TestTwoStandinMountsDoNotCollideOnRC|TestPrepareMountAuthWritesEnvAt0600' --- PASS: TestPrepareMountAuthWritesEnvAt0600AndOmitsTheSecretFromConf (0.00s) rc_auth_test.go:213: two mounts bound 127.0.0.1:38327 and 127.0.0.1:45071 --- PASS: TestTwoStandinMountsDoNotCollideOnRC (1.09s) PASS ok github.com/Nishfleet/drive/cmd/drive 1.112s ``` semgrep --config p/default --baseline-commit origin/main: no findings (exit 0) npm run check: typecheck passed; biome check exit 0 (pre-existing warnings in public/ and marketing/, none in this diff) in-run review: unavailable - empty output Closes #807 --- Need help on this PR? items.title: node:fs: stop cp from descending into a directory it is writing into
items.body:
### Problem
- `fs.cpSync`, `fs.cp` and `fs.promises.cp` can copy a directory into its own output. It happens when `dest` is a second name (symlink, bind mount) for a directory inside `src`. The copy nests until `ENAMETOOLONG` or `ENOSPC`.
- The guards in `src/js/internal/fs/cp-sync.ts` compare only path strings and the written ancestors of `dest`.

### Fix
- The JS walker keeps the `(dev, ino)` of each dest directory on its recursion path. It throws `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL` before it descends into one of them.
- If the parent of `dest` is `src` and there is no `filter`, the copy fails before any write. On macOS a realpath check guards the native copy.
- Verified: `test/js/node/fs/cp.test.ts` (33 new tests, 21 fail on main) and the 76 vendored `test-fs-cp-*` tests.
- Self-reviewed: 9 concerns raised, 7 addressed. Open: source symlink cycles under `dereference` (as in Node.js), a Windows run (CI).

### Background
- `checkPaths` already stats every source and existing dest entry with BigInt, so the comparison adds no syscall.
- The `stat` of a created root is read only when the walk reaches the directory that holds it.
- Considered a realpath comparison on every copy (the first form): it misses bind mounts and adds two `realpath` calls.

### Downsides
- A rejected copy leaves one level of partial output, as GNU `cp` does.
- With a `filter` the walk may enter its output once. If the filter lets it re-enter, the copy fails. Node.js goes on.
- Per recursive directory copy (release builds): syscalls stay at 43 (`strace -f`), +18 GC cells. Instructions not measured (no PMU, no valgrind).

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

#### What each layout does

`main` is a release build of main with its own walkers, `PR` the same tree with this change, Node.js is v26.3.0. Linux x64.

| Layout | main | PR | Node `cpSync` | Node `promises.cp` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dest` under a symlink to `src/sub` | nests, `ENAMETOOLONG` | `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL` | aborts (SIGABRT) | nests, `ENAMETOOLONG` |
| `dest` under a bind mount of `src/sub` | nests, `ENOSPC` (62 dirs on a 64-inode tmpfs) | `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL`, 3 nodes left | aborts | nests, `ENOSPC` |
| `dereference`, `dest/sub` is a symlink into `src/sub` | nests | `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL` | aborts | nests |
| `dereference`, `src/d/link` points at `dest/d` | nests | `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL` | ok | nests |
| `dereference`, `src` is a symlink to the directory that holds `dest` | nests, `ELOOP` | `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL`, nothing written | aborts | nests, `ELOOP` |
| `dest` spelled `link/../x`, kernel-resolved parent is `src` | `ENOENT`, stray directory in `src` | `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL`, nothing written | `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL` | `ENOENT`, stray directory |
| symlink layout, `filter` skips the output | ok | ok | ok | ok |
| symlink layout, `filter` prunes everything below the output | ok | ok | ok | ok |
| symlink layout, `filter: () => true` | nests | `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL`, two levels left | nests | nests |

GNU cp 9.7 on the bind mount layout: `cp: cannot copy a directory, 'a/sub', into itself, 'b/t'`, exit 1, 2 directories left.

Bind mount repro (root, or `unshare -Urm`):

```sh
W=/tmp/cp-w; rm -rf $W; mkdir -p $W/a $W/b
mount -t tmpfs -o nr_inodes=64,size=1m tmpfs $W/a
mkdir -p $W/a/sub/inner; echo hello > $W/a/sub/file
mount --bind $W/a/sub/inner $W/b
cd $W
bun -e 'try { require("fs").cpSync("a/sub", "b/t", { recursive: true }) } catch (e) { console.log(e.code) }'
find a -type d | wc -l
```

main prints `ENOSPC` and 62. The PR prints `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL` and 5. Node.js v26.3.0 aborts in `cpSync` (`terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::filesystem::__cxx11::filesystem_error'`) and runs to `ENOSPC` in `promises.cp`.

#### How the guard decides

- A frame is one dest directory on the current recursion path. An existing dest directory brings its `stat` from `checkPaths`. A directory the copy created gets a frame without a `stat`.
- Only the created root and, under `dereference`, every created directory get a frame. Without `dereference` the source walk cannot reach a created directory without passing the root first.
- The root's `stat` is read when the source walk reaches a directory with the identity of the root's parent. That identity comes from the one `stat` of `dirname(dest)` that replaces the `existsSync` probe.
- Under `dereference`, a followed symlink can land anywhere, so the unread frames on the path are read at that entry.
- The filter is asked first. A skipped entry is never compared.
- Without a filter the first match throws. With a filter the first match is let through, every directory created after it gets a frame with its `stat`, and the next match throws. This keeps the copies that Node.js completes because the filter prunes below the output.
- A directory the copy created and already left is ordinary input again (a symlink to an already copied sibling under `dereference`). A set of all created directories would reject that copy.
- `checkParentPaths` is back to main's form.

#### macOS

The default-option route hands a tree of regular files and directories to the native copy when `dest` does not exist. That code has no identity check, so `nativeDirCopyIsSafe[Sync]` compares realpaths first. It throws when `dest` resolves into `src`, and it sends the copy to the JS walker when it cannot tell: a realpath error, or a `..` segment in either path (bun's realpath collapses `..` as text, which is wrong after a symlink). The bundler drops this code from the Linux and Windows builds. I could not run it on macOS. I ran the function bodies on Linux against 17 path shapes.

#### Review findings

Addressed:
1. The macOS pre-flight did not see `..` after a symlink.
2. The "parent of dest is src" check ignored a filter that skips the output (three spellings that main and Node.js complete).
3. `link/../x` with an existing dest wrote into another directory before it failed.
4. Copies that Node.js completes because the filter prunes below the output were rejected.
5. A `catch` around the parent `stat` that could not fire.
6. Two inline copies of the error that the new helper builds.
7. Array methods in the pre-flight helper.

Not addressed:
8. A symlink cycle inside `src` under `dereference` still nests until `ELOOP` or `ENAMETOOLONG`. main and Node.js `promises.cp` do the same. It is not a copy into the output.
9. The Windows identity comparison depends on libuv's `dev` and `ino`. I could not run Windows here.

#### Evidence

- 283 cases by 3 entry points (849 runs) against the same debug binary with main's walkers: 798 identical. The other 51 are main nesting (or `ENOENT` with a stray directory for the `..` spelling) where the PR throws `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL`.
- Differential fuzz against bun 1.4.2, 3,900 seeds by 2 APIs, symlinks, bind mounts, filters, `dereference`: 0 copies rejected that 1.4.2 completes, 0 tree differences, 204 nesting copies per API now `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL`.
- 291 directed layouts, 26 of them with bind mounts.
- Suites on the debug build: `test/js/node/fs/cp.test.ts` (80 pass, 5 Windows-only skipped), `cp-symlink-target.test.ts`, the 76 vendored `test-fs-cp-*`, `tsc -p src/js/tsconfig.json`. In `fs.test.ts` only the `readdir ... x 100` stress tests time out here, with and without this change.

#### Measurements

Release builds of main 5f5799ed16 with main's walkers and with this change, Linux x64.

| | main | PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| syscalls, `cpSync`, new dest, parent exists | 43 | 43 (one `access` becomes one `statx`) |
| syscalls, `promises.cp`, same | 45 | 45 |
| syscalls, `cpSync` / `promises.cp`, two missing parents | 47 / 49 | 48 / 50 (+1 `statx`) |
| syscalls, `cpSync` / `promises.cp`, existing dest | 41 / 43 | 41 / 43 |
| syscalls, `cpSync` / `promises.cp`, 16 x 16 tree | 3226 / 3243 | 3226 / 3243 |
| syscalls, `dereference`, 16 x 16 tree | 3226 / 3243 | 3226 / 3243 |
| syscalls, `dereference`, 8 symlinked directories at depth 3 | 205 / 217 | 209 / 221 (+4 `lstat`) |
| GC cells per call, `cpSync`, one-file directory | 88 | 106 (+15 BigInt, +4 Object, -1 Arguments) |
| GC cells per call, `promises.cp`, 16 x 16 tree | 21035.5 | 21053.5 |
| GC cells per call, `cpSync`, 16 x 16 tree into an existing copy | 11859 | 11891.5 (+1 per existing dest directory) |
| GC cells per call, single file | 106 | 106 |
| embedded `cp-sync.js` / `cp.js`, bytes | 13,113 / 9,430 | 15,744 / 11,154 |
| release binary, bytes | 106,178,312 | 106,182,408 |

- Syscalls: `strace -f -y`, path syscalls between two marker `stat` calls. For `promises.cp` every one of them runs on a pool thread, so the thread-pool work is 45 to 45, and 49 to 50 with missing parents.
- GC cells: `heapStats().objectTypeCounts` around the calls, GC timer off, runs with a collection dropped.
- Wall-clock, interleaved A/B, 20 pairs on `/dev/shm`, medians, with the A/A difference beside each: `cpSync` one-file directory +0.80% (A/A -1.07%), `cpSync` into an existing copy +0.61% (+1.62%), `cpSync` 16 x 16 tree +0.61% (+1.74%), `promises.cp` one-file directory -1.90% (+2.17%), `promises.cp` 16 x 16 tree +0.48% (-0.20%). No delta is outside the noise.
- The replaced probe in a loop: `existsSync` 0.44 us, `statSync` with `bigint` 1.0 us.
- Instructions per call: not measured. `perf_event_open` returns `ENOENT` in the VM and valgrind cannot be installed there.
- macOS pre-flight: not measured. By reading it adds two `realpath` calls per native directory copy.

#### Not covered

- The native walkers (`cp_sync_inner`, `cp_async_directory` in `src/runtime/node/node_fs.rs`) have no identity check. `node:fs` reaches them for a directory only on macOS, behind the pre-flight. The shell `cp` builtin reaches them directly: #38653 adds path checks there.
- A filesystem that reports inode 0, or a second name with another `st_dev` (overlayfs), gets no protection, as with the existing identity checks.
- A dest with `..` after a symlink still has its children written to the textually normalized path (`copyDir` builds them with `path.join`). main and Node.js `promises.cp` do the same. That is a separate defect.
- `fs.realpathSync.native`, `fs.realpath.native` and `fs.promises.realpath` return the textual answer for `link/..` where Node.js returns the parent of the link target. Also separate.

</details>

<!-- robobun:evidence:begin -->

items.title: Native rootfs in userspace: enter with util-linux + chroot; drop the root chroot fallback
items.body:
Follow-up to #26 / #27, which did this for the `overlay` tier. The `rootfs` tier has not been split along the same native / third-party axis yet.

## Principle (from #27)

The goal is running software **in userspace**. Admin steps only **enable** userspace once (`admin/native/enable-userspace.sh`, `admin/third-party/install-tools.sh`). They never run the user's software as root. So this issue adds **no** root runner and **removes** the existing one.

## Terms

- A **rootfs** is a *thing*: a directory holding a complete OS (`/usr`, `/etc`, `/var`, …).
- **Creating** one is done by mmdebstrap or debootstrap.
- **Entering** one is done by a *runner*: `chroot`, `unshare` + `chroot`, `bwrap` or `proot`. These are all at the same level.
- The **tiers** go `direct` → `env` → `overlay` → `rootfs`. overlay stacks the prefix onto the host's `/usr`. rootfs replaces all of `/` (so dpkg runs postinst as namespace-root inside).

## Current state

| rootfs | userspace | root |
|---|---|---|
| **enter** | `bwrap` or `proot` only (third-party) | `chroot` fallback in `tools/prefix-run.sh` ⚠️ |
| **create** | `mmdebstrap --mode=unshare` (third-party) | — |

## Problems

1. **No native userspace way to enter a rootfs.** `unshare` + `mount` + `chroot` (util-linux + coreutils) works but is not implemented. `scripts/env/build-in-rootfs.sh` only mentions it in a comment. It is also the useful fallback when `kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=2` breaks proot.

   Verified on this machine (Debian forky/sid, kernel 7.1, `~/buildroot` from `make-buildroot.sh`):
   ```sh
   R=~/buildroot
   unshare -Urm --fork --pid sh -c "mount --rbind /dev $R/dev && mount -t proc proc $R/proc &&
     exec /usr/sbin/chroot $R /bin/sh -c '. /etc/os-release; echo \$PRETTY_NAME; id -u; dpkg -l | wc -l'"
   # -> Debian GNU/Linux forky/sid / 0 / 246
   ```

2. **The root `chroot` fallback is an escape hatch, and a privilege escalation.** When `prefix-run.sh` runs as root without bwrap or proot, it chroots into `$ROOTFS` and runs the command as real root. The rootfs is normally user-owned (`make-buildroot.sh` runs as the user), so root executes user-controlled binaries and libraries.

3. **Creating a rootfs has no native route, and shouldn't get one.** Bootstrapping Debian is not just unpacking `.deb`s. It needs:
   - resolving Essential/required packages,
   - `InRelease` → `gpgv` → SHA256 verification,
   - two-stage unpack/configure ordering (`base-passwd` first),
   - `policy-rc.d`,
   - merged-`/usr` transitions,
   - root-owned files and setuid bits without root.

   These change across releases. mmdebstrap is maintained in Debian and CI-tested across releases. A hand-rolled script would rot, and skipping signature checks would be a security hole.

## Proposed change

- **Add `tools/prefix-run.sh --mode rootfs-native`** (userspace): `unshare -Urm --fork --pid --kill-child` + bind `/dev`, `/proc`, `/tmp`, `$HOME` + `chroot`. auto order for rootfs: bwrap → rootfs-native → proot. It must handle what bwrap does for us:
  - **PID 1:** the command must not be PID 1 unless it reaps zombies and handles signals. Use a tiny shell reaper, or `--fork` with signal forwarding.
  - **die with parent:** `--kill-child`.
  - **new session:** `setsid`, which blocks TIOCSTI injection into the caller's terminal.
  - **`/sys`:** sysfs can't be mounted in a userns without a new netns. Bind the host's `/sys` read-only, or skip it.
  - **rootfs under `$HOME`:** binding `$HOME` into a rootfs that lives inside `$HOME` recurses. Bind non-recursively, or bind only what's needed.
- **Remove the root `chroot` fallback** from `prefix-run.sh`. As root, refuse: this is a userspace runner.
- **`scripts/env/build-in-rootfs.sh`:** fall back to the native entry when bwrap is missing.
- **Creating a rootfs stays third-party**, but installable without root: the repo's own userspace apt can install `mmdebstrap` into `~/.local`. Document that route next to `admin/third-party/install-tools.sh`.
- **Docs:**
  - `docs/paths.md`: separate the two axes, **tier** (overlay / rootfs) and **runner** (chroot / unshare / bwrap / proot), and add `rootfs-native` to the mode table.
  - `docs/standard.md`: update the `rootfs` row.

Stays **experimental** (`docs/standard.md`).

## Acceptance

- `prefix-run.sh --mode rootfs-native` runs a command in `~/buildroot` as namespace uid 0. `dpkg -l` works, `$HOME` is reachable, and the exit status is propagated.
- Ctrl-C / SIGTERM reach the command. Killing `prefix-run.sh` kills the whole tree. No zombies.
- auto picks `rootfs-native` when bwrap fails its probe.
- Running `prefix-run.sh --mode rootfs` as root refuses (no chroot fallback).
- Nothing is left mounted on the host after exit.
- `mmdebstrap` installed via userspace apt can build `~/buildroot` (or the doc says exactly why not).

## Related

#26, #27, `scripts/env/make-buildroot.sh`, `scripts/env/build-in-rootfs.sh`, `docs/paths.md`, `docs/standard.md`.

items.title: #12 命令の形 v1 と mount オプションを確定する
items.body:
## 概要

Issue #12（O-7・O-13・補足 S-5）。ホストと agent のあいだの命令の形を v1 に確定し、OverlayFS の mount オプションを固定する。#10 から移した「層の中身（whiteout・opaque）の確認」も入れた。

## 決めたこと

| 項目 | 決定 | 記録 |
|---|---|---|
| O-7 命令の形 | v1：層の名前はホストが決める文字列（MicroGit では Git のハッシュ）、commit は冪等、base64、`readMany`・`inspect`・`stats`、失敗に種類の記号 | [agent-protocol.md](../blob/issue/12-protocol-v1/docs/agent-protocol.md) |
| S-5 コミットの方式 | 保存ごとに層を 1 枚作る（まとめない・遅らせない）。層のコミットは 0.1〜7 ms で、保存の Git の手順（約 100 ms）より小さい | ADR-0004 |
| O-13 mount オプション | `userxattr,redirect_dir=nofollow,index=off,metacopy=off,xino=off`。最低の版は VM なし 5.11、tmpfs に層を置くなら 6.6、ゲストは 6.18.53 | ADR-0005 |

## 試して分かったこと

- `userxattr` と `redirect_dir=on`、`userxattr` と `metacopy=on` は、カーネルが同時に受け付けない（`conflicting options`）。非特権で使う以上、フォルダの名前変更は必ずコピーになる
- mount オプションを固定しても、ゴールデンテストのビューは 1 バイトも変わらなかった
- 層の中身：消したファイルは whiteout、消して作り直したディレクトリは opaque、フォルダの名前変更は「元の whiteout＋新しいコピー」で redirect は作られない
- **予想が外れた点**：ファイル `p` を消して同じ名前でディレクトリを作ると、カーネルはそのディレクトリを opaque にする（テストの期待値をカーネルに合わせた）

## テスト

| テスト | 環境 | 結果 |
|---|---|---|
| `guest/agent/agent_test.go`（8 件、新規） | WSL2（`unshare -Urm`） | PASS |
| `check-guest.mjs`（12 シナリオ＋層の中身 5 件） | WSL2 の VM なし | 一致 |
| `record-kernel.mjs`（固定オプション） | WSL2 | `*.golden` 変化なし |
| CI：agent-test（sudo）、guest（QEMU arm64 / x86_64）、golden-kernel（6.8 / 6.17） | GitHub Actions | 確認待ち |

## 文書

- `docs/agent-protocol.md`（新規、v1 の仕様）
- `docs/adr/0004-commit-per-save.md`、`docs/adr/0005-mount-options.md`（新規）
- `docs/learning/04-protocol-and-mount-options.md`（新規）
- 保存 1 回の旅（walkthrough）、guest-phase1 を v1 に合わせた

Closes #12

items.title: core: carry the sandbox's raw namespace calls in every core
items.body:
cosmic-lua/cosmic#2802 added `mount`, `umount2`, `unshare`, `setns` and `chroot` to the checked core's test instruments, so the two tests that use them ran only on the linux-x86_64-checked leg. This PR makes the five calls real in every core. Those tests, and a third converted here, now run on every Linux leg, Alpine and aarch64 included.

## Core
- **Where the calls live:** the five bindings move to a new `core/namespace_calls.c` and `core/namespace_calls.h`, in `build.zig`'s `core_sources`. Both `core/testing.c` and `core/testing_checked.c` add them to `cosmic.internal.testing` through `cosmic_add_namespace_calls`.
  - The contract is unchanged: each answers `true`, or `false, message, errno`, and `ENOSYS` off Linux.
  - The other cores' stand-in list loses the five names.
- **Docs:** `core/testing.h`, `core/testing.c`, `core/instrument_test.tl` and `cosmic/internal/testing.d.tl` now say these five are real in every core, and every other instrument stays checked-only.
- **The exception in `doc/design.md`:** it now names these five as the one exception to "a raw table reaches nothing its wrapper does not". They grant nothing a program could not already do by starting `mount` or `unshare`, since the kernel and any sandbox's filter are what refuse them.

## Tests
- **In-process test:** it moves from `core/syscalls_checked_test.tl` to `core/syscalls_namespace_test.tl`, which needs no `checked`, so every core enters the five functions. It also accepts `ENOSYS`, for macOS.
- **The two tests from #2802:**
  - `cosmic/child_policy_nest_checked_test.tl` is now `cosmic/child_policy_nest_calls_test.tl`, requiring `nest`.
  - `core/noexec_nested_checked_test.tl` is now `core/noexec_nested_test.tl`, requiring `userns`.
  - They stay separate modules because each needs grants the rest of its original module does not.
- **Database remount test:** `cosmic/child_policy_database_sandboxed_test.tl`'s remount test and its fixture no longer run the host's `unshare -Urm` and `mount` through `/bin/sh`. They make the same calls through `cosmic.internal.testing`, and the module drops the "system" profile.
  - The assertion is stricter than before: the namespace must be made and the ids mapped, and the remount must be refused with `EPERM`.
- **Hosts that refuse the nested namespace:** the remount test and the nested noexec test now call `Test.skip`, naming the refusal, where a host refuses the user namespace or the id-map write (AppArmor's restriction). Any other errno still fails them.

## Checks
- `bin/zig build boot`, `analyze` and `sanitized` pass.
- A reviewer compiled `core/namespace_calls.c` cleanly for aarch64-macos, aarch64-linux-musl and x86_64-linux-gnu.
- `o/bin/cosmic fix` on the changed paths and `fix --check .` pass.
- `o/bin/cosmic test` passes: 4269 ran, 0 failed, 450/450 C functions entered. The touched modules ran, none skipped.
- The touched modules pass on the checked core, sandboxed.
- With `COSMIC_TEST_PLATFORM=other` the nest and sandbox modules go n/a.
- A separate agent reviewed it adversarially. Its findings are addressed: the `doc/design.md` note, the stale headers, and the skips.
- Run as root with `COSMIC_TEST_SANDBOX=0`, three other cases in the database module fail. They fail the same way on the parent commit, so they are not from this change.

## TODOs
`o/bin/cosmic todos` on the changed paths lists none added by this branch.
